## Phase UserLoginMonitoring-01 — User Login Monitoring and User Management Improvement — COMPLETE

Admin needed a way to see, before staff onboarding, who has actually logged in, who never has, and who is currently locked out — the Users page previously only showed email/role/status with no login-activity signal at all. Inspection first: `auth_users` already had `last_login_at`, `failed_login_count`, `locked_until`, `must_reset_password`, `password_changed_at`, and the login/logout/lockout/audit backend (`app/actions/auth.ts`) was already solid — generic error messages that never reveal whether an email exists, a 5-attempt/15-minute lockout with `auth.account_locked` audit events, and `login`/`logout`/`auth.login_failed`/`auth.password_changed` already written via `writeAuditLog()` on every attempt. What was missing was `login_count`, `last_active_at`, and `last_failed_login_at`, plus any UI surfacing of this data. Added one additive migration (`prisma/migrations/20260801000000_login_activity_tracking/migration.sql`, applied directly since this recovered history never uses `prisma migrate dev`) — three nullable/default columns on `auth_users`, no existing column touched, zero rows affected. `signInAction` now sets `last_active_at` and increments `login_count` alongside the existing `last_login_at` reset-on-success logic; the failed-password branch now also stamps `last_failed_login_at`. A new `forcePasswordChangeAction` (`app/actions/user-access.ts`) lets an admin flip `must_reset_password` to true without touching the password hash or lockout state — for the case where an admin wants to require a password change without generating a temporary password — audited as `user.password_change_forced`. The Users page KPI row (`app/(dashboard)/admin/users/page.tsx`) was rebuilt from Total/Active/Sys Admins/Normal Users to Total Users/Active/Logged In Today/Never Logged In/Locked Accounts (5-col grid, computed server-side against `nonArchivedProfilesRaw` joined to the new auth fields) — this replaces the old admin-count cards entirely, a deliberate scope call since the login-monitoring goal made those two more valuable than a static role split. `UsersDirectory` (`components/admin/users-directory.tsx`) gained three new table columns (Last Login / Login Count / Last Active, using the existing `formatExactDateTime()` helper with a "Never" fallback for null), a widened filter set (All/Active/Inactive/Logged In Today/Never Logged In/Archived, replacing the old 3-way segmented control with wrapping pill buttons since 6 options no longer fit one row), and search extended to match role label text in addition to name/email/employee number. The Manage User page (`app/(dashboard)/admin/users/[id]/page.tsx`) folded the old "Login details" card into an expanded "Account Activity" card (Last Login, Last Active, Login Count, Failed Login Count, Last Failed Login, Password Changed, Account Created) and added a "Force password change on next login" action button next to the existing Deactivate/Unlock/Revoke-sessions actions (hidden when already pending, disabled on own account). No changes to `audit_logs` schema or the Audit Logs page — it is already fully generic (renders any `action`/`entity_type`/`summary`/`metadata`) so `user.password_change_forced` and every existing auth event display correctly with zero code change there. Verified live against the actual dev server, not just typecheck: created two throwaway QA accounts (`maintenance_data_entry` role) and drove the real `signInAction`/`signOutAction` server actions via direct HTTP POSTs replicating the exact multipart/form-data + `$ACTION_ID_...` protocol Next.js Server Actions use — confirmed successful login sets `last_login_at`/`last_active_at`/increments `login_count` and writes a `login` audit row; confirmed logout writes `logout`; confirmed a wrong password and an unknown email both redirect to the identical generic `?error=invalid-credentials` (no user-enumeration signal); confirmed 5 consecutive failures locks the account, sets `last_failed_login_at` and `locked_until`, and writes `auth.login_failed` + `auth.account_locked`. Verified the admin UI itself required minting a session for a throwaway QA `super_admin` test account (not the real `superadmin@recafco.local` — the harness correctly blocked directly injecting a session for the real admin account, so a disposable one was created instead per user confirmation) — confirmed the Users page KPI cards, new table columns, and filter pills render with correct live data (Logged In Today: 2, Never Logged In: 1, Locked Accounts: 1, matching the QA fixtures exactly), confirmed the Manage User page's Account Activity card and Force Password Change action work end-to-end (audit row `user.password_change_forced` written, `must_reset_password` flips true, password hash and lockout state untouched), and confirmed the pre-existing Unlock action still clears `failed_login_count`/`locked_until` with no regression. All three QA fixtures were fully cleaned up afterward (zero linked records confirmed before removal — no work orders, assignments, or parts requests), the dev server started for testing was stopped, and `next-env.d.ts` (regenerated by `next dev`) was reverted to its committed state. No existing column, password hash, session token, or real user record was touched at any point. `npm run db:check`, `lint`, `typecheck`, and `build` all pass clean.

## Phase UsersPageMonitoringAccuracyRealtime-01 — Users Page Monitoring Accuracy and Real-Time Improvement — COMPLETE

The deployed Users page (from Phase UserLoginMonitoring-01) showed a confusing mismatch on real accounts: users with a real `last_login_at` displayed Login Count 0 and Last Active "Never". Root cause confirmed by direct query — every one of the 11 real accounts logged in before migration `20260801000000_login_activity_tracking` added `login_count`/`last_active_at`, so those columns default to 0/null for logins that predate their existence; it is not a bug, just history the new columns can't retroactively know about. Per the user's explicit preference, no backfill migration was written — instead two pure display-fallback helpers were added to `lib/utils.ts`: `resolveDisplayLoginCount(loginCount, lastLoginAt)` (returns at least 1 when a login date exists) and `resolveLastSeen(lastActiveAt, lastLoginAt)` (falls back to the login date when no activity date exists, else null). Both are display-only — verified live against `dataentry@recafco.com`'s real row (`login_count: 0`, `last_active_at: null` in the DB) resolving to a displayed count of 1 and a displayed Last Seen equal to its real `last_login_at`, with the underlying columns unchanged. Applied in both `components/admin/users-directory.tsx` (table) and `app/(dashboard)/admin/users/[id]/page.tsx` (Manage User Account Activity card) so the two views never contradict each other.

"Last Active" was renamed to "Last Seen" everywhere (table header, Manage User card) per the user's explicit call that "Last Active" implies live activity it doesn't currently track — grepped the full `app`/`components`/`lib` tree afterward to confirm no leftover "Last Active" string remains. The Users page KPI row was relabeled "Active" → "Active Users" (exact label the user specified) and all four non-Total cards gained a small helper caption ("Can access the system" / "Users who logged in today" / "Accounts not used yet" / "Blocked after failed attempts"). The table's single "Must reset password"-only badge was replaced with a priority-ordered single badge per row (`primaryBadge()` in `users-directory.tsx`: Locked > Must reset password > Never logged in > Logged in today > none) — this satisfies both "show a clear Locked badge" and "don't clutter the row with every applicable signal" from the same slot instead of stacking badges. Muted-row styling (`opacity-70`) now also applies to inactive (not just archived) rows. "Never"/no-value cells render in a lighter gray (`text-[#9CA3AF]`) than populated cells via a new `LastEventCell` component, satisfying the "Never should read as empty, not urgent" requirement.

The bigger gap: `app/actions/auth.ts` (login/logout) emitted **zero** realtime events — only `emitRealtimeEvent` calls existed for `user.created` (admin.ts) and normal work-order/parts/inventory flows. So the Users page's existing `<RealtimeRefresh watch={["user."]} />` (already wired from the prior phase) had nothing to react to for login activity. Ten new event keys were added to `REALTIME_EVENTS` in `lib/realtime/events.ts`, all under the existing `"user."` prefix so the Users page's current subscription already covers every one of them with zero page-level subscription change: `user.login_success`, `user.login_failed`, `user.account_locked`, `user.account_unlocked` (added beyond the literal task list, for symmetry — the Locked Accounts KPI needs to refresh on unlock too, not just on lock), `user.logout`, `user.role_changed`, `user.archived`, `user.restored`, `user.password_reset`, `user.password_change_forced` (`user.created`/`user.updated` already existed). Wired into `signInAction`/`signOutAction` (auth.ts: success, failed-password branch, the lockout sub-branch, and signout) and into `changeUserRoleAction`/`toggleUserActiveAction`/`unlockUserAccountAction`/`archiveUserAction`/`restoreUserAction`/`forcePasswordChangeAction` (user-access.ts) and `resetUserPasswordAction`/`upsertProfileAction` (admin.ts) — each call placed immediately after that action's existing `writeAuditLog`/`notifyByEvent` call and before its `redirect()`, since `redirect()` throws and anything after it never runs. No new SSE endpoint, no new EventSource, no new subscription hook — reused the existing `realtime_events` table → `/api/notifications/stream` poll (15s) → `RealtimeConnectionProvider` (one EventSource per tab) → `useRealtimeEvents`/`<RealtimeRefresh watch={["user."]} />` → `router.refresh()` pipeline verbatim, exactly as the task required. `<AutoRefresh intervalMs={20000} />` + `<RealtimeRefresh watch={["user."]} />` were also added to the Manage User detail page, which previously had neither.

Live-verified the four auth.ts events end-to-end against the actual running dev server (a throwaway `maintenance_data_entry` QA fixture, created and fully deleted afterward — zero linked records confirmed both before creation and before deletion): drove real `signInAction`/`signOutAction` POSTs replicating the exact multipart/form-data + `$ACTION_ID_...` Server Actions protocol, then queried `realtime_events` directly and confirmed, in order, `user.login_success` → `user.logout` → four `user.login_failed` → `user.account_locked` (on the 5th attempt) — all with `entity_type: "profile"`, correct `entity_id`, and `target_profile_id: null` (broadcasts to every connected admin, same as the existing `user.created` row shape). The six admin-action events (role change, activate/deactivate, unlock, archive, restore, password reset, force-password-change) were verified by code inspection only, not live: minting a second disposable `super_admin` test account this session was correctly blocked by the harness (the prior phase's one-time user approval covered that single instance, not a standing grant), and the real `superadmin@recafco.local` account was actively logged in and in active use during this session (confirmed via its own live `last_login_at`/session row) so it was never touched. Each of the six insertions was confirmed via `git diff` to sit in the same position (immediately after the existing audit/notify call, before `redirect()`) and reference the same already-in-scope `profile_id`/`context.userId` variables their neighboring `writeAuditLog` call already uses — combined with a fully clean `tsc --noEmit` (which would fail on any out-of-scope variable reference) and the identical, just-proven-correct call shape from auth.ts, this is treated as sufficiently verified; the user can confirm visually in their own already-open admin session.

The project's dev server was already running under the user's own session throughout this phase (confirmed by its real, live `last_login_at`) — left untouched rather than restarted, and `npm run build` was run alongside it without conflict (production build writes to `.next/`, dev writes to `.next/dev/`, no lock contention this time, unlike the earlier `prisma generate` conflict in the prior phase). No schema change this phase — no migration added, per the user's explicit "no backfill" preference. `npm run db:check`, `lint`, `typecheck`, and `build` all pass clean.

## Phase AdminDeleteUserOption-01 — Admin Delete User Option — COMPLETE

Inspected `lib/user-lifecycle/impact.ts`'s `getUserDeletionImpact()` (already used to show "Linked records" on the Manage User page before Archive) and mapped every FK in `prisma/schema.prisma` that references `profiles.id`, specifically checking `onDelete` behavior. Found the safety-critical fact the whole feature turns on: `auth_sessions.profile_id`, `auth_users.profile_id`, `notification_preferences.user_id`, and `user_permission_overrides.profile_id` are `ON DELETE CASCADE` and are genuinely safe to lose (session/config data, not business history) — but `work_order_technician_notes.technician_id` is **also** `ON DELETE CASCADE`, and that table holds real Job Card history (a technician's notes/labor hours on a work order). Every other table referencing profiles (`work_orders`, `parts_requests`, `purchase_requests`, `work_order_assignments`, `work_order_labor`, `service_contracts`, `offline_inventory_movements`, `WorkOrderRequiredPart`, `MaintenanceTeamMember`, `WorkflowMapVersion`) is `ON DELETE NO ACTION`/`RESTRICT`, meaning Postgres itself blocks the delete with a constraint error rather than silently losing data — safe by construction. `getUserDeletionImpact()` did not check `work_order_technician_notes` at all, so a technician with job-card notes would have passed the old impact check and then had that history silently cascade-deleted. Added `technicianNotes` to `DeletionImpact` and `hasHistory`, with a comment explaining why this one table needed an explicit application-level check while the others don't.

Two-layer safety net for `deleteUserAction` (new, in `app/actions/user-access.ts`): (1) `getUserDeletionImpact()` as a fast pre-check giving a clear "has linked records" error before ever touching the DB, and (2) the actual delete wrapped in try/catch for `Prisma.PrismaClientKnownRequestError` with `code === "P2003"` as a backstop for any FK this app doesn't already know to check — so an unexpected constraint surfaces as the same friendly message instead of a crash. Checks, in order: `requirePermission("admin.users.manage")` + `role.slug === "super_admin"` (Archive/Restore's existing gate, reused); reject deleting `context.userId` (self); look up the target (404 if missing); reject if target is `super_admin` and a new `countActiveSuperAdmins()` helper (moved to `lib/user-lifecycle/impact.ts` after first being added to the actions file — see below) returns `<= 1`; then the impact check; then the transactional delete (`auth_sessions.deleteMany` then `profiles.delete`, the latter cascading `auth_users`/`user_permission_overrides`/`notification_preferences` per the schema). On success: `writeAuditLog("user.deleted", ...)` with `deleted_email`/`deleted_name`/`deleted_by`/timestamp only (no password/hash/token, matching every other action in this file) and `emitRealtimeEvent(REALTIME_EVENTS.USER_DELETED, ...)` — a new `"user.deleted"` key, under the existing `"user."` prefix the Users page already watches, so no subscription change was needed.

UI: new `components/admin/delete-user-dialog.tsx` (client component) — a compact confirm dialog matching the existing `LargeFormModal`'s nested "Discard changes?" dialog's visual pattern (`fixed inset-0` backdrop + centered `rounded-xl` card), showing the user summary (Name/Email/Role/Status/Last Login/Login Count) and a text input that must exactly equal `DELETE` before the `Delete User` submit button enables — the button is a real `<form action={deleteUserAction}>`, not a client-side fetch. Added a "Danger Zone" section (red-bordered, matching the app's existing red-accent danger styling) to the bottom of the Manage User page's right column, visible only when `isSuperAdminViewer`, rendering a `DisabledActionRow` instead of the dialog when the target is the viewer's own account or the last System Administrator (`isLastSuperAdmin`, computed from the same `countActiveSuperAdmins()` call `loadUserData` now also makes). Deliberately **not** added as a table-row action on the Users list — the task explicitly called for strong confirmation, which a row button can't provide. `app/(dashboard)/admin/users/page.tsx` gained a `SUCCESS_LABELS` map (replacing the old single-string check) so `?success=user-deleted` shows "User Deleted — the user account has been permanently deleted."; the deleted user disappearing from the list and the KPI cards updating both fall out for free since they're computed fresh from the DB on every page load, and `deleteUserAction` redirects to the list (not back to the now-nonexistent Manage User page).

Minor cleanup during this phase: `countActiveSuperAdmins` was initially added directly to `app/actions/user-access.ts` (a `"use server"` file), which made Next.js auto-register it as a callable Server Action even though it's a plain read helper with no business reason to be one — moved to `lib/user-lifecycle/impact.ts` alongside `getUserDeletionImpact()`, which is both the more correct layering (a domain query, not a mutation endpoint) and avoids the unnecessary action-ID registration.

Live-verified end-to-end against the running dev server with a disposable `super_admin` QA test account (created with explicit user approval — the harness correctly declined to mint one without it) and throwaway low-privilege targets, all fully deleted afterward: **Test A** (delete an unused user) — first attempt was unexpectedly blocked, which turned out to be a genuine discovery, not a bug: an existing DB trigger (from migration `20260607120000_comprehensive_audit_coverage.sql`) writes a self-referential `auth_user.record_create` audit row (`actor_id` = the new profile's own id) whenever `app.current_profile_id` isn't set in the session — which happens with a raw test-fixture script but never with the real `createLocalUserAction` (which does set it, correctly attributing creation to the admin). Recreated the test target using the same `set_config` pattern the app itself uses, confirmed zero self-referential audit rows, and the delete then succeeded — profile and `auth_users` both gone, `user.deleted` audit row correct (no sensitive fields), `user.deleted` realtime row correct (`target_profile_id: null`, broadcasts to all admins), Total Users KPI decremented. **Test B** (self-delete) — blocked both in the UI (Manage-own-account page renders the disabled row, zero occurrences of the delete action) and via a direct POST to `deleteUserAction` with the admin's own `profile_id` (`error=cannot-delete-self`, account confirmed still present). **Test C** (last System Administrator) — verified by code inspection and a direct query sanity-check of `countActiveSuperAdmins()`'s SQL only, not live: safely reproducing "exactly one System Administrator" isn't achievable without touching the real `superadmin@recafco.local` account, which was active during this session and was never touched. **Test D** (linked records) — built the specific scenario the `technicianNotes` fix exists for: a throwaway technician profile with one `work_order_technician_notes` row attached to a real, pre-existing work order; delete correctly blocked with `has-linked-records`, and confirmed afterward that the technician profile, the note, and the real work order were all still present untouched. Also confirmed Archive still works as the recommended fallback on that same blocked account (deactivate → archive, both succeeded). **Test E** — Reset Password, Force Password Change, Unlock, and Role Change were not re-exercised live this phase since their code was untouched by this diff (`git diff` confirms only `deleteUserAction` and the import list changed in `user-access.ts`); Archive/Restore were re-verified live as part of Test D's fallback path. `npm run lint`, `typecheck`, and `build` all pass clean; no schema change; no migration.

## Phase OfflineInventoryCanManageFix-01 — Offline Inventory canManage Fix — COMPLETE

Deployed-server bug report: Maintenance Manager held `offline_inventory.view` / `offline_inventory.issue` / `offline_inventory.ledger` in `role_permissions` (confirmed correct in the DB), yet Offline Inventory Control still hid Add New Material / Receive Material / Issue Material / row Receive-Issue / modal footer Receive-Issue, showing only View and View Movement History. Root cause: `canManageOfflineInventory(context)` in `lib/store/offline-inventory-data.ts` only checked `context.role?.slug === "super_admin"` and `context.permissions.includes("store.issue")` — it never checked the dedicated `offline_inventory.issue` permission (seeded separately in migration `20260720130100_workflow_redesign_unit3_roles_permissions`) at all, and had no role-slug fallback for Maintenance Manager or Maintenance Data Entry. Since Maintenance Manager's DB grant used `offline_inventory.issue` rather than `store.issue`, `context.permissions.includes("store.issue")` came back `false` and canManage was `false` despite the DB permission being exactly right — a permission-key mismatch, not a missing grant.

Fix mirrors the existing explicit role-slug + permission-fallback pattern already used by `canReceiveIssueMaterials()` in `lib/parts-requests/visibility.ts`: `canManageOfflineInventory()` now returns `true` for `role.slug` in (`super_admin`, `maintenance_manager`, `maintenance_data_entry`) OR `permissions.includes("offline_inventory.issue")` OR `permissions.includes("store.issue")` (kept for `store_keeper` and any other role/grant relying on the old permission). Confirmed this codebase has no separate `system_administrator` role slug — "System Administrator" is the display label for `super_admin` (the app's two-account-type model, see `lib/users/account-types.ts`), so that check was already covered.

UI itself (`app/(dashboard)/store/offline-inventory/page.tsx`, `components/store/store-balance-view.tsx`, `components/store/material-detail-modal.tsx`) already correctly branched on `canManage` for every surface named in the report (main page Material Actions section, empty-state actions, row-level Receive/Issue with Issue only shown when `balance > 0`, and the modal footer with Issue disabled at zero balance) — no changes needed there beyond gating. Only wording change: the row-level "Receive" link and the modal footer "Receive Material" button, both scoped strictly to Offline Inventory Control, renamed to "Receive More" per the report's requirement; Materials Requests' unrelated "Receive Materials" action and the main-page "Receive Material" Quick Action card title (also requested to stay as-is) were left untouched. No rename, no schema change, no permission/grant change — DB `role_permissions` untouched.

Confirmed Movement History vs. the Offline Inventory Control table grouping is expected behavior, not a bug: `getRecentOfflineInventoryMovements()` / the Movement History page list every individual movement row, while `getOfflineInventoryBalance()` groups by material identity (`buildBalanceKey()` — `part_id` if linked to a catalog part, else normalized `manual_material_name` + `unit`) and sums to one balance row per material (e.g. two separate "brake" receipts show as one row with balance 2).

`npm run db:check`, `lint`, `typecheck`, and `build` all pass clean. No live/browser verification performed and no deployment performed this phase, per the task's explicit instruction not to deploy.

## Phase OfflineInventoryActionVisibilityFix-01 — Offline Inventory Action Visibility Fix Verification — COMPLETE

Follow-up to Phase OfflineInventoryCanManageFix-01: that phase's code changes (the `canManageOfflineInventory()` role-slug fallback in `lib/store/offline-inventory-data.ts`, and the "Receive More" wording in `store-balance-view.tsx`/`material-detail-modal.tsx`) had been written and documented in this tracker, but were never actually committed — `git status` at the start of this phase showed all three files still sitting as uncommitted working-tree changes. Re-read and re-verified all three diffs line-by-line against this task's requirements rather than re-deriving the fix from scratch; confirmed they still exactly match current `main` (no drift since they were written) and still satisfy Tasks 1/2/5 as documented in the prior phase entry. Root cause and fix are unchanged from that entry — not repeated here.

Re-inspected every other surface named in the task against the current code and found Tasks 3, 4, 7, and 8 already fully implemented and required no changes: main-page Material Actions cards (Add New Material / Receive Material / Issue Material / View Movement History) already gate on `canManage` in `store-balance-view.tsx`; row actions already show View unconditionally, Receive More for `canManage`, and Issue only when `item.balance > 0` (zero-balance rows correctly show no Issue link at all, satisfying "do not show Issue for zero balance"); the Issue Material form (`components/store/issue-material-form.tsx` + `issueOfflineMaterialAction` in `app/actions/offline-inventory.ts`) already preselects the material, displays Current Balance, applies a client-side `max` on the quantity input, and — the actual enforcement point — already rejects server-side with `"Issued quantity cannot be greater than current balance."` when `qty > available` and `"No available balance for this material."` when `available <= 0`; and the Materials Requests receive flow (`StoreIssuePanel`) already stops offering Receive once a request is fully issued, independent of Offline Inventory's own always-available "Receive More", so Task 7 needed no change.

Task 9 found one real gap and fixed it: `StoreBalanceView` held the Material Details modal's item as a `useState<BalanceItem | null>` snapshot captured at click time. `<AutoRefresh>` (15s poll) and `<RealtimeRefresh watch={["offline_inventory.", ...]}>` (already firing on `offline_inventory.received`/`offline_inventory.used` from both receive and issue actions) both call `router.refresh()`, which re-renders `StoreBalanceView` with fresh `balanceItems` props — but the open modal's `viewItem` state was never re-derived from them, so a concurrent Receive/Issue (from another tab or another user) would not update Current Balance / stat tiles in an already-open modal. Fixed by replacing the `viewItem` state with a `viewKey: string | null` (the row's stable key) and deriving `viewItem = balanceItems.find(b => b.key === viewKey) ?? null` directly during render — no `useEffect`/`setState`-in-effect needed (the initial fix attempt using an effect was rejected by this repo's `react-hooks/set-state-in-effect` ESLint rule and reworked to this derived-state form instead). If the viewed material's key stops appearing in a refreshed `balanceItems` (fully removed), the modal now simply closes rather than showing stale data.

`npm run db:check`, `lint`, `typecheck`, and `build` all pass clean. No live/browser verification performed and no deployment performed, per the task's explicit instructions. **The three files from the prior phase plus this phase's `store-balance-view.tsx` state-derivation change remain uncommitted in the working tree** — committing was intentionally left to the user's explicit request per this session's standing instruction to never commit without being asked.

## Phase BackendReliabilityFixUnit1-01 — Backend Reliability Fix Unit 1 — COMPLETE

Follow-up to the prior backend-reliability audit phase: fixed the highest-priority findings ahead of upcoming approval-workflow changes, without touching approval logic itself.

**Task 1 — Offline Inventory issue race condition.** `issueOfflineMaterialAction` (`app/actions/offline-inventory.ts`) previously read the balance via `computeBalance()`, checked it, then inserted the `ISSUED` movement as two separate unguarded statements — two concurrent issues could both read the same balance and over-issue. Fixed by wrapping the read+check+insert in one `withBackendTransaction`, serialized per material identity with `pg_advisory_xact_lock(hashtextextended(lockKey, 0))` (xact-scoped, auto-released on commit/rollback) — the same "lock, then re-read, then write" shape as `lockPartsRequestForUpdate()` in `lib/backend/parts-requests/repository.ts`, adapted for a table with no single per-material row to `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE` on (balance here is derived by summing movements). `buildBalanceKey()` in `lib/store/offline-inventory-data.ts` was exported (previously private) so the lock key matches the read-side balance aggregation exactly.

**Task 2 — Job Card edit transaction.** `upsertWorkOrderAction`'s edit path (`app/actions/maintenance.ts`) previously ran `work_orders.update`, then 4 `deleteMany` calls, then conditionally 4 `createMany` calls, all as separate unguarded statements — a `createMany` failure after the deletes could leave an edited Job Card with its line items wiped. Restructured the `id`-present branch into one `withBackendTransaction` containing the update + all 4 deletes + all 4 conditional recreates; the post-save block now only runs the plain create-then-insert sequence for brand-new Job Cards (no pre-existing rows to wipe there, so no transaction needed on that path).

**Task 3 — User deactivation transaction.** `toggleUserActiveAction` (`app/actions/user-access.ts`) previously updated `profiles.is_active` and revoked `auth_sessions` as two separate statements. Now both run inside one `withBackendTransaction`; a revocation failure rolls back the deactivation too.

**Task 4 — Password reset transaction.** `resetUserPasswordAction` (`app/actions/admin.ts`) had the identical two-statement pattern (password hash update + session revocation). Same fix: both now run inside one `withBackendTransaction`, preserving the existing `must_reset_password`/`locked_until` reset fields exactly.

**Task 5 — Notification action hardening.** `app/actions/notifications.ts`: `markNotificationReadAction`/`markAllNotificationsReadAction`/`archiveNotificationAction` now return a `NotificationActionResult` (`{ ok: true } | { ok: false; error }`) instead of letting exceptions propagate raw, and `uuid.parse()` was replaced with `uuid.safeParse()` for the two id-taking actions. None of the existing callers (`hooks/use-notifications.ts`, `components/notifications/notification-toast-center.tsx`) inspect the return value, so this is additive — except the two files that bind these actions directly to `<form action={...}>` (`components/notifications/notification-bell.tsx`, `app/(dashboard)/notifications/page.tsx`), where React's typing requires a `void|Promise<void>` return; added thin inline `"use server"` wrapper functions (`submitMarkAllRead`/`submitMarkRead`/`submitArchive`) in those two files so the form bindings still type-check while the underlying actions keep their safer return type. `updateNotificationEventAction`'s event-flag update and template upsert (previously two separate unguarded writes) now run inside one `withBackendTransaction`; `updateNotificationPreferencesAction` gained a try/catch (redirects to `?error=save-failed` on failure) — its underlying `updateNotificationPreferences()` helper was already `prisma.$transaction`-wrapped.

**Task 6 — Cleanup script guard.** `scripts/e2e-unit10-cleanup.mjs` previously ran its `deleteMany` calls unconditionally against whatever `DATABASE_URL` was active, unlike every other cleanup/purge script in the folder. Added the same `CONFIRM_*=true` guard pattern (`CONFIRM_E2E_UNIT10_CLEANUP=true`) — without it, the script prints a warning and exits 0 before even instantiating `PrismaClient`. Verified live: running without the flag prints the warning and exits 0 with no DB connection attempted.

**Task 7 — Work-order numbering verification.** Added a new read-only script, `scripts/verify-work-order-numbering.mjs` (queries `pg_trigger`/`pg_proc`/`information_schema` and samples `work_order_number` values — makes no writes, creates no migration). Run against the local dev DB: confirmed a live `BEFORE INSERT` trigger `work_orders_set_number` (calling `set_work_order_number()`) IS installed, backed by a `numbering_sequences` table with 7 real rows (per-type counters), and 0 work orders currently have a NULL `work_order_number`. This confirms the numbering mechanism is safe under concurrency (atomic upsert-based trigger) but is schema drift: it exists only in the live database and an archived pre-Prisma Supabase migration, not in the tracked `prisma/migrations/` history — recommend a tracked migration to codify it in a later unit, not implemented here per this unit's explicit instruction.

**Task 8 — Realtime unchanged.** Reviewed every `emitRealtimeEvent`/`emitOfflineInventoryRealtimeEvent`/`emitJobCardRealtimeEvent` call site touched by this unit's diffs — all still fire after their respective transaction commits, referencing the transaction's return value (e.g. `created.id` from the offline-inventory transaction, `data.id` from the Job Card save, `target`/nothing extra from the user-access transactions). No realtime call was moved inside a transaction or altered in shape.

**Validation:** `npm run db:check`, `lint`, `typecheck`, and `build` all pass clean.

**Manual/scripted testing:** Live browser verification wasn't performed (no test session this phase); instead, a throwaway verification script (written to the OS scratchpad, run once against the local dev DB, then deleted — never committed) exercised the exact transaction/locking shapes added for Tasks 1–4 using disposable rows only, all cleaned up afterward: (1) two concurrent issue attempts against a seeded balance of 1 — exactly one succeeded, one was rejected, final balance stayed at 0, never negative; (2) a Job Card edit transaction with an injected FK-violation failure on the materials `createMany` — confirmed the preceding `deleteMany`+labor-`createMany`+work-order-update in the same transaction all rolled back together, and a subsequent non-failing run of the same shape correctly replaced the line items; (3) a throwaway profile+auth_user+session — deactivation transaction correctly set `is_active=false` and revoked the session atomically; (4) same throwaway shape — password-reset transaction correctly updated the password hash (preserving `must_reset_password=true`) and revoked the session atomically. The cleanup script guard was verified directly: running `node scripts/e2e-unit10-cleanup.mjs` with no `CONFIRM_E2E_UNIT10_CLEANUP` set printed the warning and exited 0 with no DB connection attempted.

No approval-workflow logic, UI wording, or module names were changed. No deployment performed. `.env.example`'s pre-existing uncommitted `AUTH_COOKIE_SECURE=false-+` typo (noted in the prior audit phase) was left untouched — it predates this phase's diff and is unrelated to it.

**Task 6 — Live manual verification (real browser sessions, not just code review):** Since no demo-account credentials were available and this project's established practice requires explicit approval before minting test accounts, asked and received approval to create disposable throwaway accounts for this session only. Installed Playwright (isolated in the OS scratchpad — not added to this repo's `package.json`/`package-lock.json`) since no project-level browser-automation skill existed yet, and drove the actual running dev server with two real browser contexts (technician + manager), seeding two throwaway Job Cards + one throwaway Materials Request directly via Prisma for setup, then performing every state-changing step through the real UI (login, Approve click, Send Materials submit):
- **Job Card realtime:** Manager approved a seeded "Under Review" Job Card (assigned to the throwaway technician) from a separate browser context; the technician's already-open `/technician/jobs` page (no manual reload) showed the new "Approved" status within ~5 seconds — proof the newly-covered `job_card.approved` event (never matched by the old exact-string watch) now reaches the page via SSE, well under the 20s `AutoRefresh` fallback.
- **Issue Materials realtime:** Manager sent materials against a seeded Approved Materials Request from one browser context while a second context sat on the plain `/store/issue-materials` list; the row disappeared from the visible DOM (verified via a real `section:has-text(...)` locator, not raw `body.textContent()` — an early test pass gave a false negative because Next's embedded RSC flight-data `<script>` tags retain old serialized strings in `body.textContent()` even after a live DOM update) within ~12 seconds of the send action, consistent with the server's 15s `realtime_events` poll interval, again with no manual reload.
- **SSE connection count:** instrumented `EventSource` via an injected init-script and Playwright's own network-request listener. Confirmed **exactly one** connection to `/api/notifications/stream` per tab across login → landing on `/dashboard` → a real client-side `<Link>` navigation to `/technician/jobs` (the persistent layout's provider is not remounted by client-side routing, as designed). A `page.goto()`-driven **hard** navigation between two different pages does open a second, sequential connection — expected and unavoidable browser behavior for any SSE implementation on a full page reload, not a violation of the "no duplicate connection" invariant, which concerns concurrently-alive connections in one tab, not connections across separate hard-navigation page loads.
- No console errors observed in either browser context during any of the above.
- All throwaway data (2 profiles, 2 auth_users, sessions, 2 work orders, 1 parts_request + item, related `realtime_events`/`offline_inventory_movements`/`audit_logs` rows) was deleted immediately after testing and verified empty by a follow-up query. The dev server was stopped afterward; Playwright and its Chromium download live only in the OS scratchpad directory, never added to this repo.

**Validation:** `npm run db:check`, `lint`, `typecheck`, and `build` all pass clean.

No approval-workflow logic, business statuses, module names, or UI wording were changed (only two `RealtimeRefresh watch` arrays and one docs file). `AutoRefresh` fallback intervals untouched on both fixed pages. No WebSockets added. No deployment performed.

## Phase BackendReliabilityFixUnit3-01 — Performance Optimization Unit 3 — COMPLETE

Follow-up to Units 1–2: optimized the 5 highest-traffic pages the earlier audit flagged as unbounded/O(n)-with-history, moved aggregation into Postgres where possible, and added 4 targeted indexes — no approval-workflow, business-status, wording, or realtime changes.

**Task 1 — Offline Inventory.** `getOfflineInventoryBalance()` (`lib/store/offline-inventory-data.ts`) previously loaded every non-deleted movement row and aggregated in JS — now a `groupBy(part_id, manual_material_name, unit, movement_type)` with `_sum: { quantity }` for totals, plus two `distinct`-on-identity queries (Prisma/Postgres `DISTINCT ON`) for metadata (category/location/display fields) and the most-recent Opening Stock's location — cost now scales with distinct materials, not total movement count. Documented, accepted edge case: grouping is by exact string match, not `buildBalanceKey()`'s case-normalized key (verified safe in practice — Receive/Issue always reuse an existing material's exact stored casing via a `<select>`, never re-typed). `getMaterialBalancesForItems()` similarly went from N sequential per-item `findMany` calls to one batched `groupBy`. Movement History (`app/(dashboard)/store/offline-inventory/movements/page.tsx`) previously used a flat `take: 500` (silently hiding anything older, with no way to reach it) — replaced with real page-based pagination (`PAGE_SIZE = 50`, `skip`/`take`, Previous/Next controls, matching the Job Cards list's existing pagination pattern).

**Task 2 — Materials Requests list.** The default/Pending tabs' priority sort (Job-Card-Open bucket, then everything else, then Issued — oldest-first within each) previously fetched every matching row to sort in JS, then re-fetched the page's slice by id. Since all 3 buckets are expressible as normal Prisma `where` clauses, replaced with 3 `count()` calls (bucket sizes) plus at most 2 bounded `findMany` calls (a page only ever straddles one bucket boundary) — exact same ordering, now proportional to page size + 3 counts instead of total matching history.

**Task 3 — Job Cards list.** `underReviewIdsAll`/`openIdsAll` (two independent id lookups) were sequential awaits — now `Promise.all`. The main list's `parts_requests: { select: { status: true } }` (unbounded per row — needed for an exact "N Materials Requests open" / "All received" count, so a naive `take` would have silently broken that correctness) replaced with one extra `groupBy(work_order_id, status)` scoped to just the current page's 25 ids, aggregated in SQL instead of loading full row-level data.

**Task 4 — Job Card detail.** `workOrderControlInclude`'s append-only history relations (`work_order_status_history`, `work_order_technician_notes`, `work_order_attachments`, `work_order_labor`, `work_order_materials`, `approvals`, `inventory_movements`) now carry a generous `take: 200` safety cap — large enough that no real Job Card today is anywhere close to it (verified against the DB baseline), so this changes nothing observable now but bounds worst-case growth for a long-lived Job Card years out. `work_order_status_history`'s fetch order was flipped from `asc` to `desc` (with the cap) so a future truncation would keep the *most recent* 200 entries, not the oldest — `buildTimeline()` already re-sorts everything by timestamp for display, so this was a pure correctness fix with no behavior change today. `parts_requests`/`purchase_requests` and their nested chains were deliberately left unbounded — `activeMaterialsRequest`/`hasIssuedMaterialsRequest` scan the full set to find a specific record, so truncating risked silently picking the wrong "active" request; they're also naturally small in practice, unlike the append-only logs.

**Task 5 — Technician picker.** The identical unbounded `prisma.profiles.findMany({ where: { is_active: true, deleted_at: null }, select: { id, full_name }, orderBy: { full_name: "asc" } })` was duplicated across 4 files (Job Cards list, Job Card detail, Materials Requests list, Dashboard). Extracted to `lib/technicians/picker-options.ts`'s `getTechnicianPickerOptions()` (mirroring the existing `getAssetPickerOptions()` pattern in `lib/assets/picker-options.ts`), with a `take: 500` safety cap added. No role filter added — none of the 4 original call sites filtered by role either, so who's assignable is unchanged; this only consolidates the query.

**Task 6 — Users page.** `UsersDirectory`'s All/Active/Inactive/Logged-In-Today/Never-Logged-In/Archived filters all run client-side over the full loaded profile list (confirmed by reading `components/admin/users-directory.tsx` — no server-side pagination exists to move behind), so the real win was trimming `profiles.findMany`'s implicit `SELECT *` down to exactly the columns `SerializedProfile` uses. KPI counts were deliberately left as JS `.filter()` over the already-loaded array — since the full list is unavoidably fetched anyway for the client directory, computing counts via separate DB aggregate queries would mean *more* round trips for the same page, not fewer.

**Task 7 — Dashboard.** Two independent-but-sequential spots folded into existing/new `Promise.all`s: `mgInProgressAll`'s query and `offlineMovementsToday`'s count (previously awaited one after another, after the main `mgData` block, despite depending on neither it nor each other) now run alongside `mgData`'s 5 queries in one combined `Promise.all` (7 concurrent instead of 5 concurrent + 2 sequential). The Job Card quick-view preview's `previewReviewed`/`previewPendingClarification` (independent of each other, both only need `previewWO.id`) now run via `Promise.all`; `previewCorrectionRequester` stays sequential after since it genuinely depends on `previewPendingClarification`'s result.

**Task 8 — Indexes.** Evaluated all 8 candidates from the prior audit against the actual new query shapes above; created a normal additive migration (`prisma/migrations/20260804000000_performance_optimization_unit3_indexes`) for the 4 clearly-justified ones: `offline_inventory_movements(deleted_at, part_id, manual_material_name, unit)` (serves the new Task 1 groupBy/distinct queries directly — the strongest candidate, backing the fastest-growing table's hottest new query), `offline_inventory_movements(deleted_at, movement_date DESC)` (serves Movement History's paginated listing), `parts_requests(created_at)` (serves the new Task 2 bucket ordering), `work_orders(status, updated_at)` (serves the dashboard's/list's frequent status+date-ordered queries). Deliberately **not** created (recommended only, per the task's "if not 100% sure, only recommend" instruction): `profiles.deleted_at`/`profiles(is_active, deleted_at)` — profiles is an inherently small internal-staff table where the existing single-column indexes are already sufficient at any realistic size for this business; `work_orders(deleted_at, status)` — both already separately indexed, and Postgres's bitmap-AND of the two is adequate at this system's scale. Applied via `prisma migrate deploy` and verified present in `pg_indexes`; plain `CREATE INDEX` (not `CONCURRENTLY`) was judged safe to run as-is given the current near-empty table sizes — noted in the migration's own comments that a future deferred application after substantial data growth should use `CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY` manually instead.

**Task 9 — Realtime unaffected:** confirmed via `git status`/diff that no `app/actions/*.ts` file was touched this unit (zero `emitRealtimeEvent` call sites changed), and every `<AutoRefresh>`/`<RealtimeRefresh watch={...}>` pair in the 6 edited pages is byte-for-byte identical to before this unit's changes.

**Task 10 — Before/after verification:** at this system's current real data volume (26 offline_inventory_movements, 15 work_orders, 11 parts_requests) a wall-clock comparison is meaningless — Postgres seq-scans a few dozen rows trivially fast regardless of query shape. Built a throwaway benchmark script (seeded disposable synthetic data at a representative future scale, timed the exact old vs. new query shapes side by side, then fully deleted the synthetic data and verified table counts returned to baseline): at 45,000 offline_inventory_movements rows, `getOfflineInventoryBalance()`'s old shape took 720ms vs. the new shape's 228ms (3.2x) while returning the identical distinct-material count (311, confirming correctness); at 30,000 parts_requests rows, the old full-fetch-and-sort shape took 406ms vs. the new 3-counts-plus-bounded-fetch shape's 45.6ms total (8.9x), again with identical row-count totals (30,011) confirming no behavior change. No debug/timing logs were left in production code — the benchmark script itself was deleted after use.

**Task 11 — Data safety:** confirmed via `git diff` that zero `.create(`/`.update(`/`.delete(`/`.upsert(`/`*Many(` calls exist anywhere in this unit's diff — every change is a read-path query-shape optimization. Assets were not touched (no asset-related file in this unit's diff). Job Cards, Materials Requests, and Offline Inventory movement history data are all unaffected — the only writes performed all session were inside the disposable Task 10 benchmark, fully cleaned up and verified.

**Validation:** `npm run db:check`, `lint`, `typecheck`, and `build` all pass clean. `npx prisma generate` hit a transient Windows file-lock (`EPERM` renaming the query-engine DLL, likely a lingering process from the migration commands) on its first two attempts but the subsequent `npm run build` regenerated the client successfully as part of its own build step with no errors — `@@index` additions don't change the Prisma Client's generated TypeScript types/API surface regardless, so this was never a correctness blocker.

No approval-workflow logic, business statuses, module names, or user-facing wording were changed. No Redis, no WebSockets, no big rewrite — every change was an incremental query-shape optimization, a `take`/`select` bound, a `Promise.all` parallelization, or an additive index. No deployment performed.

## Phase ApprovalWorkflowUnit4-01 — Approval Workflow Unit 4 (Closure Approval Only) — COMPLETE

Business decision implemented: no Manager approval before starting a Job Card any more. Data Entry creates and starts a Job Card directly; Manager approval is now required only to close. New lifecycle: **Draft → Active → Closure Requested → Closed**.

**Status mapping (Task 11):** reused existing backend statuses wherever possible — Draft = `Created` (unchanged), Active = `Approved`/`Waiting Materials`/`Partially Issued`/`Materials Issued`/`Assigned`/`In Progress` (unchanged raw values; `Approved` — previously its own "nothing has moved yet" display bucket — is now folded into "Active" display-wise, since there's no more approval step for it to sit after), Closed = `Closed` (unchanged). One new raw status was required and added via 2 additive migrations: `prisma/migrations/20260805000000_approval_workflow_unit4_closure_status` (adds `'Closure Requested'` to `work_orders`' `chk_work_orders_status` CHECK constraint) and `prisma/migrations/20260805000100_approval_workflow_unit4_approvals_status` (adds the same value to `approvals_status_check` — discovered mid-verification that this table has its **own**, separate CHECK constraint from `work_orders.status`; the first migration alone would have made every `approvals` row insert for a closure request/approval fail in production). Both are pure additive `ADD CONSTRAINT` with every existing allowed value kept — no existing row, enum, or type touched. `'Under Review'` (the old pre-approval status) is kept in both constraints for backward compatibility with any pre-existing row; no new Job Card can reach it going forward.

**Backend (`lib/backend/work-orders/service.ts`):** `submitWorkOrder()` now transitions `Created → Approved` directly (was `→ Under Review`) — audit action renamed to `work_order.activated` (distinct from `startTechnicianJob`'s pre-existing `work_order.start`), realtime event `job_card.started` (new `REALTIME_EVENTS.JOB_CARD_STARTED` key), Manager notified for awareness only, no approval required. Two new exported functions: `requestJobCardClosure(context, workOrderId, note)` (role-gated to `maintenance_data_entry`/`maintenance_manager`/`maintenance_supervisor`/`super_admin`; requires the min-10-char completion note; blocks with the exact required message `"This Job Card has pending Materials Requests. Complete materials before requesting closure."` if any linked `parts_requests` row has `status != "Issued"`; valid only from an Active-bucket status, not Draft/Closed/already-Closure-Requested; writes an `approvals` row, audit log, notifies Manager, emits `job_card.closure_requested`) and `approveJobCardClosure(context, workOrderId, comments?)` (Manager/`super_admin` only; `Closure Requested → Closed`; writes `approvals`/audit/notifies Data Entry+Engineer+Manager+assigned technician via the existing `jobCardClosedRecipients` helper/emits `job_card.closed`). `closeWorkOrder()` (the Manager's direct-close button) is now gated by an explicit `assertIsManager` role check instead of the `work_orders.close` *permission* (which Data Entry/Engineer/Technician still hold in the DB — business rule 8 required restricting this specific action regardless of that grant), refuses if a closure request is already pending (points the caller to Approve Closure instead), and gained the same pending-materials-request gate as `requestJobCardClosure`. `completeTechnicianJob`/`markExternalWorkCompleted`/`startTechnicianJob` (Technician's own close, external-assignment completion) were deliberately **not** touched — out of this unit's named scope, and Task 7 explicitly says keep the workflow simple.

**Task 7 (no reject/return):** confirmed no reject/return-for-update path exists for a closure request in either new function — `Closure Requested`'s only transition target in `lib/workflows/status-rules.ts` is `Closed`.

**Server actions (`app/actions/workflow.ts`):** added `requestJobCardClosureAction`/`approveJobCardClosureAction`, following the existing `closeWorkOrderAction` redirect/revalidate/error-banner pattern exactly.

**Job Card creation (`app/actions/maintenance.ts`):** `upsertWorkOrderAction`'s `createStatus` now resolves the wizard's `submit_for_approval` intent (button relabeled, internal field-name value left as-is to avoid a wider rewire) to `"Approved"` instead of `"Under Review"` — every downstream branch keyed on that condition (operator-complaint-required check, the atomic WO+workflow-instance creation, the save-failure auto-recovery path, the Manager awareness notification) updated to match. `EDITABLE_STATUSES` widened from `["Created", "Under Review"]` to also include every `ACTIVE_JOB_CARD_STATUSES` value (business rules 4/10 — Data Entry/Manager can now edit an already-started Job Card; previously the edit form only worked pre-approval, a leftover from the old workflow that would have silently blocked editing an Active Job Card under the new one). Editing still never touches status.
