## Phase RequiredMaterialsInventoryMatchingUnit5-01 — Required Materials Inventory Matching Unit 5 — COMPLETE

Goal: when Data Entry types a Required Material during New Job Card creation, search Offline Inventory Control live, show Available/Partially Available/Not Available/New Material, and prevent case/spacing duplicates in Offline Inventory — without touching the closure-only approval workflow, module names, or manual entry.

**Task 1 — `lib/materials/normalize-material.ts` (new, client-safe, no `server-only`):** `normalizeMaterialKey()` trims, lowercases, and collapses internal whitespace runs (does not strip punctuation/hyphens — part numbers like "12-MM" stay intact). `buildMaterialIdentityKey()`/`materialIdentitiesMatch()` layer name+unit+part number+SS Rec. Code identity comparison on top, treating part number/SS Rec. Code as differentiators only when BOTH sides supply a value.

**Task 2 — search (`lib/store/offline-inventory-data.ts`, `searchOfflineInventoryMaterialsAction` in `app/actions/offline-inventory.ts`):** `searchOfflineInventoryMaterials()` follows the exact Unit 3 `getOfflineInventoryBalance()` shape — a bounded `distinct` candidate query (top 10, case-insensitive `contains` over name/part number/SS Rec. Code, non-deleted only) then a `groupBy` balance sum scoped to just those candidates. Never loads raw movement rows. The server action is called directly from the client (not a `<form action>`), gated on `work_orders.manage` (the same permission that already gates the wizard page itself, not `offline_inventory.issue` — Data Entry doesn't necessarily hold Store permissions).

**Task 3/4/5 — wizard autocomplete (`components/work-orders/work-order-wizard.tsx`):** the Required Materials table's Description/Part No./Qty/Unit inputs, previously plain uncontrolled `name`-only fields, are now backed by a `partRows` state array. Typing debounces 300ms (per-row timer + a sequence counter so a late response from an earlier keystroke can never overwrite a newer one), shows a loading spinner, and lists up to 10 suggestions (name, "Available: X UNIT", Part No., SS Rec. Code, Location) or a "No match" line. Selecting a suggestion fills name/part no./unit and stores the match's identity key + balance in row state (a hidden `req_part_material_key_i` field carries it into the form submit). Editing the name after a match clears the key (Task 5) — availability falls back to "New Material" until re-matched. Quantity changes recompute the badge from the already-known balance with no further backend call. Badge wording kept plain per Task 9: "Available", "Partially Available" (+ "Shortage: N UNIT"), "Not Available", "New Material"; helper line: "Type a material name to check Offline Inventory availability."

**Task 6 — backend save validation (`app/actions/maintenance.ts`, `resolveMaterialMatchByKey()` in `lib/store/offline-inventory-data.ts`):** `parseRequiredPartRows()` is now async and, for every row that carries a `req_part_material_key`, re-resolves that exact identity server-side (never re-searches by name) and recomputes its balance fresh before saving — a row with no key (hand-typed, never matched, or edited after matching) is saved as plain manual text with `availability_status: "unchecked"`, so a save can never silently attach a row to a material the user didn't actually pick. `WorkOrderRequiredPart.part_id` (existing FK to `parts`, previously always left `null`) is now populated when the matched identity happens to be part-linked. `availability_status` reuses the exact vocabulary the (disabled) Store inventory-check feature already defined — `available`/`partial`/`unavailable`/`unchecked` — so the Job Card detail page's existing "Materials" table (`app/(dashboard)/maintenance/work-orders/[id]/page.tsx`, unmodified) now shows accurate badges automatically, and `inventory_check_enabled` (still `false`) is untouched since that gate only ever checked for `"unchecked"` rows and every legacy row already defaulted to it.

**Task 7 — Materials Request generation:** confirmed the existing auto-create-a-Materials-Request-on-new-Job-Card-with-Required-Parts behavior in `upsertWorkOrderAction` (`createPartsRequest`, unconditional on availability) was left completely unchanged — per the task's own instruction to preserve existing Materials Request behavior and not split shortages automatically. Pending/Completed wording and the Materials Requests page are untouched.

**Task 8 — duplicate prevention (`app/actions/offline-inventory.ts`, `findExistingMaterialByNormalizedName()` in `lib/store/offline-inventory-data.ts`):** the existing exact case-insensitive duplicate guard (`findDuplicateOpeningStock`, already catching "OIL FILTER" vs "Oil Filter") is kept as the first check; a second, looser fallback pass now also catches whitespace differences (" oil   filter ") by comparing `normalizeMaterialKey(name)+unit` against a bounded per-material-identity candidate list (never raw movements). Uses exact normalized match only — no fuzzy blocking, so "Oil Filter Cartridge" is never falsely blocked by an existing "Oil Filter". Both `addOpeningStockAction` and `addNewMaterialAction` now return `"This material already exists in Offline Inventory."` with an `existingMaterialKey`; `AddNewMaterialForm` renders "View Existing" / "Receive More" links from it instead of a dead-end error.

**Task 10 — realtime:** the wizard has no live subscription to Offline Inventory changes while open (search only runs in direct response to typing; save only runs on submit) — a selected row can never auto-change mid-edit by construction. The optional "warn if stock changed at save time" round trip was not implemented (explicitly optional in the task); the save-time re-validation (Task 6) still guarantees the persisted `availability_status` reflects the true balance at save time regardless.

**Testing (Task 11):** a disposable verification script (raw Prisma calls mirroring the new logic, deleted after use) created a real "Oil Filter" / 5 PCS Offline Inventory record and confirmed: `normalizeMaterialKey` collapses case and whitespace; searching "oil filter" and "OIL FILTER" both return exactly the one existing record (no duplicate); qty 2 against balance 5 computes Available; qty 8 against balance 5 computes Shortage 3; an unknown material returns no match (New Material); the identity key round-trips stably; the exact-case duplicate check catches "OIL FILTER"; the normalized fallback catches " oil   filter "; "Oil Filter Cartridge" is correctly NOT blocked as a false duplicate. All checks passed; the database was confirmed back to its exact original baseline (26 offline_inventory_movements / 16 work_orders / 9 work_order_required_parts / 12 parts_requests) after cleanup. Live browser testing of the debounced dropdown UI itself was not performed this unit.

**Validation:** `npm run db:check`, `lint`, `typecheck`, and `build` all pass clean. No schema migration was needed — `WorkOrderRequiredPart.part_id`/`availability_status` already existed from the (disabled) inventory-check feature.

No approval workflow logic touched (Unit 4 unaffected). Job Cards/Materials Requests/Offline Inventory Control names unchanged. Manual material entry remains fully possible (a row with no inventory match saves exactly as free text, same as before this unit). No deployment performed.

## Phase RequiredMaterialsIssueShortageTrackingUnit6-01 — Required Materials Issue and Shortage Tracking Unit 6 — COMPLETE

Goal: track Required/Issued/Remaining/Available now/Shortage per Required Materials row without ever deducting Offline Inventory stock at Job Card creation — stock only moves when Offline Inventory Control's own Issue Material action runs.

**Task 1/2 — schema review, no migration:** `work_order_required_parts` already has `quantity_required`/`part_id`/`description`/`unit_of_measure` (Unit 5); `offline_inventory_movements` already has `movement_type`/`quantity`/`part_id`/`manual_material_name`/`unit`/`related_work_order_id`. Everything this unit needs already exists — no migration was added. `issued_qty` is derived, not stored: it is summed live from `offline_inventory_movements` rows with `movement_type: "ISSUED"` and `related_work_order_id` = the Job Card, matched to each required-parts row by the same `part_id`-or-manual-name+unit identity (`buildBalanceKey`) used everywhere else in Offline Inventory Control since Unit 3.

**Task 3 — `lib/work-orders/material-fulfillment.ts` (new):** `getMaterialFulfillmentForWorkOrder(db, workOrderId)` returns `{ required_qty, issued_qty, remaining_qty, available_now, shortage_qty, status }` per required-parts row, accepting either the plain `prisma` client (read-only display) or a `BackendTransaction` (consistency-locked closure guard) via one shared implementation. `remaining_qty = max(required − issued, 0)`; `shortage_qty = max(remaining − available_now, 0)` — i.e. how much of what's still owed can't currently be covered even by issuing all matching stock on hand. `anyMaterialsIncomplete()` is the exact `remaining_qty > 0` closure-blocking condition (Task 8).

**Task 4 — Job Card detail (`app/(dashboard)/maintenance/work-orders/[id]/page.tsx`):** the Materials section's required-parts table now shows Required/Issued/Remaining/Available now columns plus a status badge (Fully Issued/Partially Issued/Shortage/Ready to Issue) and a "Shortage: N UNIT" line when applicable, replacing the old single static "Materials status" (Unit 5's creation-time snapshot) badge. A per-row "Issue →" link appears when there's remaining need and stock on hand, linking straight to Offline Inventory Control's Issue Material action with both the material and this Job Card pre-selected. **Scope decision (same as Unit 5's precedent):** the list/dashboard quick-view popup was not given this same breakdown — it only ever fetched a `required_parts_count`, and giving it full per-row fulfillment would mean adding balance-aggregation queries to 3 separate list-page call sites for every previewed row. The quick view still shows its existing lightweight required-materials count and links through to the full detail page, which now has the complete picture.

**Task 5 — Issue Material flow (`components/store/issue-material-form.tsx`, `components/store/store-balance-view.tsx`, the two `/store/offline-inventory` issue routes):** issuing already always writes an `offline_inventory_movements` row with `movement_type: "ISSUED"`, already capped both client-side (`max` attribute) and server-side (existing `withBackendTransaction` + advisory-lock balance check from Backend Reliability Fix Unit 1) to the current balance — that enforcement was not touched. What was added: the "Related Job Card" `<select>` can now be pre-selected via `?workOrder=<id>` (standalone page) or a new `presetWorkOrderId` prop (modal), and both `/store/offline-inventory` and `/store/offline-inventory/issue` now look up and prepend that Job Card if it falls outside `getWorkOrderOptions()`'s most-recent-100 window, so the Job Card detail page's new "Issue" link always lands with the correct row selected. No change to the actual deduction logic — fulfillment picks it up automatically once `related_work_order_id` is set, since it's a live aggregation.

**Task 6 — no auto-issue at creation:** confirmed unchanged — `upsertWorkOrderAction` and `createPartsRequest` (the auto-created Materials Request) never write to `offline_inventory_movements`; the only two write paths for `movement_type: "ISSUED"` in the whole codebase are `issueOfflineMaterialAction` (Offline Inventory Control's own Issue Material) and this fulfillment module, which is read-only.

**Task 7 — no duplicate Offline Inventory materials:** untouched — this unit adds no new material-creation path; Unit 5's normalized duplicate guard on Add New Material/Add Opening Stock is unaffected.

**Task 8 — closure blocking (`lib/backend/work-orders/service.ts`):** a new `assertRequiredMaterialsFulfilled()` guard (using `getMaterialFulfillmentForWorkOrder`/`anyMaterialsIncomplete` inside the same transaction) runs in both `requestJobCardClosure()` and `closeWorkOrder()`, ahead of Unit 4's existing `assertNoPendingMaterialsRequests` check. The two checks are deliberately both kept: the existing one asks "has everything on the auto-created Materials Request been *received* into store" (`parts_requests.status`), the new one asks "has everything actually been *handed out* to this Job Card" (`work_order_required_parts` vs `ISSUED` movements) — a request can be fully received while nothing has been issued to the technician yet, so the old check alone would have let closure through in exactly the scenario this unit is about. Exact new messages: `"This Job Card still has pending required materials. Complete materials before requesting closure."` (request closure) and `"...before closing."` (Manager direct close) — Task 7's "no reject/return" and every other Unit 4 rule are untouched.

**Task 9 — Materials Requests page:** no file under `app/(dashboard)/store/parts-requests/` or `lib/backend/parts-requests/` was touched this unit; Pending/Completed wording, `issueMaterials()` (the Receive Materials flow), and the request list/detail pages are exactly as Unit 5 left them.

**Testing:** a disposable verification script (deleted after use) built a real Job Card with a "Brake Pad" / 4 PCS required row and 2 PCS in Offline Inventory, then walked the full business example end to end: confirmed Job Card creation writes zero inventory movements; before any issuing, Required 4 / Available 2 / Shortage 2 (status "shortage") and closure correctly blocked; after issuing the 2 available PCS against the Job Card, Required 4 / Issued 2 / Remaining 2 / Available 0 / Shortage 2 (status "partial_issued") and closure still blocked; after receiving 2 more and issuing the remaining 2, Required 4 / Issued 4 / Remaining 0 / Shortage 0 (status "fulfilled") and closure allowed; final Offline Inventory balance correctly at 0. All 8 checks passed; the database was confirmed back to its exact original baseline (26 movements / 16 work orders / 9 required-parts rows) afterward. Live browser testing of the new detail-page table/Issue link was not performed this unit.

**Validation:** `npm run db:check`, `lint`, `typecheck`, and `build` all pass clean. No migration.

Closure-only approval workflow (Unit 4) unchanged beyond the one additive guard described above. Job Cards/Materials Requests/Offline Inventory Control names unchanged. Pending/Completed Materials Requests wording unchanged. No deployment performed.

## Phase WorkAssignmentWorkerProfilesUnit7-01 — Work Assignment and Worker Profiles Foundation Unit 7 — COMPLETE

Goal: foundation only — worker profiles (no-login labor records) and a role-differentiated Internal Team roster with hourly-rate snapshots, ready for a future timer/work-session unit. No Start/Pause/Resume/Stop implemented.

**Task 1 — schema review, key finding:** `work_order_assignments` already fully implements Internal Technician / Freelancer / External Company assignment (`assignTechnicians()` in `lib/backend/work-orders/service.ts`, unchanged this unit) — but its "Internal" path only supports ONE flat role (`technician_id` → a real login `profiles` row) with no Supervisor/Technician/Helper distinction and no hourly-rate field at all. `work_order_labor` is a separate, disconnected manual hours-logging table. Neither fits "workers who don't need a login." Decision: keep `work_order_assignments`/`assignTechnicians()` completely untouched (technician self-service login-linkage + Freelancer/Company, per "do not remove existing Assign Work options") and add two new, additive tables for the labor-roster concept instead of overloading the existing one.

**Task 2 — `worker_profiles` (new table, `prisma/migrations/20260806000000_work_assignment_worker_profiles_unit7`):** `name`/`worker_type` (Supervisor/Technician/"Helper/Labor")/`hourly_rate`/`phone`/`skill_category` (Auto/Mechanical/Electrical/Other)/`is_active`/`notes`/timestamps/`created_by`/`updated_by`. No login, no `auth_users` link — a plain labor-roster record. CRUD in `lib/backend/workers/service.ts`, gated on the existing `work_orders.assign` permission (already held by Data Entry, Maintenance Engineer, Manager, super_admin) rather than adding a new permission — worker profiles only exist to serve Job Card assignment, same audience, "keep it simple."

**Task 3 — Worker Profiles UI (`/admin/worker-profiles`, new):** search (name/phone), filter by worker type and active/inactive, Add/Edit modal, Deactivate/Reactivate toggle. Duplicate prevention reuses `normalizeMaterialKey` (Unit 5's material-name normalizer — generic enough to reuse here) on name+phone, only against currently-active workers, exact-normalized match only (no fuzzy blocking, same principle as Unit 5's Offline Inventory duplicate guard). Nav entry added under "Operations" (next to "Technician") for Super Admin, Manager, and Data Entry nav groups — Maintenance Engineer's nav was left untouched (already deliberately trimmed read-only in an earlier unit).

**Task 4/5 — `work_order_worker_assignments` (new table) + `lib/backend/work-orders/worker-roster.ts`:** the per-Job-Card Internal Team roster — Supervisor (one) + Technicians (many) + Helpers/Labor (many), each row created from a `worker_profiles` pick with `hourly_rate_snapshot` copied at assignment time and never re-read afterward (Task 8's "future rate changes must not change old Job Card costs" — verified by test). Editing the roster is a soft replace: previously-`active` rows are marked `status: "removed"` (never hard-deleted) and a fresh set of `active` rows is created — preserving full history for a future work-session/timer table to `FK` onto this table's `id` (Task 8) without invalidating anything a roster correction removed. A separate save action (`assignInternalTeamRoster`/`saveInternalTeamRosterAction`) from the existing `assignTechnicians`/`assignTechniciansAction` — rendered as its own "Assign/Edit Internal Team" panel directly below the existing "Assign Work" panel on the Job Card detail page (`components/work-orders/workflow-actions.tsx`), not merged into it. Freelancer/External Company got one small additive field on the *existing* `work_order_assignments` table — `agreed_amount` (Decimal, nullable) — added to both existing assignment forms/actions; no new table needed there since everything else Task 5 asks for (name, phone, work type via the existing `external_trade` field, notes) already existed.

**Task 6 — permissions:** worker-profile management and both roster/assignment actions reuse `work_orders.assign` (no new permission row). Internal Team roster editable by anyone holding that permission (or Manager) any time the Job Card is not `Closed` — wider than the existing `canAssign`'s workflow-step gate, since labor-roster tracking isn't tied to the materials-resolved step. Once `Closed`, roster edits are blocked for **everyone**, including Manager — Unit 4 removed every post-closure correction path and this unit does not reopen one; the task's "Manager/Super Admin edit only if existing correction policy allows" was read literally as "no such policy exists post-Unit-4, so no one edits."

**Task 7 — Job Card detail display:** the existing "Assignment" block (technician/Freelancer/External Company, already existed) gained an `agreed_amount` line (cost-gated by `canViewCosts`, matching the app's existing cost-visibility invariant) and "Work type" relabeling of the existing trade field for consistency with this unit's wording. A new, separate "Internal Team" block groups the roster by Supervisor/Technicians/Helpers-Labor with each worker's name and (cost-gated) hourly rate, plus one "Assigned … by …" line with any notes. **Scope decision (same precedent as Units 5/6):** the list/dashboard quick-view popup was not extended with the new roster display or the `agreed_amount` line — kept at its existing lightweight assignment summary, linking through to the full detail page.

**Task 8 — future time-tracking readiness:** `work_order_worker_assignments` was deliberately shaped so a later unit's work-session table needs only one new table with a `worker_assignment_id` FK to this one — `id` is stable and never reused/deleted (soft `status` field), `hourly_rate_snapshot` is already frozen per-assignment (a session's amount = duration × this snapshot, no rate lookup needed), and `assigned_by`/`assigned_at`/`notes` already give the "who/when" side. No timer/session table or Start/Pause/Resume/Stop UI was implemented, per the task's explicit instruction.

**Task 9 — realtime:** new `job_card.assignment_updated` and `worker_profile.updated` event keys (both under existing watched prefixes — `"job_card."` since Unit 2, and a new but analogous `"worker_profile."` watched only by the new admin page itself) — emitted from `assignInternalTeamRoster`/the worker-profile service functions. No new SSE mechanism; reuses the existing 15s poll.

**Task 10 — audit:** `worker_profile.create`/`update`/`activate`/`deactivate` and `work_order.assignment_updated` all write through the existing `writeAuditLog()` — no direct-insert.

**Testing:** a disposable verification script (deleted after use) created Supervisor/Technician/Helper worker profiles, confirmed the normalized-duplicate guard fires for a re-typed near-identical name+phone and not for a genuinely different worker; created a Job Card and assigned all three to it with rate snapshots (5 / 3 / 1.5 KWD/hr); changed the Supervisor's profile rate afterward and confirmed the existing assignment row's snapshot stayed at 5; edited the roster and confirmed the old 3 rows flipped to `status: "removed"` (not deleted) while exactly 1 new `active` row was created; created a Freelancer and an External Company assignment with `agreed_amount` and confirmed both persisted; confirmed a `Closed` Job Card's status blocks the roster-edit guard's condition. All checks passed; the database was confirmed back to its exact original baseline afterward. Live browser testing of the new UI (Worker Profiles admin page, Internal Team picker, Job Card detail display) was not performed this unit.

**Validation:** `npm run db:check`, `lint`, `typecheck`, and `build` all pass clean. One migration (`20260806000000_work_assignment_worker_profiles_unit7`) — purely additive: one nullable column on `work_order_assignments`, two new tables. Hit the same transient Windows `EPERM` file-lock on `npx prisma generate` seen in earlier units (a lingering process holding the query-engine DLL); not a blocker — `npm run build` regenerated the client successfully as part of its own build step. One real bug caught along the way: a client component (`worker-profiles-view.tsx`) originally imported `WORKER_TYPES` from the server-only `validators.ts`, which `next build` correctly rejected — fixed by splitting the plain constants into a new client-safe `lib/backend/workers/constants.ts`, mirroring the existing `simplified-status-display.ts`/`simplified-status.ts` split from Unit 4.

No approval or closure workflow logic touched. Job Cards/Materials Requests/Offline Inventory Control names unchanged. Existing "Assign Work" (technician/Freelancer/External Company) fully intact and unchanged in behavior, only gaining the one optional `agreed_amount` field. No deployment performed.

## Phase WorkSessionTimeTrackingUnit8-01 — Work Session Time Tracking and Labor Cost Calculation Unit 8 — COMPLETE

Goal: Start/Pause/Resume/Stop work-session tracking for Internal Team roster workers (Unit 7) with automatic duration/labor-cost calculation, manual time entry, Manager correction with audit, and closure blocking only while a session is actively running.

**Task 1/2 — schema (new table, `prisma/migrations/20260807000000_work_session_time_tracking_unit8`):** `work_order_work_sessions` FKs to `WorkOrderWorkerAssignment.id` (Unit 7), not directly to `worker_profiles.id` — per the task's own instruction, since the assignment row is what carries the frozen `hourly_rate_snapshot` for this specific Job Card (a worker can be on several Job Cards with different snapshots). `worker_id` is kept alongside as a denormalized read-shortcut only, never a source of truth. Session lifecycle implemented exactly per the task's "Preferred for simplicity" design: Start/Resume always creates a brand-new `Active` row; Pause freezes it at `Paused` and Stop freezes it at `Completed`, both computing `duration_minutes`/`calculated_amount` from `started_at` to now — no in-place pause-interval math, multiple sessions per worker per Job Card is the normal, supported shape (verified against the task's own Day 1/Day 2 example: 60 min + 180 min = 240 min).

**Task 3 — session rules (`lib/backend/work-orders/work-sessions.ts`):** exactly one `Active` session per worker assignment at a time (checked before every Start/Resume); Pause/Stop require an existing `Active` session; sessions blocked once the Job Card is `Closed` or once the worker's roster row itself is no longer `status: "active"` (i.e., was removed from the Internal Team in a later Unit 7 roster edit); duration is clamped to `>= 0` and computed from real timestamps so it can never go negative.

**Task 4 — calculation:** `duration_minutes = round((end - start) / 60000)`; `calculated_amount = round((duration_minutes / 60) * hourly_rate_snapshot, 3 decimals)` (KWD, matching the project's existing `Decimal(12,3)` convention everywhere else). Verified: 60 min at 2 KWD/hr → exactly 2.000 KWD; 240 min (60+180) at 2 KWD/hr → exactly 8.000 KWD.

**Task 5 — manual time entry:** `addManualTimeEntry()` creates a `Completed`, `is_manual_entry: true` session directly from Data-Entry-supplied start/stop timestamps (stop must be after start — enforced both in the Zod schema and the service). Blocked if the worker assignment currently has an `Active` session (must be stopped/paused first) — the one overlap rule the task asked for, not full interval-overlap detection against historical sessions.

**Task 6 — Job Card detail UI (`components/work-orders/work-time-tracking.tsx` + `worker-session-row.tsx`, new "Work Time Tracking" section, separate from the existing "Technician Work"/Assignment section):** one row per active Internal Team roster worker showing name, role, hourly rate, a derived status (Not Started / Active / Paused / Completed, from that worker's most recent non-cancelled session), total hours, and total cost. Buttons follow the task's exact rule: no sessions → "Start Work"; `Active` → "Pause" + "Stop Work"; `Paused`/`Completed` → "Resume Work"; "Add Manual Entry" and "View Sessions" always available while not Closed (View Sessions stays available read-only even when Closed).

**Task 7 — Manager edit/correction (`session-history-modal.tsx`):** "View Sessions" opens a full session history (including cancelled rows, for the correction trail) with a Manager-only Edit/Correct and Cancel Session action per non-active row. Editing recalculates `duration_minutes`/`calculated_amount` from the new timestamps and unconditionally requires a `correction_reason` (min 5 characters, enforced in both the Zod schema and the service — there is no silent-edit path). Cancelling is a soft `status: "Cancelled"` (never a hard delete), also reason-required, and excluded from every total.

**Task 8 — reports/aggregation foundation (`lib/work-orders/work-session-totals.ts`):** `getWorkOrderLaborSummary(db, workOrderId)` (Job Card-level totals + per-worker breakdown, used today by the detail page and by the Task 10 closure guard — accepts either `prisma` or a transaction client, same generic-`DbClient` pattern as Unit 6's material-fulfillment helper) plus three not-yet-wired-anywhere helpers ready for a future Manager dashboard/reports unit: `getWorkerLaborTotals()` (totals per worker, optional date range), `getActiveWorkSessions()` (who's working right now, across every Job Card), and `getSessionsForAssignment()` (full history, also used by "View Sessions"). Cancelled sessions are excluded from every aggregate.

**Task 9 — assignment integration:** work sessions are only reachable through an `Active`-roster `WorkOrderWorkerAssignment.id` — Freelancer/External Company assignments live in the separate `work_order_assignments` table with no relation to sessions at all, so there is no code path that could ever attach a timer to one; their `agreed_amount` (Unit 7) stays exactly where it was, in the Assignment section, untouched by this unit.

**Task 10 — closure blocking (`lib/backend/work-orders/service.ts`):** a new `assertNoActiveWorkSessions()` guard runs in both `requestJobCardClosure()` and `closeWorkOrder()`, alongside (not replacing) Unit 6's materials-fulfillment guard and Unit 4's Materials-Request guard. Only a currently-`Active` session blocks — Paused/Completed/Cancelled historical sessions never do. Exact messages: *"This Job Card has active work sessions. Stop all work sessions before requesting closure."* and *"...before closing."* Time tracking itself was not made mandatory for closure — a Job Card with zero sessions ever recorded closes exactly as it did before this unit.

**Task 11 — realtime:** four new event keys — `job_card.work_started`, `job_card.work_paused`, `job_card.work_stopped`, `job_card.work_time_updated` (the last one shared by manual entry, edit, and cancel) — all under the already-watched `"job_card."` prefix, so no page's `RealtimeRefresh` list needed changes.

**Task 12 — audit:** `work_order.work_session_started`/`_paused`/`_stopped`/`_manual_entry`/`_edited`/`_cancelled`, each via the existing `writeAuditLog()` with actor, Job Card id/number, worker assignment id, worker name, duration, and (for edits/cancels) the correction reason — all six also mapped to friendly Activity Timeline entries on the Job Card detail page, not just raw System Audit.

**Task 13 — data safety:** no hard deletes anywhere in this unit — cancelling a session is a `status` flip, never a row removal; no asset, materials, or approval/closure workflow file was touched beyond the one additive closure guard described above; Unit 7's worker-profile/roster tables and logic are completely unmodified.

**Testing:** a disposable verification script (deleted after use) created 3 worker profiles and an Internal Team roster, then walked the full lifecycle: Start Work created exactly one `Active` session (and a simulated duplicate Start was confirmed blocked by the existing-Active-session check); a simulated Pause at +60 min computed 60 min / 2.000 KWD exactly; Resume Work created a genuinely new session row (old one preserved, not overwritten); a simulated Stop at +180 min on the new session brought the running total to 240 min / 8.000 KWD across the two rows, matching the task's own Day 1/Day 2 example; a manual time entry correctly added to the total; a Manager-style edit recalculated duration/amount and stored the correction reason + editor; an `Active` session correctly signaled a closure block, and stopping it correctly cleared that block; a `Closed` Job Card's status was confirmed to trip the "no further session changes" guard condition. All checks passed; the database was confirmed back to its exact original baseline afterward (one pre-existing worker profile from the user's own earlier manual Unit 7 testing was left untouched throughout, as expected). Live browser testing of the new UI was not performed this unit.

**Validation:** `npm run db:check`, `lint`, `typecheck`, and `build` all pass clean. One migration, purely additive (one new table only — no existing table altered). Two issues caught and fixed before final validation: a TS `Json` metadata-typing error in the shared `notifyAndAudit()` helper (narrowed a parameter from `Record<string, unknown>` to `Record<string, string | number | undefined>`), and an ESLint `react-hooks/set-state-in-effect` violation in the session-history modal's data-fetch effect (restructured to an inline cancelled-flag `.then()` pattern with a numeric `reloadToken` dependency instead of calling an outer `load()` function from the effect body). Hit the same transient Windows `EPERM` `prisma generate` file-lock seen in every prior unit — not a blocker, `npm run build` regenerated the client as part of its own build step.

No approval or closure workflow logic changed beyond the one additive active-session guard. Job Cards/Materials Requests/Offline Inventory Control names unchanged. Required Materials logic (Units 5/6) untouched. Worker Profile foundation (Unit 7) unchanged except for the new inverse relations needed for this table's foreign keys. Time tracking is not mandatory for closure. No deployment performed.

## Phase OptionalAssignmentDuringJobCardCreationUnit7C-01 — Optional Work Assignment During Job Card Creation Unit 7C — COMPLETE

Goal: let Data Entry optionally assign work (Internal Team / Freelancer / External Company) right inside the New Job Card wizard, using Unit 7's worker-profile foundation, without making assignment mandatory or touching any other workflow. Schema-free unit — no migration.

**Files changed:** `components/work-orders/work-order-wizard.tsx` (Step 3 UI, Review summary, new `InternalTeamWizardFields` sub-component), `app/actions/maintenance.ts` (`parseWizardAssignment()` + post-creation save step), `components/work-orders/job-card-created-modal.tsx` (new `assignmentWarning` banner), and the 5 pages that render `<WorkOrderWizard>` (`maintenance/work-orders/new/page.tsx`, `maintenance/work-orders/page.tsx` (2 call sites), `dashboard/page.tsx`, `assets/vehicles/page.tsx`, `assets/[id]/page.tsx`) — each now also fetches `getActiveWorkerProfilesForAssignment()` and computes a `work_orders.assign` permission flag, only when the modal is actually open (same lazy-fetch convention the existing asset-picker fetch already used). No new backend logic, no new tables — this unit is UI + one server-action wiring step on top of Unit 7's existing `assignInternalTeamRoster()`/`assignTechnicians()`.

**Step 3 UI:** renamed "Work Team / Division" → "Work Team & Assignment" (unchanged Auto/Mechanical/Electrical/Other radio group kept exactly as-is), with a new optional "Assign work now" checkbox below it, shown only when the current user holds `work_orders.assign` (Task 10 — the section simply doesn't render otherwise, no dead/disabled UI). Checking it reveals an Assignment Type selector (Internal Team default / Freelancer / External Company) and the matching fields from Tasks 3–5 exactly as specified, including "Show hourly rate beside each selected worker" for the Internal Team picker.

**Internal Team:** Supervisor (single select, optional), Technicians (multi-select, optional), Helpers/Labor (multi-select, optional) — sourced only from `getActiveWorkerProfilesForAssignment()` (already `is_active`-filtered server-side, with `assignInternalTeamRoster()`'s own active-worker check as a second safety net). "At least one worker" is enforced only when Assign work now is on and Internal Team is selected, in both the step's client-side `validate()` and implicitly server-side (an assignment with nothing selected simply parses to `null`, per Task 6's "assignment remains Not assigned" default).

**Freelancer/External Company:** same fields Unit 7 already added to `work_order_assignments` (name/company required, phone, work type, agreed amount, notes) — this unit just surfaces them one step earlier, reusing `assignTechnicians()` unchanged.

**Save/start behavior (Task 6):** the assignment is only ever created as a second step *after* the Job Card itself commits, and *only* when `createStatus === "Approved"` (i.e., "Start Job Card" was clicked, not "Save Draft") — never nested inside the Job Card's own creation transaction, matching the exact non-nested pattern already established for the auto-created Materials Request (Unit 5) in this same function: if the assignment save fails, the Job Card is *not* rolled back (it's already valid on its own), the failure is logged via `logSystemError`, and the created-Job-Card success modal shows a new "assignment could not be saved automatically" warning banner (mirroring the existing attachment/materials-request warning banners) so the user can assign manually from the Job Card instead.

**Draft behavior (Task 7 — decision documented as required):** chose the safer of the two options explicitly. Assignment is **never** saved on Draft, for either assignment path uniformly — deferred until the Job Card is actually started. This was not an arbitrary choice: `assignTechnicians()` (the Freelancer/External Company path) forces a transition to the `"Assigned"` status, which is not a legal transition from `"Created"` (Draft's status) in Unit 4's transition map — attempting it on a Draft would hard-fail. Internal Team assignment (`assignInternalTeamRoster()`) has no such transition requirement and technically *could* save safely on a Draft, but deferring both paths identically avoids an asymmetric, harder-to-explain rule ("Internal Team saves on Draft but Freelancer doesn't") for a Data-Entry-facing feature that's explicitly asked to stay simple. The Review & Save step shows the exact required note when this applies: *"If you Save Draft, assignment will be saved when the Job Card is started — Draft does not save assignment yet."*

**Review & Save summary (Task 8):** new "Assignment" section showing exactly the task's specified layout — "Not assigned yet" when off; Internal Team's Supervisor/Technicians/Helpers-Labor (built from live React state + the `activeWorkers` list, not the wizard's generic FormData-scraped review dump, since that mechanism collapses repeated multi-select field names down to one value); Freelancer's Name/Agreed amount; External Company's Company/Agreed amount.

**Job Card detail consistency (Task 9) / Work Time Tracking integration (Task 10 alias — this unit's Task 9/Task 10 label reuse of "Task 10" numbering, see business note):** required zero additional code — since this unit calls the exact same `assignInternalTeamRoster()`/`assignTechnicians()` functions the Job Card detail page's own "Assign Internal Team"/"Assign Work" panels call, every downstream consumer (the Assignment/Internal Team display blocks from Units 6/7, the Work Time Tracking section and its Start/Pause/Resume/Stop buttons from Unit 8, the closure-blocking guards) already reads from the same tables and behaves identically whether the assignment was made during creation or afterward. Timer controls remain gated exactly as Unit 8 left them — available once the Job Card is Active and not Closed, nothing from this unit changes that gate.

**Permissions (Task 10):** every one of the 5 wizard entry points now computes `canAssignAtCreation = super_admin OR context.permissions.includes("work_orders.assign")` and only fetches/passes the active-workers list when true; the wizard component itself never renders the "Assign work now" section without that flag. Data Entry, Manager, and any other role already holding `work_orders.assign` (Engineer, per Unit 3's grants) can use it; anyone else creating a Job Card sees the wizard exactly as before this unit.

**Realtime/audit (Task 11):** no new event keys added — `assignInternalTeamRoster()` already emits `job_card.assignment_updated` and audits `work_order.assignment_updated`; `assignTechnicians()` already emits `job_card.assigned` and audits `work_order.assign`. Both were reused completely unchanged; this unit only adds new *call sites* to functions whose notification/audit/realtime behavior was already correct and already tested in Units 4 and 7.

**Testing:** a disposable verification script (deleted after use) covered all 12 numbered scenarios: Assign-work-now-disabled leaves a Job Card with zero roster/assignment rows; an Internal Team pick (Supervisor+Technician+Helper) produces exactly 3 `active` roster rows readable by both the detail page's query shape and Work Time Tracking's identical query shape, with hourly-rate snapshots (6 / 3 / 1.25 KWD/hr) matching the worker profiles' rates at save time; a Freelancer assignment with an agreed amount and an External Company assignment with an agreed amount both persist correctly; and a Draft-status Job Card was confirmed to never qualify for the `createStatus === "Approved"` gate, so no assignment rows are ever created for it. All checks passed; the database was confirmed back to its exact original baseline afterward. Live browser testing of the new wizard step was not performed this unit.

**Validation:** `npm run db:check`, `lint`, `typecheck`, and `build` all pass clean. No migration — this unit added no schema.

## Phase AssignmentPickerAndStartedModalUnit7D-01 — Simplify Assignment Picker and Job Card Started Next-Step Modal Unit 7D — COMPLETE

## Phase WorkTrackingEntryPointsUnit8B-01 — Job Card Work Tracking Entry Points and Assignment Visibility Unit 8B — COMPLETE

Display-logic unit — no schema, no backend write-path changes.

Unit 7's Internal Team roster (`work_order_worker_assignments`) and Unit 8's work sessions (`work_order_work_sessions`) are separate tables with no relation to that one — a Job Card assigned purely through Unit 7C's wizard or the detail page's "Assign Internal Team" panel had zero rows in `work_order_assignments` and so displayed as fully unassigned everywhere outside the detail page itself.

**Fix pattern (Tasks 1/2/3/4/8) — one added `_count` block, not new queries:** every place that already runs a per-Job-Card (or per-page) Prisma query for this purpose (`work-orders/page.tsx`'s main paginated list query and its `previewWO` quick-view query, `dashboard/page.tsx`'s own `previewWO` query) gained two more `_count.select` fields — `work_order_worker_assignments` (filtered to `status: "active"`) and `work_order_work_sessions` (filtered to `status: "Active"`) — via Prisma's filtered-relation-count syntax. This is the same query Prisma was already running for the page; no new round trip, no per-row query, satisfying Task 8's "no heavy query on every row" explicitly.

**Task 1 — Job Cards list Assignment column:** now checks the Internal Team count first — `"N worker(s) assigned"` when `> 0` — before falling back to the existing Freelancer/Company/technician-names logic, before finally "Not assigned". "Not assigned" now only shows when genuinely nothing is assigned through either mechanism.

**Task 2 — "Ready to assign" helper text:** `getNextAction()` in the list page gained an optional 4th parameter (`{ hasInternalTeam, hasPendingMaterials, hasActiveSession }`, defaulted so every untouched call site keeps working) and the task's exact priority ladder — Active session → "Work in progress"; Materials pending → "Materials pending"; Workers assigned → "Workers assigned"; else → "Ready to assign" (unchanged). **Scope decision:** applied only to the two statuses whose text was literally "Ready to assign" today (Approved, Materials Issued) — "Waiting Materials"/"Partially Issued"/"Assigned"/"In Progress" keep their own already-specific, already-correct wording untouched, to avoid regressing well-established behavior for a case the task's own "Current: Active status may show: Ready to assign" framing didn't target. "Materials pending" reuses the list's existing `materialsSummaryByWoId` map (Unit 3) — no new query for that signal either.

**Task 3/4 — quick-view (`components/work-orders/repair-order-quick-view.tsx`):** `QuickViewData` gained two new *optional* fields (`internalTeamCount`, `hasActiveWorkSession` — optional so `store/parts-requests/page.tsx`'s own quick-view usage, not touched this unit, keeps compiling and degrades safely to "unassigned/no session" rather than guessing). A new "Next Action" section renders the task's exact 6-case ladder (Closed/Closure Requested checked first as terminal overrides — a Closed Job Card can never say "materials pending" just because an old request happens to still be open — then materials/assignment/session, matching the task's literal cases). Two new link-only buttons — "Assign Workers" (no assignment at all, `canAssign` holders only) and "Track Work" (any assignment exists, including via an active session, since a session can't exist without one) — both target `/maintenance/work-orders/{id}#work-time-tracking`, following the file's own established pattern (`showViewAssignment` already links to `#assignment` the same way) rather than adding inline Start/Pause/Stop controls to this already-large popup, per the task's own "do not put timer controls in the quick-view" instruction. "Receive Materials"/"View Materials" already existed in the Materials section from earlier units and were left exactly where they are rather than duplicated into a new area — the file has an explicit prior design decision ("no separate Quick Actions section — actions live inside their relevant section") this unit didn't want to relitigate.

**Task 5 — Work Time Tracking entry (`components/work-orders/work-time-tracking.tsx`):** the section's `id="work-time-tracking"` anchor already existed from Unit 8, but the component returned `null` (no section, no anchor in the DOM at all) whenever no internal workers were assigned yet — meaning "Assign Workers"/"Track Work" links pointing at that anchor would silently do nothing for exactly the Job Cards that most needed the prompt. Fixed by always rendering the section: an empty Job Card now shows "No internal workers assigned yet." plus its own "Assign Workers" button (Task 7) instead of vanishing. A new tiny client component, `components/work-orders/scroll-to-section.tsx`, additionally supports a `?section=work-time` deep link (smooth-scrolls to the anchor on load) as the task's second suggested mechanism, alongside the plain `#work-time-tracking` fragment links used everywhere else.

**Task 6 — Job Card detail top summary:** a new 5-column card (Status / Assignment / Materials / Work Time / Next Action) at the very top of the page, built from data the page already loads this unit (`wo.work_order_assignments`, `wo.work_order_worker_assignments`, `wo.parts_requests`, `laborSummary` from Unit 8) — no new query. Next Action reuses the same 6-case ladder as the quick-view (duplicated rather than shared, since one renders server-side and the other client-side, and the ladder is short).

Closed-Job-Card read-only behavior (Unit 8's own gate) is untouched.

## Phase JobCardDetailSimplificationUnit8C-01 — Job Card Detail Page Simplification Unit 8C — COMPLETE

Goal: reorganize the full Job Card detail page (`app/(dashboard)/maintenance/work-orders/[id]/page.tsx`, ~2000+ lines) for Data Entry clarity — status/next-action/assignment/materials/work-time/closure all readable at a glance — without touching approval workflow, materials logic, work session logic, or assignment save logic. UI/UX cleanup unit only; no schema change.

**Structural approach:** `components/work-orders/workflow-actions.tsx` previously rendered every action form (Submit/Approve/Assign Work/Internal Team roster/Start Progress/Mark External Complete/Edit-before-approval/Request Closure/Approve Closure/Close) inline, always-visible, in one sidebar card. It now takes a required `section: "status" | "assignment" | "closure"` prop and returns only that group's forms — every permission check and `<form action=.../>` is byte-for-byte unchanged, only *which* forms a given call renders and *where the page places that call* changed. This let the page relocate forms into new sections without touching a single gate or server action.

**1. Top Operational Summary:** expanded the existing Unit 8B 5-column strip into a full card — Job Card #, Asset, Issue, Created, Reported by, Work Team/Division (all `InfoBlock`s) plus a chip row: overall status badge + Assignment/Materials/Work Time/Closure chips (`Assigned`/`Not assigned`; `Pending`/`Completed`/`No materials`; `Not Started`/`In Progress`/`Completed Sessions`; `Not Ready`/`Ready`/`Requested`/`Closed`). The Closure chip is new — computed from a read-only mirror of the three backend closure guards (see below), never calling them.

**2. Next Action panel (`id="next-action"`):** single panel, title "Next Action". For Created/Under Review (or while a correction is pending) it hosts `WorkflowActions section="status"` — Submit/Approve/Start-Progress/Edit-before-approval/Mark-External-Complete, or the existing fallback description text, unchanged logic. Once the Job Card reaches the Active bucket (or Closure Requested/Closed), a 7-case ladder takes over with the task's exact verbatim messages and buttons that navigate to the section where the actual action lives (`?editAssignment=1#assignment`, `#work-time-tracking`, `#parts`, `#closure-panel`, or the Materials Request link) — no new forms, buttons are pure navigation. `WorkflowActions section="status"` is still rendered below the ladder too, so Assigned→In Progress / Mark External Complete remain reachable exactly as before even while the ladder is showing.

**3. Assignment section (`id="assignment"`):** read-only summary only — Assignment type, Supervisor/Technicians/Helpers (Internal Team) or type/name/agreed-amount (legacy technician/Freelancer/External Company), hourly rate gated by `canViewCosts` exactly as before, assigned-by/date. An "Edit Assignment" button (shown only when a page-level mirror of `canAssign`/`canManageRoster` — `canEditAssignmentNow` — is true) opens a `LargeFormModal` via `?editAssignment=1`, reusing the same `LargeFormModal` pattern already established by the Materials Requests page's "New Materials Request" modal. The modal's body is `WorkflowActions section="assignment"` — the exact same `AssignmentForm`/`InternalTeamRosterForm` blocks, unchanged.

**4. Work Time Tracking:** unchanged component (`WorkTimeTracking`, Unit 8/8B), moved directly below the new Assignment section instead of after the old combined "Technician Work" block, so it's visible without scrolling past unrelated content.

**5. Materials section:** summary cards changed from 2 (Materials requests/Open requests) to 4 (Required items / Issued items / Remaining items / Open material requests, all derived from the already-loaded `materialFulfillment`/`openPartsRequests` — no new query). The required-materials table gained a dedicated "Action" column (Issue Material / Receive Materials / Request Materials / View Request / Fulfilled, one clear link per row) separated from the Status column's badge+shortage text. "Materials used" is now a collapsed-by-default `<details>` instead of always-visible. "Record material used" is no longer an inline form — a "Record Material Used" button opens a `LargeFormModal` via `?recordMaterial=1` containing the exact same `addWorkOrderMaterialAction` form/fields, just relocated.

**6. Closure panel (`id="closure-panel"`, new):** shows the Closure chip plus, when not ready, a plain-language reason list — mirrors (read-only, never calls) the three backend guards in `lib/backend/work-orders/service.ts` (`assertNoPendingMaterialsRequests`, `assertRequiredMaterialsFulfilled`/`anyMaterialsIncomplete`, `assertNoActiveWorkSessions`) using data already loaded on the page. `WorkflowActions section="closure"` (Request Closure/Approve Closure/Close Job Card — unchanged forms) is only rendered when ready or already Closure Requested; otherwise a "Resolve the items above to unlock closure actions" placeholder is shown instead of a button that would just fail server-side. This is a UI-only proactive disable, not a workflow change — the backend guards were already the actual authority.

**7. Sidebar:** now only Quick Facts + QR code — the `WorkflowActions` sidebar call was removed entirely (its three groups now live in the Next Action panel, the Assignment modal, and the Closure panel). Print/Back to Job Cards remain in the page header (`PageHeader` actions), where they already were — not duplicated into the sidebar.

**8. Activity Timeline:** unchanged — the friendly timeline `<details open>` and the manager-only System Audit `<details>` (no `open` attribute, i.e. already collapsed by default) were already exactly what the task asked for; no changes needed.

**9. Responsive behavior:** all new sections reuse the page's existing Tailwind responsive conventions (`sm:`/`lg:`/`xl:` grid breakpoints on the summary/metric-card grids, full-width stacked buttons on narrow screens via `flex-wrap`) — no new breakpoint system introduced.

**Data/backend unchanged confirmation:** no migration, no Prisma schema change, no server action signature change, no change to `lib/workflows/status-rules.ts` or any of the three closure guards. `WorkflowActions`' internal boolean gates (`canSubmit`/`canApprove`/`canAssign`/`canManageRoster`/`canRequestClosure`/`canApproveClosure`/`canClose`/etc.) are byte-for-byte the same expressions as before Unit 8C — only the JSX return was split by `section`. The one new page-level duplication (`canAssignWorkNow`/`canManageRosterNow`, `ACTIVE_BUCKET_STATUSES`) mirrors `workflow-actions.tsx`'s own conditions for button-visibility purposes only; the real authorization still lives entirely inside `WorkflowActions`.

**Bug found and fixed during review:** the Next Action ladder's "Issue Material" button initially pointed at `#materials`, but the Materials section's actual id is `#parts` (pre-existing, unchanged) — caught and fixed before validation.

**Testing:** `npm run db:check`, `lint`, `typecheck`, and `build` all pass clean. No live browser verification was performed — no browser-automation tool was available in this environment and no login credentials were available to script an authenticated HTTP check either, so this was not claimed as tested. Verification was static: full manual re-read of the rewritten JSX for anchor-id consistency (caught the `#materials`/`#parts` bug above), prop-shape consistency across all three new `WorkflowActions` call sites, and confirmation that every pre-existing form's hidden inputs/`action=`/required-field attributes are unchanged from before the split.

No approval or closure workflow changed. Materials logic, work session logic, and assignment save logic untouched. Job Cards/Materials Requests/Offline Inventory Control names unchanged. No deployment performed.

## Phase JobCardActionClarityFix-01 — RECAFCO MMS Job Card Action Clarity Fix — COMPLETE

Goal: the Job Cards list showed an Assign button even when a Job Card already had Internal Team workers assigned, and the quick-view Materials section always said "Receive Materials" even when the required material was already sitting in Offline Inventory and should be issued instead. Fix both so Data Entry always sees the one correct action.

**New shared primitive:** `summarizeMaterialAvailability(fulfillment)` added to `lib/work-orders/material-fulfillment.ts` — a pure function reducing an array of `MaterialFulfillment` rows (already computed by the existing `getMaterialFulfillmentForWorkOrder`, Unit 6) to one Job-Card-level verdict: `"none"` (no Required Materials rows to reason about — legacy fallback), `"fulfilled"`, `"issuable"` (every outstanding row fully covered by current Offline Inventory balance), `"shortage"` (nothing available for any outstanding row), or `"partial"` (mixed). This one function now drives every "Issue vs Receive" decision across both surfaces touched by this fix, instead of each surface guessing independently.

**Task 1 — Job Cards list Action button (`app/(dashboard)/maintenance/work-orders/page.tsx`):** `getRowActLabel()` gained a `hasAssignment` parameter; the Approved/Partially Issued/Materials Issued branch now returns `"Track Work"` when `hasAssignment` (internal roster count > 0 OR `work_order_assignments.length > 0` — computed per-row from the exact same data the Assignment column already reads, so the two can never disagree) instead of always `"Assign"`. The Action-column render site now special-cases `actLabel === "Track Work"` with its own direct `Link` to `/maintenance/work-orders/{id}#work-time-tracking` (a real navigation, not the same-page quick-view popup every other row action opens — deliberately not given `scroll={false}`).

**Task 2 — quick-view "Assign Work" (`components/work-orders/repair-order-quick-view.tsx`):** `showAssign` (the inline `AssignmentFormModal` trigger, distinct from the link-only `showAssignWorkers`/`showTrackWork` pair Unit 8B already added correctly) was missing a `!hasAnyAssignment` check — it could render next to a Job Card that already had a full Internal Team roster. `hasAnyAssignment`'s declaration was moved earlier in the component (it was previously computed after `showAssign`, which would have been a temporal-dead-zone reference error) and `showAssign` now requires it to be false. Only one of "Assign Work"/"Track Work" ever shows now.

**Task 3 — `QuickViewData.materialsAvailability` (new optional field) + Materials action buttons:** wired into all three server pages that build a `previewWO`-based `QuickViewData` — `work-orders/page.tsx`, `dashboard/page.tsx`, and `store/parts-requests/page.tsx` — each now also calls `getMaterialFulfillmentForWorkOrder(prisma, previewId)` (gated behind the single previewed id exactly like the existing `previewWO` query itself, so this is one extra per-popup-open read, never a per-list-row query) and passes `summarizeMaterialAvailability(...)` through. In the popup: `hasRequiredMaterialsTracking = materialsAvailability !== "none"` switches the Materials section from the old blanket "Receive Materials" shortcut to four new states — `"issuable"` → primary "Issue Material" button (links to the Job Card detail page's Materials section, `#parts`, since the popup doesn't have per-material balance-key granularity to issue directly); `"shortage"` → "Receive Materials" (links to the active Materials Request's Receive panel, or the Materials section if none exists yet); `"partial"` → both buttons, relabeled "Issue Available" / "Receive Shortage"; `"fulfilled"` → a static green "Materials Completed" label, no button. Job Cards with no Required Materials rows (`materialsAvailability` "none"/undefined — created before that feature existed) keep the exact old shortcut behavior, untouched. The section heading was also updated to reflect availability instead of Materials-Request receipt status once tracking applies, since the two can legitimately disagree (a request can be "Received" into the store while nothing's been issued to this specific Job Card yet).

**Task 4 — quick-view Next Action ladder:** extended with the task's exact wording, in priority order after the existing Closed/Closure-Requested terminal checks: `shortage` → "Materials are pending. Receive materials when they arrive."; `partial` → "Some materials are available. Issue available stock and receive shortage later."; assignment exists + `issuable` → "Materials are available. Issue materials to this Job Card."; then the pre-existing open-Materials-Request-count check (now scoped to `!hasRequiredMaterialsTracking` only, so it doesn't double-fire for Job Cards the new availability logic already covered); then the pre-existing no-assignment/active-session checks; then a new case — assignment exists and materials `fulfilled` (or no tracking at all) → "Workers are assigned. Start work tracking." — before falling through to the original generic "Open Work Tracking to start work." fallback.

**Task 5 — full Job Card detail consistency (`app/(dashboard)/maintenance/work-orders/[id]/page.tsx`):** the per-row Materials table Action column (built in Unit 8C) already prioritized Issue over Receive correctly and needed no change. The page-level Next Action panel's materials branch (also Unit 8C) did not — it always led with "Receive Materials" whenever anything was outstanding, regardless of whether stock was actually sitting in Offline Inventory ready to issue. Rewritten to call the same `summarizeMaterialAvailability(materialFulfillment)` and use the identical partial/issuable/shortage precedence and message strings as the quick-view (Task 4), so the two surfaces never disagree. The Closure panel's readiness reason list was left untouched — those are still-accurate blocking reasons ("Required materials have not been fully issued yet.") independent of whether the shortfall happens to be currently issuable.

**Task 6 — backend unchanged confirmation:** no migration, no schema change, no server action touched. `summarizeMaterialAvailability` is a pure read of the exact same `MaterialFulfillment` rows Unit 6's `getMaterialFulfillmentForWorkOrder` already computes from `work_order_required_parts` + `offline_inventory_movements` — no new stock deduction anywhere, no Job-Card-creation-time inventory change, no Materials Request status wording changed, Offline Inventory Control not renamed, approval/closure workflow (`lib/workflows/status-rules.ts`, the three closure guards) not touched, work session calculation (`lib/work-orders/work-session-totals.ts`) not touched.

**Task 7 — testing:** a disposable script (`verify-job-card-action-clarity-fix.mjs`, deleted after use) covered all 6 scenarios from the spec — (1) 1 internal worker assigned → `"Track Work"`; (2) no worker assigned → `"Assign Workers"` (plus a no-permission control case); (3) required material fully available → `"issuable"`; (4) not available → `"shortage"`; (5) partially available → `"partial"`; (6) fully issued → `"fulfilled"`, plus confirming `"none"` for a Job Card with zero Required Materials rows. It also cross-checked the task's exact required message/button strings are present byte-identical in both the detail page and quick-view source, by reading both files directly (same technique the Unit 8 verify script used for its duplicate-request error string). Finally, one real DB round trip — inside a transaction rolled back at the end, same pattern as every prior `verify-*.mjs` script — created a real `work_orders` row + `work_order_required_parts` row, then walked it through no-stock (`shortage`) → received-but-not-issued (`issuable`) → issued (`fulfilled`) using real `offline_inventory_movements` rows, confirming the actual DB read path (not just the pure function in isolation). All 24 checks passed; a follow-up query confirmed zero leftover `TMP/ACTION-CLARITY/...` rows after rollback.

## Phase PopupFeedbackStandardizationUnit8D-01 — Popup and Feedback Design Standardization Unit 8D — COMPLETE

Goal: one consistent feedback design system across two formats — a Workflow Success Modal for major workflow actions needing next-step guidance, and a Quick Feedback Toast for simple confirmations — instead of the mix of a full-screen backdrop-blurred "toast" and several independently hand-rolled success modals the app had converged on. UI/feedback-presentation unit only; no schema, no workflow/materials/assignment/work-session logic changed.

**New standard doc:** `context/feedback-standard.md` — the full usage rules table (which format for which action), the two trigger mechanisms for the toast, the already-consistent inline-field-error pattern (documented, not changed), and the audit findings below.

**Task 2 — `components/ui/workflow-success-modal.tsx` (new):** shared shell — backdrop, centered dialog, close X, icon circle (`iconVariant: success|warning|info`), centered title/description, optional `warnings` (amber inline notices), optional `summaryItems` (label/value pairs, value is any ReactNode so a row can hold a `<StatusBadge/>` or an item list), optional `statusLabel`, optional `nextStepTitle`/`nextStepDescription` (the boxed red "Next Recommended Step" panel), optional `progressSteps` (stage pill row), `primaryAction`/`secondaryActions` (`{kind:"link"|"button"|"form"}` — `"form"` covers the one case, Start Job Card on a just-created Draft, where the primary action is a real server-action submit, not a navigation), and a shared `closeAction` wired to the backdrop click, X, Esc, and the trailing text "Close" button. Rendered conditionally by the host page, same convention as every other modal in this codebase — no `open` prop.

**Task 3 — applied to all 7 existing workflow success screens:** `JobCardCreatedModal`, `JobCardSubmittedModal`, `JobCardClosedModal`, `JobCardOpenedModal`, `CorrectionRequestSentModal`, `MaterialsRequestCreatedModal`, `MaterialsReceivedModal` were all already independently converged on the same hand-rolled markup (backdrop, dialog, icon circle, summary card, footer buttons) — refactored each into a thin wrapper around `WorkflowSuccessModal`, keeping every external prop/call site byte-identical (zero changes needed anywhere these are invoked). This also fixed the one real visual drift found: `JobCardOpenedModal`/`CorrectionRequestSentModal`/the two Materials modals used a plain "**Next:** ..." inline line while `JobCardCreatedModal`/`JobCardSubmittedModal` used the boxed "Next Recommended Step" panel — all 7 now use the boxed panel.

**Task 4 — wording:** the old one-size-fits-all "Assign work, update details, or request closure once work is done." next-step line (already retired everywhere by earlier units per `context/progress-tracker.md`'s own history) stays retired — confirmed no modal reintroduced it. Every modal's next-step text is still the case-specific guidance each earlier unit already wrote (Task 3's refactor didn't touch wording, only markup).

**Task 5 — `components/ui/action-toast.tsx` (redesigned):** previously a full-screen `bg-black/20 backdrop-blur` overlay with a centered ~480px card — functionally a second modal system, not a toast (the exact inconsistency this unit fixes; `components/notifications/notification-toast-center.tsx` already had a long-standing comment calling this out explicitly). Redesigned to a compact card (smaller icon circle, smaller type, tighter padding), no backdrop, anchored bottom-right on `sm:` screens and above the fixed mobile bottom nav bar (`bottom-[calc(5.5rem+env(safe-area-inset-bottom))]`) below that — non-blocking, `pointer-events-none` container with `pointer-events-auto` cards. Kept the existing top-accent-line + auto-dismiss progress strip (a nice touch worth keeping) and the existing tone system (success/error/warning/info, same icon shapes `WorkflowSuccessModal` uses). Positioned opposite corner from `NotificationToastCenter` (top-right, a different kind of feedback — pushed from elsewhere, not this tab's own action) so the two never overlap.

**New trigger mechanism (Task 6 groundwork):** `dispatchActionToast(message)` + `ACTION_TOAST_EVENT` added to `lib/action-messages.ts` — dispatches a `CustomEvent` on `window` that `<ActionToast/>` (mounted once, globally) also listens for, alongside its existing `?success=`/`?error=` URL-param path. This was needed because several quick actions use `useActionState` forms that don't redirect/navigate on success, so the URL-param mechanism alone couldn't reach them.

**Task 6 — applied to quick actions that previously gave *no* success feedback at all** (silent re-render on success, only an inline red error on failure — confirmed by reading each component before editing):
- `worker-session-row.tsx`: Start/Pause/Stop/Resume Work now call `dispatchActionToast` with "Work Session Started"/"Paused"/"Stopped".
- `manual-time-entry-modal.tsx`: "Manual Time Entry Saved".
- `session-history-modal.tsx`: Edit → "Session Updated"; Cancel → "Session Cancelled" (`warning` tone, since it's a correction/undo of recorded work).
- `worker-profile-form-modal.tsx`: "Worker Profile Saved".
- `internal-team-roster-form.tsx`: "Assignment Updated" (a quick edit — doesn't change the Job Card's workflow status, unlike starting/closing it, so toast not modal, per the usage rules).
- `assignTechniciansAction` (`app/actions/workflow.ts`, the legacy technician/Freelancer/Company assignment path): redirect target gained `?success=assignment-updated`; new `SUCCESS_MAP` entry added.
- `uploadWorkOrderFileAction` (`app/actions/files.ts`): redirect target gained `?success=file-uploaded` via a new small `withSuccessParam()` helper that safely inserts the query param before any existing `#hash` (the Attachments section's `return_to` carries `#attachments`); new `SUCCESS_MAP` entry added.
- "Note Saved" was added to `SUCCESS_MAP` per the usage-rules table but **not wired to anything** — grepped the codebase and confirmed no live "save a technician note" action currently exists to attach it to (the feature appears retired; only historical notes are displayed). Documented as prepared-but-unused rather than force-attached to something that doesn't exist.

**Task 7 — error/warning consistency:**
- Confirmation-for-destructive-actions rule spot-checked, not rebuilt: Delete User already goes through a dedicated `DeleteUserDialog`; Cancel Work Session already requires typing a reason and a distinct "Confirm Cancel Session" click (`session-history-modal.tsx`) — both already satisfy the rule, nothing to change.
- Error toast for recoverable errors: `ERROR_MAP` in `lib/action-messages.ts` gained entries for every `?error=<code>` value found in `app/actions/*.ts` that had none — `no-file`/`file-upload-failed`/`file-metadata-failed`/`upload-permission`/`delete-permission` (files.ts), `invalid-name`/`name-exists`/`invalid-parent`/`invalid-id`/`has-active-children` (asset-categories.ts), `no-items`/`invalid-issued-quantity` (phase4.ts), `cannot-force-own-password-change`/`cannot-delete-self`/`cannot-delete-last-admin`/`has-linked-records` (user-access.ts) — these previously fell through to a bare "Error: \<raw-code\>" toast.
- The generic unmapped-error fallback's title changed from "Error" to "Action could not be completed" (matches the wording the Job Card detail page's own inline error banner already used), so an error that reaches the fallback still reads naturally instead of a dead-end "Error".
- "Material not enough stock" and Job Card closure-blocked errors (materials pending / active work session) already flow through the existing `AppError`/`?error=` mechanisms — confirmed, not changed.

**Task 8 — audit findings (full list in `context/feedback-standard.md`'s "Found and fixed" section):** the toast/modal drift above (fixed), the missing `ERROR_MAP` entries (fixed), the missing quick-action success feedback (fixed). One finding was **not** fixed, by design: the Job Card detail page's own inline error banner (`errorMessage`/`humanizeError()`) reads the same `?error=` param the global toast also reads, so a workflow error can show twice on that one page (banner + toast) — the safe fix would require either removing that page's banner (risking loss of its one special case, the "Open Existing Materials Request" link for the duplicate-request error) or teaching the global toast to suppress itself per-page; neither is a small change, so it's documented as a known follow-up rather than rewritten under this unit's time budget. No `window.alert`/`window.confirm`/bare `alert()`/`confirm()` calls were found anywhere in the codebase (grepped `*.tsx`) — nothing to fix there.

**Task 9 — accessibility:** `WorkflowSuccessModal` — focus moves to the first interactive element in the footer on open, `Escape` closes, visible X button, `role="dialog"`/`aria-modal`/`aria-labelledby`, body-scroll-locked while open (all carried over unchanged from the 7 original modals, now centralized in one place instead of copy-pasted 7 times). `ActionToast` — `role`/`aria-live` now vary by tone (`status`/`polite` for success and info, `alert`/`assertive` for error and warning — previously every tone used `assertive` unconditionally), never moves focus, always has a manual close button.

**Task 10 — responsive:** modal buttons are `flex-col` (stacked, full-width) by default and become `sm:flex-row` once there's room; the dialog itself is capped `max-h-[90vh]` with internal scroll so it never overflows a short mobile viewport. Toast is capped `max-w-[380px]`, centered and full-width-minus-padding below `sm:`, positioned above the fixed mobile bottom nav bar rather than under it.

**Task 11 — backend/data unchanged confirmation:** no migration, no Prisma schema change. No server action's actual business logic changed — `assignTechniciansAction`/`uploadWorkOrderFileAction` only had their redirect target's query string extended (a `?success=` code appended), the underlying `assignTechnicians()`/`uploadPrivateFile()` calls and everything they do are untouched. `lib/action-messages.ts` changes are additive (new map entries, one new exported function) — `resolveToastMessage()`'s existing behavior for every already-mapped code is unchanged; only the previously-generic fallback's title text changed. No workflow transition, materials calculation, or work-session duration/rate calculation touched anywhere.

**Task 12 — manual test coverage:** could not be run live — no browser-automation tool is available in this environment and no login credentials were available to script an authenticated check (same limitation noted in Unit 8C's report). Verified statically instead: `npm run build` succeeds (confirms every modal/toast call site's props still type-check against the new shared components — a prop mismatch would have failed the build), `npm run lint`/`typecheck` clean, and a full manual re-read of every edited file confirming the exact button labels/hrefs/hidden-field names the tests describe (e.g. "Continue This Job Card", `?success=assignment-updated`, `#attachments` hash preserved through `withSuccessParam()`) are present and unchanged from before.

**Validation:** `npm run db:check`, `lint`, `typecheck`, and `build` all pass clean. No migration.
