## Phase DailyActivityUnit9-01 — Daily Activity / Active Job Cards Work Tracking Unit 9 — COMPLETE

Goal: a dedicated, lightweight page (`/maintenance/daily-activity`) where Data Entry/Manager can monitor every active Job Card — assignment, live work-session status, today's/total labor hours, materials status, closure readiness — from one screen, without replacing the full Job Card detail page or its own Work Time Tracking section.

**New files:** `app/(dashboard)/maintenance/daily-activity/page.tsx`, `components/work-orders/daily-activity-card.tsx`. **Extended (additive only):** `lib/work-orders/material-fulfillment.ts` (new `getMaterialFulfillmentForWorkOrders` bulk export), `lib/work-orders/work-session-totals.ts` (new `getWorkOrderLaborSummariesBulk` bulk export + two new optional fields on `WorkerLaborRow`), `components/work-orders/worker-session-row.tsx` (new optional `todayHours` prop), `components/layout/app-layout.tsx` (nav entry).

**Task 1 — scope:** `where` clause is `visibilityFilter AND deleted_at IS NULL AND status != 'Closed' AND (status IN ACTIVE_JOB_CARD_STATUSES OR id IN <ids with an Active work session>)`. `ACTIVE_JOB_CARD_STATUSES` is the existing exported constant from `lib/work-orders/simplified-status.ts` (Approved/Waiting Materials/Partially Issued/Materials Issued/Assigned/In Progress) — reused, not re-derived. The `id IN <active-session ids>` branch is the Task 1 exception: a non-Closed Job Card outside the normal bucket (e.g. a legacy/edge status) still appears, flagged with an amber "Active work session" warning badge on its card, if a session is currently running — active work is never silently hidden. Draft/Closure Requested/Closed are excluded by construction (none of them are in `ACTIVE_JOB_CARD_STATUSES`, and Closed is hard-excluded even from the exception path).

**Task 2 — summary cards:** Active Job Cards (real `count()`, not capped by the page's 50-row display limit, so this one number stays accurate even when the list itself is truncated), Workers Working Now, Paused Workers, Total Labor Hours Today, Labor Cost Today (cost-gated), Jobs Ready for Closure (the optional 6th card) — all computed as a fast in-memory reduce over the already-loaded/bulk-computed batch, no extra queries.

**Task 3 — filters:** search (`q`) is a real Prisma `where` OR-clause across Job Card #, complaint/description, asset name/code/plate number, and a nested relation filter on the active worker roster's name — all DB-level, scales with an index, not an in-memory scan. Work Team (`team`) is also DB-level (`worker_type` equals). Status quick-filter (Working Now/Paused/Not Started/Materials Pending/Ready for Closure) and the Materials filter (Pending/Ready to Issue/Completed/No Materials) are applied in-memory after the bulk compute, since both depend on derived (not stored-column) state — documented in code as a deliberate scoping decision, consistent with the page's own 50-row cap.

**Task 4 — Job Card activity card (`DailyActivityJobCard`):** header (number/status badge/warning badge/asset/issue/created/work team) + up to 4 primary actions (Open Job Card always; the materials action — dynamic label per Task 8; Assign Workers only when unassigned and permitted; Request Closure only when ready and permitted) + the 4 operational chips (Assignment/Materials/Work Time/Closure — reuses the exact same 4-bucket Materials-chip formula and Work-Time-chip formula the Job Card detail page uses post-Unit-8C.2, so a card never reads differently between the two pages).

**Task 5/6/7 — worker rows:** each internal worker renders via the existing `WorkerSessionRow` component from Unit 8/8C.2 — the *same* component, same Start/Pause/Resume/Stop/Add Manual Entry/View Sessions forms, same individual `useActionState` per row (confirmed: starting one worker's form has no effect on any other row — each is its own `<form>` with its own state). Nothing about session start/pause/resume/stop logic was reimplemented for this page. Live timer reuses `components/work-orders/live-timer.tsx` from Unit 8C.2 unchanged, ticking client-side from the session's `started_at` — no per-second DB write, backend stays the source of truth for `duration_minutes`/`calculated_amount` (computed only at Pause/Stop, exactly as Unit 8 built it). Added one new optional `todayHours` prop/field so this page can also show "Today's worked time" per worker without touching the Job Card detail page's existing display (that call site simply doesn't pass/read it).

**Task 8 — materials:** the card's single materials action button (kept to one button, per Task 4's "not too many buttons") uses `getMaterialFulfillmentForWorkOrders` + `summarizeMaterialAvailability` (both already existing per-Job-Card helpers from Unit 6/the Job Card Action Clarity Fix, now with a bulk sibling) — label switches between "Issue Material" (gated by the same `canManageOfflineInventory` check the detail page's own Issue action uses), "Receive Materials", "View Materials", and "Materials Completed", matching Task 8's exact rule set. No inventory is deducted anywhere on this page — every button navigates to the real action surface (detail page's Materials section or the Materials Request itself); nothing here writes to `offline_inventory_movements`.

**Task 9 — closure readiness:** mirrors (read-only, never calls) the exact three signals Task 9 names — no pending Materials Request (`parts_requests` status != "Issued"), required materials fully issued (`anyMaterialsIncomplete` on the bulk fulfillment result), no active work session (`laborSummary.has_active_session`) — same three backend guards the Job Card detail page's Closure panel already mirrors. Completion-note requirement is deliberately left to the Job Card itself (Task 9's own note: "handled on request") — this page's "Request Closure" button links to `#closure-panel` on the detail page rather than embedding a duplicate note-entry form for up to 50 cards at once.

**Task 10 — realtime:** `<RealtimeRefresh watch={["job_card.", "work_order.", "materials_request.", "offline_inventory.", "material_ledger."]} />` plus the existing `<AutoRefresh intervalMs={20000} />` fallback poll — the exact watch list Task 10 specifies. Confirmed (by reading `lib/realtime/events.ts` and `lib/backend/work-orders/work-sessions.ts`) that every event Start/Pause/Stop/manual-entry/edit already emits (`job_card.work_started`/`work_paused`/`work_stopped`/`work_time_updated`) already carries the `job_card.` prefix — no backend/event changes needed. Uses the single shared `RealtimeConnectionProvider` EventSource already wrapping the whole app layout (Unit 2's SSE Connection Consolidation) — no new connection.

**Task 11 — performance:** the lean `work_orders` select carries no attachments, no audit logs, no full parts-request-item history, no full session history — just identity fields, `assets`/`departments` (select-scoped), `work_order_assignments` (id only, presence check), and `parts_requests` (id+status only). Materials and labor data both come from the two new *bulk* helpers (one groupBy pair total for materials across every Job Card on the page, one 2-query pair total for sessions across every Job Card on the page) instead of looping the existing single-Job-Card helpers — avoiding the N+1 that would otherwise be 2–4 queries × up to 50 Job Cards. Page capped at the task's specified "latest 50", ordered by `updated_at desc`; a footer note tells the user how many more exist beyond the cap so search/filters are the documented way to narrow further (no pagination UI built yet, per the task's own "limit ... or use show more" — the limit alone was judged sufficient for this unit).

**Task 12 — permissions:** `canViewCosts` (existing cost-visibility guard) gates the Labor Cost Today card and every `WorkerSessionRow`'s cost display exactly as the detail page already does — hourly rate/cost never renders for a viewer without that grant. `canManageSessions` mirrors the detail page's own gate (`work_orders.assign` or Manager/Super Admin, and never on a Closed Job Card — moot here since Closed is excluded from this page's scope entirely, but kept for defense-in-depth). `canEditAssignment`/`canRequestClosureRole` are page-level mirrors of the same role checks `workflow-actions.tsx` and the Job Card detail page already use (documented as intentionally slightly broader than the exact per-status nuance, since these only gate whether a *navigation* button is offered — the real mutation is still enforced server-side on the destination page regardless of what this list shows).

**Task 13 — empty states:** "No active Job Cards to track." when the whole page is empty; a distinct "No Job Cards match the current filters" message when filters narrowed an otherwise non-empty result to zero; "No workers assigned yet." + "Assign Workers" button per card with no roster; `WorkerSessionRow`'s own existing "Not Started" state (Unit 8) covers "work not started yet" per worker — not re-implemented.

**Task 14 — navigation:** "Daily Activity" added to the sidebar (and, automatically, the mobile drawer — it's derived from the same `visibleGroups` list) for every role that already shows "Job Cards": Super Admin, Maintenance Manager, Maintenance Engineer, Viewer/Auditor, and Maintenance Data Entry — right after the "Job Cards" entry in each, before "Materials Requests". Uses the `Activity` icon, already registered in `navIcons` (no new icon import needed). Technician and Store Keeper nav arrays untouched (Technician has its own mobile-first "My Jobs" list; Store Keeper has no Job Card visibility) — no existing nav entry renamed or removed anywhere.

**Task 15 — full Job Card detail page unchanged:** confirmed no edits to `app/(dashboard)/maintenance/work-orders/[id]/page.tsx` itself in this unit — the only shared files touched are the two lib helpers (additive exports) and `WorkerSessionRow` (one new optional prop, default-unused by the detail page's existing call site). The detail page's Work Time Tracking section, attachments, QR, print, and full activity timeline are all exactly as Unit 8C.2 left them.

**Task 16 — manual browser tests:** could not be run live — no browser-automation tool is available in this environment and no login credentials were available to script an authenticated check (same limitation noted in every prior unit's report). Verified statically instead: successful production build (registers `/maintenance/daily-activity` as a real route and would fail on any prop/type mismatch across the new/edited components), clean lint/typecheck, and a full manual trace of the data flow confirming — by reading the code, not by clicking — that each `WorkerSessionRow` on this page is an independent `<form>`/`useActionState` pair (so starting one worker cannot start another), that the live timer reads `active_session_started_at` (recomputed correctly from the DB value on every fresh page load, satisfying "on refresh, calculate elapsed from started_at"), and that Pause/Resume/Stop dispatch the exact same `pauseWorkSessionAction`/`startWorkSessionAction`/`stopWorkSessionAction` server actions Unit 8 built (no new session-transition logic written).

**Validation:** `npm run db:check`, `lint`, `typecheck`, and `build` all pass clean. No migration — every schema table/column this unit reads already existed.

No approval or closure workflow changed. No materials/assignment/work-session calculation logic changed. Job Cards page, Technician page, and every existing nav entry/module name unchanged. No deployment performed.

## Phase DailyActivityUiUxUnit9B-01 — Daily Activity Page UI/UX Simplification Unit 9B — COMPLETE

Goal: the Daily Activity page (Unit 9) worked but still asked Data Entry to scan too much text to answer "what needs action right now." Redesign it into a simple operational monitoring/control screen — clearer summary cards, priority-sorted cards, one obvious Next Action per Job Card, calmer worker rows — with zero backend/workflow/materials/assignment/work-session-calculation changes.

**Files changed:** `app/(dashboard)/maintenance/daily-activity/page.tsx`, `components/work-orders/daily-activity-card.tsx`, `components/work-orders/worker-session-row.tsx` (shared with the Job Card detail page — see Task 7 note below). `live-timer.tsx` untouched (already fit, just given a bigger `className` override where it's rendered now).

**Task 1 — header:** description text updated to the task's exact wording ("Monitor active Job Cards, workers, materials, and closure readiness."). The helper line ("Use this page for daily work control. Open the Job Card for full details.") is a small `<p>` in the page body just under `PageHeader`, not a new `PageHeader` prop — keeps the header itself exactly as compact as before and leaves every other page using `PageHeader` untouched.

**Task 2 — summary cards:** Active Job Cards (blue), Workers Working Now (green), Paused Workers (amber), Total Labor Hours Today (blue), Jobs Ready for Closure (green), Labor Cost Today (cost-gated, neutral). Three of them (Working Now/Paused/Ready for Closure) plus Active Job Cards are now real links into the matching quick filter — clicking preserves whatever search/team/materials filter is already active and only changes `status`; "Active Job Cards" resets `status` back to "All Active." The active one gets a red ring so it's clear which filter is currently applied.

**Task 3 — priority sort/label:** one `priorityBucket` computed per card (`working > paused > materials > closure > assigned-idle > unassigned`, matching the task's numbered order exactly), used both to sort the list (`Array.prototype.sort`, stable — ties keep the existing `updated_at desc` order) and to print one small priority `StatusBadge` on the card ("Working Now"/"Paused"/"Materials Pending"/"Ready for Closure"/"Not Started"/"Needs Assignment"). Pure derivation from data already loaded in Unit 9 — no new query, no new backend logic.

**Task 4 — filters:** the status `<select>` is gone, replaced by six pill `FilterChip` links (All Active/Working Now/Paused/Materials Pending/Ready for Closure/Not Started) — each is instant navigation, no Apply step, since a status filter change is just a link with a different `?status=`. Work Team and Materials stay as dropdowns inside a small form (they're real `where`-clause/derived-value filters alongside free-text search, which does need a submit) — the button is now labeled "Search" instead of the previous generic "Apply" so it's clear what it does. "Reset Filters" is now always visible (previously conditional), visually dimmed/non-interactive when there's nothing to reset.

**Task 5/6 — card redesign + Next Action:** restructured into the task's exact layout — top row (identity left, one red primary-action button right) → one "Next: …" sentence (always shown, even when there's no button) → operational chips → material alert / closure reason line → worker rows → a footer row of neutral (white/bordered, never red) secondary actions (Open Job Card, materials link, Assign Workers, Request Closure). `nextAction` is computed server-side per card in the task's own priority order (materials pending → materials ready/partial → no assignment → assigned-but-idle → working → paused → closure-ready → closure-requested) and reused for both the top-row button and to suppress the matching footer button so the same action never appears twice on one card ("do not show conflicting actions"). "Working"/"Paused" states intentionally render no card-level button at all — the real action is a specific worker's own row below, which a card-level button can't disambiguate among multiple workers.

**Task 7 — worker rows:** restructured into left (name/role/status badge) / middle (Today, Total, and — only while Active — a live timer sized up to `text-xl font-black`, "large enough to read") / right (buttons) using a responsive flex row that stacks to a column below `sm:`. Button sets are now exactly per-status per the task's table: Not Started → Start only; Working → Pause (new amber-outline style, distinct from both the green "go" and red "stop" colors) + Stop (red); Paused → Resume + View Sessions (no Add Manual Entry while a session is literally paused); Completed → Resume Work + Add Manual Entry + View Sessions. **Shared-component note:** `WorkerSessionRow` is the same component the Job Card detail page's Work Time Tracking section uses (Unit 8/8C.2) — this button-set and layout change applies there too, which is an intentional, in-scope side effect (Task 7 lists this file as a "related component," and one consistent, clearer worker-row experience across both pages is a feature, not drift). No session start/pause/resume/stop logic changed anywhere — only which buttons render for which status, and how the row is laid out.

**Task 8 — multiple-worker clarity:** "Worker timers are tracked individually." now renders once per page (above the whole card list, only when at least one visible card has more than one worker) instead of being considered per-card — avoids repeating the same sentence on every multi-worker card.

**Task 9 — materials clarity:** materials chip is now a 5-state scale scoped to this page (No Materials/Materials Pending/Ready to Issue/Partially Available/Materials Completed) — a deliberate, task-directed divergence from the Job Card detail page's existing 4-state chip (documented in code so it doesn't read as an accidental inconsistency). Added the one-line material alert ("Materials are pending." / "Material is available to issue." / "Some materials are available; shortage remains.") shown only when materials need attention. The single materials action button never offers "Receive Materials" once stock is issuable — Ready to Issue and Partially Available both resolve to "Issue Material" (gated by the same `canManageOfflineInventory` check the detail page's own Issue action uses).

**Task 10 — closure clarity:** closure chip now matches the Job Card detail page's full 4-state scale (Not Ready/Ready/Requested/Closed) instead of Unit 9's 2-state version. While Not Ready, a brief reason line lists exactly the three short phrases the task specifies ("Materials pending" / "Required materials not fully issued" / "Active work session running") — no full closure form duplicated here; Request Closure still links to the Job Card's own `#closure-panel`.

**Task 12 — visual noise:** at most one red button per card now (down from up to three in Unit 9); every secondary action is neutral (white/bordered); the multi-worker helper text collapsed from per-card to page-level; duplicate action buttons (e.g. "Assign Workers" appearing both as the primary action and again in the footer) are suppressed via the same `nextAction` comparison used for Task 6.

**Task 13 — responsive:** card top row stacks to a column below `sm:` (button moves under the identity block instead of squeezing beside it); worker rows stack their three sections vertically below `sm:`; filter chips/dropdowns wrap via `flex-wrap`; summary cards already used a `grid-cols-2` → `lg:grid-cols-3` → `xl:grid-cols-6` responsive grid from Unit 9, unchanged.

**Task 14/15 — realtime and backend unchanged:** `RealtimeRefresh`'s watch list and `AutoRefresh`'s poll interval are byte-for-byte unchanged from Unit 9 — not touched in this unit. No migration, no server action changed, no calculation logic (materials fulfillment, work session duration/cost, assignment save, closure guards) changed anywhere — every edit in this unit is presentation logic (chip labels/tones, sort order, which button renders where) computed from data Unit 9 already loaded.

**Task 16 — manual browser tests:** could not be run live — no browser-automation tool is available in this environment and no login credentials were available to script an authenticated check (same limitation noted in every prior unit's report). Verified statically: successful production build (would fail on any prop/type mismatch between the page and the two redesigned components), clean lint/typecheck, and a full manual re-read confirming each worker's `SessionActionForm` remains its own independent `<form>`/`useActionState` pair (starting one still cannot start/affect another), that the live timer still reads `active_session_started_at` fresh on every page load, and that Pause/Resume/Stop still dispatch the exact same Unit 8 server actions with no new transition logic.

**Validation:** `npm run db:check`, `lint`, `typecheck`, and `build` all pass clean. No migration.

No approval or closure workflow changed. No materials/assignment/work-session calculation logic changed. Job Cards page, Job Card detail page's Work Time Tracking section, and every existing route/nav entry unchanged (only the shared `WorkerSessionRow` component's button layout changed, benefiting both pages identically — see Task 7). No deployment performed.

## Phase DailyActivityCompactBoardUnit9C-01 — Daily Activity Compact Control Board Unit 9C — COMPLETE

Goal: Unit 9B's Daily Activity page was clearer but still a long, fully-repeated card list — every one of up to 50 Job Cards rendered its own full worker-control block, forcing heavy scrolling. Redesign into a compact split-screen control board (compact header/summary/filters at top, a short scannable list on the left, one selected Job Card's full control panel on the right) so Data Entry can monitor and act on active Job Cards with far less scrolling, with zero backend/workflow/materials/assignment/work-session-calculation changes.

**Files changed:** `app/(dashboard)/maintenance/daily-activity/page.tsx`, `components/work-orders/daily-activity-card.tsx` (split into `DailyActivityListRow` + `DailyActivitySelectedPanel`, replacing the old single `DailyActivityJobCard`), and one new file `components/work-orders/daily-activity-board.tsx` (client component owning selection state). `worker-session-row.tsx` untouched — reused as-is, just rendered in one place now instead of once per card.

**Task 1 — compact header:** replaced this page's use of the shared `<PageHeader/>` with a page-local header block (same red left-accent-bar language, `PageBreadcrumb` kept) using tighter padding (`py-2.5` vs `py-4/py-6`) and smaller type (`text-lg/xl` vs `text-2xl/3xl`). Title ("Daily Activity") and subtitle ("Monitor active Job Cards, workers, materials, and closure readiness.") kept exactly as specified, with Unit 9B's helper sentence folded into the same line instead of a separate paragraph. `PageHeader` itself was not touched — every other page using it is unaffected.

**Task 2 — compact summary cards:** `SummaryCard`/`SummaryCardLink` rebuilt from a stacked (icon block, then label, then value, `p-4`) layout to a horizontal one (icon left, label+value stacked right, `px-2.5 py-2`) — noticeably shorter. Same five cards (Active Job Cards, Working Now, Paused, Labor Hours Today, Ready for Closure) plus the cost-gated Labor Cost Today card; all click-to-filter behavior from Unit 9B (active-filter red ring, preserves other filters) kept unchanged.

**Task 3 — compact filters:** collapsed from two stacked rows (a chips row, then a separate form row) into one wrapping flex row — six `FilterChip`s, then the search input/Work Team/Materials dropdowns/submit/Reset all inline. The submit button is now an icon-only square button (magnifying glass, `aria-label="Search"`) instead of a labeled "Search" button, saving width for the search input, which keeps `flex-1 min-w-[200px]` so it never gets squeezed to unusable width.

**Task 4/7 — split layout:** the long `sorted.map(...)` card list is gone. `page.tsx` now builds one serializable `DailyActivityCardData[]` (`boardCards` — one object per Job Card, same fields Unit 9B already computed, plus a new `materialsTotals` required/issued/remaining aggregate and `detailHref`) and hands it to the new client `DailyActivityBoard`. That component renders a `grid-cols-[35%_65%]` split at `lg:` and up: a compact left list and one right-side control panel for whichever Job Card is selected. Crucially, only the selected card's panel renders `WorkerSessionRow` controls — every other card in the list is just a short identity/chip row with no worker controls at all. This is the actual fix for the scrolling problem: previously up to 50 full worker-control blocks could render at once; now at most one does.

**Task 5 — left list row design:** `DailyActivityListRow` shows Job Card #, asset/plate label, a one-line issue clamp, and three small `MiniChip`s (Materials/Work status/Assignment — smaller than the shared `StatusBadge` so they fit a short row). A left accent bar (`border-l-4`) colors by priority bucket: red for Materials Pending, amber for Paused, green for Working/Ready for Closure, neutral gray otherwise (Not Started/Needs Assignment) — matching the task's red/amber-blocked, green-working/ready, neutral-not-started rule. Clicking a row calls the board's `onSelect`; the selected row gets a red ring plus a tinted background. Default selection is the first row in the already priority-sorted list (Unit 9B's sort order, untouched).

**Task 6 — right control panel:** `DailyActivitySelectedPanel` shows: a header (Job Card #, status badge, unusual-session badge, issue, asset, created date, work team); the one Next Action message plus primary button (same `nextAction` computation from Unit 9B — unchanged priority order — with a neutral "Open Job Card" fallback button when there is no specific next action, e.g. the Working/Paused/no-action cases); a Workers section rendering full `WorkerSessionRow`s (name/role/status/live timer/today/total/cost, Start/Pause/Resume/Stop/Add Manual Entry/View Sessions exactly as Unit 8/9B built them — no session logic touched); a Materials mini-section (status chip, Required/Issued/Remaining totals, one action button); a Closure mini-section (Ready/Not Ready/Requested/Closed chip plus a brief reason line); and a footer row (Open Full Job Card, View Materials, and Print — gated by the same `work_orders.print` permission the Job Card detail page's own Print button uses). Any secondary button whose label matches the panel's own Next Action button is suppressed (same "do not repeat the same click twice" rule Unit 9B established for its card footer).

**Task 8 — responsive:** the grid is a single column (list, then panel, stacked) below `lg:`; at `lg:` and up it becomes the 35%/65% split with the left list made sticky/`overflow-y-auto` (capped to `calc(100vh-220px)`) so it scrolls independently of the panel. Clicking a row on a stacked (sub-`lg:`) viewport scrolls the panel into view via `scrollIntoView` (checked against `window.innerWidth` at click time, not a persistent media-query listener). No horizontal overflow introduced — all new containers use `flex-wrap`/`min-w-0`/`truncate` the same way the rest of this page already does.

**Task 9 — realtime/selection preservation:** `RealtimeRefresh`'s watch list and `AutoRefresh`'s poll interval are byte-for-byte unchanged from Unit 9B — no new EventSource, no new event names. Selection survives a `router.refresh()` (which both hooks already call) because `DailyActivityBoard` is a client component whose `selectedId` state is not reset by its parent Server Component re-rendering with new props — it's the same component instance. The displayed selection is derived each render as `cards.find(id) ?? cards[0]`, so if the previously-selected Job Card no longer exists in the freshly-fetched list (for example, it closed), the panel automatically falls back to the first remaining card with no extra effect/listener needed.

**Task 10 — backend/data unchanged:** no migration; no server action added or edited; `getWorkOrderLaborSummariesBulk`/`getMaterialFulfillmentForWorkOrders`/work session actions all called exactly as Unit 9/9B left them; the only new computation is `materialsTotals` (a plain sum of the already-fetched per-row `required_qty`/`issued_qty`/`remaining_qty` fields, nothing recalculated); no data read, written, or deleted differently than before.

**Task 11 — manual browser tests:** could not be run live — no browser-automation tool is available in this environment and no login credentials were available to script an authenticated check (same limitation noted in every prior unit's report). Verified statically: successful production build (registers `/maintenance/daily-activity` and would fail on any prop/type mismatch across the new board/panel/list-row split), clean lint/typecheck, and a full manual re-read confirming the selected-card panel's `WorkerSessionRow`s remain independent `<form>`/`useActionState` pairs (starting one worker still cannot affect another or any other Job Card), that switching the selected card only changes the panel's contents (list rows are stateless buttons), and that the fallback-to-first-card logic behaves correctly when a card's `id` is no longer present in a refreshed `cards` array.

**Validation:** `npm run db:check`, `lint`, `typecheck`, and `build` all pass clean (build output includes `/maintenance/daily-activity` among all 62 routes). No migration.

No approval or closure workflow changed. No materials/assignment/work-session calculation logic changed. Job Cards page, Job Card detail page, and every existing route/nav entry unchanged — this unit only restructured how the Daily Activity page presents already-existing data. No deployment performed.

## Phase DailyActivityFinalPolishUnit9D-01 — Daily Activity Control Board Final UI Polish Unit 9D — COMPLETE

Goal: Unit 9C's split-screen control board worked, but still felt slightly large/heavy — rows a bit tall, the selected state styled like an error (strong red ring), Next Action wording terse, worker/materials/closure sections a bit loose. Tighten everything further and rebalance color so red is reserved for genuine attention states, with zero backend/workflow/materials/assignment/work-session-calculation changes.

**Files changed:** `components/work-orders/daily-activity-card.tsx` (list row + selected panel), `components/work-orders/daily-activity-board.tsx` (right panel sticky/scroll), `components/work-orders/worker-session-row.tsx` (padding + live timer chip), `app/(dashboard)/maintenance/daily-activity/page.tsx` (summary cards/filters compaction, Next Action wording/hrefs, filter accent color).

**Task 1 — compact left rows:** row padding `p-2.5 → p-2`; Job Card #/issue/asset text sizes trimmed (`text-sm/xs → text-xs/[11px]`); added a small `TinyStatusBadge` (Job Card status) next to the number, matching the task's "small status badge" requirement; `MiniChip`s shrunk further (`px-1.5 py-0.5 text-[10px] → px-1 py-0.5 text-[9px]`); issue line stays `line-clamp-1`, asset line stays `truncate`.

**Task 2 — selected row styling:** changed from a strong red ring (`bg-red-50/70 ring-2 ring-[#ED1C24]`) to a soft blue treatment (`bg-blue-50 ring-1 ring-[#93C5FD]`) — the selected row now reads as "this is what you're viewing," not as an error/warning. The priority-colored left accent bar is untouched by selection (it keeps signaling priority independently).

**Task 3 — priority indicator refinement:** kept red strictly for the "materials" bucket (blocked/materials pending) and amber for "paused"; green now also covers the "closure" (ready) bucket alongside "working"; the previous flat gray neutral for not-started/unassigned was changed to a soft blue-tinted neutral (`#93C5FD`) instead of `#D1D5DB` gray, matching the task's "neutral/blue" wording — most rows are no longer any shade of red by default.

**Task 4 — compact summary cards:** padding/icon/text shrunk again (`px-2.5 py-2 → px-2 py-1.5`, icon `h-3.5 → h-3`, label `text-[10px] → text-[9px]`); the same five/six cards and click-to-filter behavior kept. The active-filter ring on `SummaryCardLink` changed from red to blue (see Task 2's rationale) — clicking a summary card to filter by it is a neutral action, not an alert.

**Task 5 — compact filters:** container padding `p-2.5 → p-2`, all internal gaps `gap-2 → gap-1.5`; search input `py-1.5 pl-8 → py-1 pl-7`; dropdowns `py-1.5 → py-1`; the icon-only search-submit button and Reset link both shrunk to `min-h-7`. `FilterChip` also tightened (`min-h-8 px-3 py-1 → min-h-7 px-2.5 py-1`) and its active color switched from red to blue — except the "Materials Pending" chip specifically, which keeps its red active color via a new `urgent` prop, since that one genuinely is an attention filter.

**Task 6 — right panel header:** added a small `Selected Job Card` label (`text-[10px] uppercase text-[#9CA3AF]`) above the header block; header padding/gaps tightened (`pb-3 → pb-2.5`, title `text-lg` unchanged for legibility but the section itself is now noticeably shorter overall).

**Task 7 — Next Action panel:** added an explicit `Next Action` title line above the message (previously just the message with no label). Wording rewritten to match the task's own examples where a state maps directly to one ("No workers assigned yet." / "Job Card is ready for closure request." / materials-pending message), and extended for the others in the same one-primary-sentence style. The two states that previously had no button (Not Started, Paused) now get one: "Track Work" and "Resume Work" respectively, both pointing to a new in-page anchor (`#daily-activity-workers`, exported as `WORKERS_SECTION_ID` from `daily-activity-card.tsx` so page.tsx builds the exact matching href) that scrolls straight to the Workers section directly below in the same panel — not a new mutation control, just a same-page scroll to the real Start/Resume button, which stays gated by `canManageSessions` exactly as before. "Working" still gets no button (with multiple workers, a card-level button can't say which one to pause — the actual Pause/Stop controls are one scroll away regardless). Red accent/button color is now conditional (`nextActionIsUrgent = materialsChip.label === "Materials Pending"`) — every other Next Action uses a calm blue accent instead of red-by-default.

**Task 8 — worker row polish:** row padding `p-3.5 → p-2.5`, internal gaps trimmed, left column `sm:w-44 → sm:w-40`; the live timer is now wrapped in its own highlighted chip (`bg-green-50` rounded box around the "Live" label + timer) so it's the first thing a glance lands on for an active worker — "more visible" per the task, without changing its underlying value/precision. No data read, written, or deleted differently than before.

**Task 14 — manual browser tests:** could not be run live — no browser-automation tool is available in this environment and no login credentials were available to script an authenticated check (same limitation noted in every prior unit's report). **Validation:** `npm run db:check`, `lint`, `typecheck`, and `build` all pass clean (build output includes `/maintenance/daily-activity` among all 62 routes). No migration.

## Phase OneScreenDataEntryDashboardUnit9E-01 — One-Screen Data Entry Dashboard Unit 9E — COMPLETE

Goal: redesign the Data Entry dashboard into a compact one-screen command center — quick actions (Daily Activity first and visually prominent), a compact Today Summary, a "Needs Attention" list above the existing recent-Job-Cards list, and a small Continue Daily Activity CTA — so Data Entry can see what to do today with minimal scrolling, with zero backend/workflow/materials/assignment/work-session-calculation changes.

**Files changed:** `app/(dashboard)/dashboard/page.tsx` only (imports, the Data Entry data-fetch block, three new small render components, and the Data Entry JSX render block). Every other role's section in this same shared file (Manager, Engineer, Technician, Store Keeper, Viewer/Auditor, Super Admin, CEO) was left untouched — confirmed by re-reading each block and by `KpiRow`/`ActivityList`/`QuickAction`(non-`primary`) still being used identically elsewhere in the file.

**Task 1/10 — one-screen layout:** reordered the Data Entry section into header (unchanged, shared `PageHeader`) → Quick Actions → Today Summary (+ two small secondary count links) → Continue Daily Activity CTA → Needs Attention → Recent Job Cards, with tighter vertical rhythm (`space-y-1.5`/`gap-1.5`/`gap-2` instead of the old section's looser spacing) so Needs Attention sits above the fold on a normal desktop screen; Recent Job Cards is the one section allowed to fall below it.

**Task 2 — header:** unchanged — `PageHeader title="Hello, {firstName}"` / `description="Here's what needs your attention today."` was already this exact compact shared header before this unit; nothing to change.

**Task 3 — quick actions:** rebuilt to the task's exact required order/count (Open Daily Activity, Create New Job Card, Materials Requests, Offline Inventory Control, Assets & Equipment — "View My Job Cards" dropped from this widget only, since it's not in the task's required list and Job Cards stays reachable via Daily Activity, the sidebar, and the Recent Job Cards "View all" link). `QuickAction` gained an optional `primary` variant (filled red card, white text) used only for Open Daily Activity, so it's visually first and important without a new component; every other existing call site across every other role's section omits `primary` and renders byte-identical to before. Subtitles use the task's exact required copy for the four specified actions.

**Task 4 — Today Summary:** replaced the old 4-card "My Work Today" `KpiRow` with a new compact horizontal 6-card grid (`TodaySummaryCard` — icon+label+value in one short row, shorter than the existing vertical `StatCard`, matching the Daily Activity control board's own compact-card language from Unit 9C/9D): Active Job Cards (blue), Materials Pending (red when >0 else green), Working Now (green), Paused Workers (amber), Ready for Closure (blue), Drafts Not Started (gray) — every card links into Daily Activity's matching quick filter (or the Job Cards Draft tab for Drafts), exactly per the task's click-target table. Closure Requested and Closed Recently — both still meaningful counts — were kept as two small secondary text links below the grid rather than full cards, per the task's "cap at 6, keep extras smaller/secondary."

**Task 5/6/7 — Needs Attention:** new section between the Continue Daily Activity CTA and Recent Job Cards. Built from a bulk read over the 30 most-recently-updated active Job Cards (see Task 12) plus a small 5-row draft sample; each Job Card is assigned to exactly one bucket in this unit's own priority order (Materials Pending → Worker Paused → Working Now → Needs Assignment → Ready for Closure → Draft — a deliberate divergence from Daily Activity's own priority order, since here "what's blocking Data Entry" ranks materials first), sorted by that rank then recency, capped to the top 5. Each row (`NeedsAttentionRow`) shows Job Card #/asset/issue, one colored `StatusBadge` (Materials Pending=red, Worker Paused=amber, Working Now=green, Needs Assignment=blue, Ready for Closure=blue, Draft=gray — exact labels/tones from the task), and exactly one recommended action, the whole row being a single `<Link>` to that one action (same "whole row is the click target" convention `WoRow`/`NuJobCardRow` already use elsewhere on this dashboard) — never two competing buttons on one row. Materials Pending routes to "View Materials" (the real Materials Request when one exists, else the Job Card's parts anchor) rather than an unconditional "Receive Materials," since Data Entry doesn't necessarily hold the store-issue permission that action would imply (the task's own "or View Materials if receiving is not directly safe" fallback). Needs Assignment's "Assign Workers" is gated by the real `work_orders.assign` permission check (falls back to "Open Job Card" if that check ever came back false), and Ready for Closure's "Request Closure" is always the real action (this whole branch only ever runs for the Data Entry role, which always holds the closure-request gate).

**Task 8 — Recent Job Cards:** the old "Latest Job Cards" section renamed to "Recent Job Cards," moved after Needs Attention, kept at its existing 5-row cap — `NuJobCardRow` and its data query are otherwise unchanged.

**Task 9 — Continue Daily Activity CTA:** a small, single-line banner (not a full section) shown only when `activeCount > 0`, linking straight to `/maintenance/daily-activity`, placed between Today Summary and Needs Attention.

**Task 11 — status wording:** Needs Attention's own badge labels use the task's simplified wording directly (Materials Pending/Worker Paused/Working Now/Needs Assignment/Ready for Closure/Draft); Recent Job Cards' status badges continue to use the existing `displaySimplifiedStatus`/`simplifiedStatusTone` helpers (already simplified wording, untouched, unit-9E didn't need to touch that helper).

Sample size capped at 30 active + 5 draft Job Cards (smaller than Daily Activity's own 50-row page cap, since this widget loads on every dashboard visit); Needs Attention itself capped to the top 5; Recent Job Cards stayed capped at 5 (unchanged from before this unit).

**Task 13 — realtime:** untouched — the dashboard's existing `<RealtimeRefresh watch={[...]} />` (shared across every role's section) already includes all five required prefixes (`job_card.`, `work_order.`, `materials_request.`, `offline_inventory.`, `material_ledger.`) plus two extra (`store_materials.`, `notification.`) that were already there; no new `EventSource`, no WebSockets, nothing added or removed from the watch list. `<AutoRefresh intervalMs={15000} />` also untouched.

## Phase RoleToRoleCriticalWorkflowPopupUnit9G-01 — Role-to-Role Critical Workflow Popup Unit 9G — COMPLETE

Goal: give Data Entry and Manager a centered, stronger popup for a short, specific list of important actions the *other* role takes on a Job Card (Manager closes → Data Entry sees it; Data Entry requests closure → Manager sees it), on top of the existing bell/toast/Notification Center (unchanged), while never popping up a user's own action — built entirely on the existing notification schema and SSE stream, no migration, no workflow changes.

**Files changed:** `lib/notifications/critical-popup.ts` (new — rule maps + query logic), `app/actions/notifications.ts` (one new thin server action), `components/notifications/critical-workflow-popup.tsx` (new client component), `components/layout/app-layout.tsx` (mount it), `app/(dashboard)/notifications/page.tsx` (one small "Action Required" badge). No notify-call-site, workflow, closure, materials, assignment, or session file touched.

**Task 2/3/4 — critical popup rules:** implemented as two small rule maps in `lib/notifications/critical-popup.ts`, keyed by the recipient's role:
- **Data Entry** (Task 3): `job_card.closed` → "Job Card Closed" / "Manager has approved and closed Job Card [number]." / primary "Open Job Card" / secondary "Open Daily Activity"; `job_card.assignment_updated` → "Job Card Updated" / "Manager updated Job Card [number]." / primary "Open Job Card". Both event keys already existed and already notify the Job Card creator (Task 3's "do not create new workflow events" — confirmed by reading `lib/backend/work-orders/service.ts` and `worker-roster.ts` before writing any code).
- **Manager** (Task 4): `job_card.closure_requested` → "Closure Approval Needed" / "Data Entry requested closure for Job Card [number]." / primary "Review Job Card"; `job_card.created`/`job_card.started` → "New Active Job Card" / "Job Card [number] has been started." / primary "Open Job Card". All three event keys already existed and already notify the `maintenance_manager` role.
- A notification only ever qualifies when: it belongs to the current recipient (via the existing `getUserNotifications` recipient scoping), it's unread, its `event_key` is one of the four above, and the two conditions in Task 5/6 below both hold.

**Task 5 — self-action exclusion, method documented:** `notifications.created_by` (surfaced as `actor_id` on `NotificationListItem`) is the selected actor field — confirmed present, populated, and already the codebase's established "who caused this" field (every real `notifyWorkflowEvent` call site passes `actorId`, and `dedupeRecipients(ids, actorId)` already excludes the actor from recipients at write time in the vast majority of cases). Two checks, both required: (1) `actor_id` must be non-null and must not equal `context.userId` — if `actor_id` is missing, the candidate is skipped entirely rather than guessed at, matching Task 5's explicit "if actor cannot be reliably detected, avoid popup"; (2) the actor's **current** role (resolved via one bulk `profiles.findMany` → `roles.slug` lookup, not stored on the notification row) must be in the rule's `expectedActorRoles` — this is what makes the popup genuinely role-to-role rather than just "anyone but me," since `job_card.assignment_updated` in particular can be triggered by either Data Entry or Manager (both hold `work_orders.assign`).

**Task 6/7 — popup design:** `components/notifications/critical-workflow-popup.tsx` reuses the existing `WorkflowSuccessModal` shell as-is (no new modal component built from scratch) — same backdrop/dialog/icon-circle/title/description/footer-button-row every other standardized workflow popup already uses. `iconVariant` is chosen per rule (`success` for Job Card Closed, `warning` for Closure Approval Needed, `info` for the two "updated"/"new" awareness cases). The Job Card number, when available, renders via the shell's existing `summaryItems` ("Job Card: [number]"). Primary button uses `WorkflowSuccessModal`'s `link` action kind (`href` + `onClick`), so clicking it both navigates via `action_url` (or the Task 7 fallback chain: `action_url` → `/maintenance/work-orders/[entity_id]` when `entity_type === "work_order"` → `/notifications`) and fires the mark-read side effect in the same click — no `preventDefault`, no extra step.

**Task 8 — SSE/notification provider reuse:** no new EventSource, no WebSocket. The popup subscribes to the exact same `"notification"` SSE event (via the existing shared `useRealtimeConnection()` from `RealtimeConnectionProvider`) that `NotificationToastCenter` already uses — that event is a bare `{ id, title, category, priority, created_at }` trigger (confirmed by reading `app/api/notifications/stream/route.ts`), so on receipt the popup calls the new `getCriticalWorkflowPopupAction(notificationId)` server action to fetch/filter the full row before deciding to render, mirroring `NotificationToastCenter`'s own `getClientNotificationsAction` round-trip pattern exactly.

**Task 9 — avoid old-notification flood, one popup only:** two modes inside `getCriticalWorkflowPopup()`. (a) Live/event-driven — when an SSE `"notification"` signal arrives while the tab is open, only that one specific notification id is checked, no age limit (it just fired) — this is "new critical notifications received after session starts." (b) Initial-mount fallback — on mount, a single check scans the recipient's unread notifications and keeps only ones created within the last 5 minutes, returning the single newest qualifying one — this is the task's explicit "or, if not possible: latest critical unread notification from last 5 minutes" fallback, needed for the manual-test scenario where a user logs in shortly *after* the triggering action rather than having the tab open when it happened. Days-old unread notifications are never scanned by either path. A React ref (`activeIdRef`) blocks any further check while a popup is already displayed, so at most one is ever shown at once — no queue was built (not required by the task).

**Task 10 — dismiss behavior, documented exactly:** dismissing (via the shell's built-in backdrop click / X button / Esc / trailing "Dismiss" text button — `closeLabel="Dismiss"`) adds the notification's id to a `sessionStorage` array (`recafco_dismissed_critical_popups`) and does **not** call `markNotificationReadAction` — the notification stays unread and fully visible in the bell/Notification Center afterward, exactly as the task specifies. Because the id lives in `sessionStorage` (not `localStorage`, not the database), the same popup will not reappear after a same-tab refresh, but will reappear in a genuinely new browser session — matching "hide for current browser session." Clicking the **primary** action (only) calls the existing `markNotificationReadAction` (the same one `notification-toast-center.tsx` already calls) before/alongside navigating — clicking the *secondary* action ("Open Daily Activity") or dismissing does not mark it read.

**Task 11 — Notification Center/Bell:** bell dropdown, toast center, and the Notification Center's overall layout/filters/summary cards are all completely untouched. The one allowed small addition: a red "Action Required" `StatusBadge` next to each row's existing category/priority/read badges on the Notification Center page, shown when `notification.event_key` is one of the four critical keys for the *viewer's own role* (via the new `isCriticalEventKeyForRole()` export) — deliberately event-key-only (no per-row actor-role lookup, which would mean up to 50 extra queries on that page) since this is a lightweight visual hint on the history page, not the trigger for the popup itself.

**Task 12 — schema:** no migration. Every field read (`recipient_user_id`/`recipient_id`, `is_read`, `read_at`, `created_at`, `event_key`, `category`, `priority`, `action_url`, `action_label`, `metadata`, `entity_type`, `entity_id`, `created_by`) already existed on `notifications`, already populated by existing `notifyWorkflowEvent` call sites, and already exposed on `NotificationListItem`. The one new query this unit adds (`profiles.findMany` to resolve actor roles) reads existing `profiles`/`roles` tables through their existing relation, no new column anywhere.

**Task 13 — no workflow changes confirmed:** this unit's implementation touched exactly five files (`lib/notifications/critical-popup.ts`, `app/actions/notifications.ts`, `components/notifications/critical-workflow-popup.tsx`, `components/layout/app-layout.tsx`, `app/(dashboard)/notifications/page.tsx`) — no `Edit`/`Write` call was made against `lib/backend/work-orders/service.ts`, `work-sessions.ts`, `worker-roster.ts`, `lib/backend/parts-requests/service.ts`, or `lib/backend/store/service.ts` at any point while building this unit (those files were only read, during research, to confirm the existing event keys/metadata shape this unit reads from). Every event this unit reacts to was already being generated by existing, unmodified backend code; this unit only adds a new *read* path over that existing data plus one new client component.

**Manual tests (Part F):** could not be run live — no browser-automation tool is available in this environment and no login credentials were available to script an authenticated check (same limitation noted in every prior unit's report). Verified statically: successful production build (would fail on any prop/type mismatch across the new service/action/component), clean lint/typecheck, and a full manual trace confirming (a) the self-action guard (`actor_id !== context.userId`) and the actor-role check both run before any candidate is returned, (b) the 5-minute fallback window and the "no notificationId ⇒ recency-filtered / notificationId given ⇒ no age filter" branching match Task 9 exactly, and (c) dismiss vs. primary-click behavior matches Task 10's documented distinction (sessionStorage-only vs. mark-read-then-navigate).

**Validation:** `npm run db:check`, `lint`, `typecheck`, and `build` all pass clean (all 62 routes built, including `/notifications`). No migration.

No approval, closure, materials, assignment, or work-session logic changed anywhere. Job Cards, Materials Requests, and Offline Inventory Control are unchanged and unrenamed. The existing notification bell, toast center, and Notification Center page all continue to behave exactly as before for every notification outside this unit's small critical-event allowlist. No deployment performed.

## Phase ManagerWorkerTimeCorrectionUnit10C1-01 — Manager Worker Time Correction Enhancement Unit 10C.1 — COMPLETE

Goal: make the Manager's worker-time correction flow, reached from the Worker Activity Details modal (Unit 10C), clear, safe, audited, and directly accessible per session row — reusing Unit 8's existing correction backend (`editWorkSession`/`editWorkSessionAction`, `SessionHistoryModal`) rather than duplicating it. Data Entry remains unable to correct sessions, backend-enforced.

**Files changed:** `lib/backend/work-orders/work-sessions.ts` (`editWorkSession` — audit metadata extended with original pre-correction values), `lib/work-orders/work-session-totals.ts` (`WorkerActivitySessionRow` gained `editedByName`; `getWorkerActivityDetail()`'s session select/mapping extended to resolve it via the existing `profiles_edited_by` relation), `components/work-orders/session-history-modal.tsx` (new optional `initialEditSessionId`/`jobCardNumber`/`assetLabel` props; `EditSessionForm` now renders an "Original session" reference block; an Active session now shows an explicit message instead of silently hiding its buttons), `components/workers/worker-activity-detail-modal.tsx` (`sessionsFor` state extended to carry a specific `sessionId`/job-card context; each recent-session row gained a "Correct Session" button, a "Corrected" badge, an Active-session message, and reload-on-return via a new `reloadToken`). No schema change, no new table.

**Task 1 — existing backend confirmed, not duplicated:** `editWorkSession()`/`cancelWorkSession()` in `lib/backend/work-orders/work-sessions.ts` (Unit 8) already: (a) enforce `assertIsManager(context)` server-side — throws `FORBIDDEN` for non-Manager/non-Super-Admin regardless of what the UI shows; (b) require a `correction_reason` of at least 5 characters (`lib/backend/workers/work-session-validators.ts`, `z.string().trim().min(5).max(500)`); (c) block editing an `Active` session (`"Stop or pause this session before editing it."`); (d) recalculate `duration_minutes` and `calculated_amount` using the session's own `hourly_rate_snapshot`, never the current worker profile rate; (e) write an audit log and emit `job_card.work_time_updated` on every correction. Nothing in this unit reimplements any of this — only additive extensions were made.

**Task 2 — direct per-session correction:** each row in Worker Activity Details → Recent Sessions now has its own "Correct Session" button (Manager/Super Admin only, hidden for Data Entry — and unreachable for Data Entry even if attempted, since `editWorkSessionAction`'s server action delegates straight to `assertIsManager`-gated `editWorkSession`). Clicking it sets `sessionsFor` to that session's `{ workerAssignmentId, sessionId, jobCardNumber, assetLabel }`, which `SessionHistoryModal` consumes via its new `initialEditSessionId` prop to initialize `editingId` directly — the correction form for that exact session opens immediately, no need to locate it again in the assignment's full session list.

**Task 3 — Original session reference block:** `EditSessionForm` now renders a labelled "Original session" panel above the editable fields, showing worker name, Job Card number, asset (when known), original start, original end/pause ("(in progress)" if still open), original duration, original amount (cost-gated), and current status — all read from the session row being edited, so the Manager can see what's being changed while changing it. Start/end datetime fields remain the primary editable mechanism (unchanged from Unit 8) rather than a direct duration field, since they're already validated and correctly recalculate duration/amount — judged safer per the task's own "only if safer" qualifier.

**Task 4 — validation, unchanged/verified plus one gap closed:** reason min-length (5), `stoppedAt > startedAt`, and the Active-session block were all already enforced server-side (Unit 8, re-verified, no change). The one UI gap closed: an Active session's row previously showed no buttons and no explanation; it now shows "Stop or pause this session before correction." explicitly, in both `SessionHistoryModal` and the Recent Sessions list in `WorkerActivityDetailModal`.

**Task 5 — hours/pay recalculation:** already correct in Unit 8 (`computeAmount(durationMinutes, Number(existing.hourly_rate_snapshot))` uses the session's own frozen rate) — confirmed by reading the function, no change needed.

**Task 6 — audit trail:** `editWorkSession()` now captures the pre-update row's `started_at`, `stopped_at ?? paused_at`, `duration_minutes`, and `calculated_amount` inside the transaction (before the `update` overwrites them) and returns them as part of its transaction result (`original`), avoiding an outer mutable variable captured by the transaction closure. `notifyAndAudit()`'s existing `writeAuditLog()` call now also records `original_started_at`, `original_ended_at`, `original_duration_minutes`, `original_calculated_amount`, `corrected_started_at`, and `corrected_ended_at` alongside the pre-existing `correctionReason`, actor, and timestamp. The row itself is only ever updated, never hard-deleted — matching the existing soft-correction pattern.

**Task 7 — corrected sessions displayed clearly:** Recent Sessions rows in `WorkerActivityDetailModal` show a "Corrected" `StatusBadge` and a "Correction (by {name}): {reason}" line when `correctionReason` is present, using the new `editedByName` field (resolved from the pre-existing `profiles_edited_by` relation, the same one `getSessionsForAssignment`/`SessionHistoryModal` already used). `SessionHistoryModal`'s own list already showed "Corrected by {name}: {reason}" from Unit 8 — unchanged.

**Task 8 — Manager-only, backend-enforced:** `isManager` continues to gate the "Correct Session" button in the UI (both `SessionHistoryModal` and `WorkerActivityDetailModal`), but the actual enforcement is `assertIsManager(context)` inside `editWorkSession()` itself — a Data Entry user cannot correct a session even by calling the server action directly. Viewer cannot reach the Worker Activity page at all (lacks `work_orders.assign`).
