(Task 7); a review checklist (Materials completed / No active worker session — both real, read-only mirrors of the backend guards; Worker hours reviewed / Attachments reviewed — click-to-toggle Manager acknowledgements that never gate the button, Task 8) plus an optional Manager approval note and the only "Approve Closure" button, submitting through the same `approveJobCardClosureModalAction` wrapper added in the original Unit 10G (itself unchanged, still calling the real `approveJobCardClosure` service function verbatim).

## Unit 10G.3 Fix — Closure Review Rate/Pay Not Showing

**Requirement:** the Manager Closure Review popup was reported as still not showing worker hourly rate/pay (only Total Hours/Sessions/session duration visible) despite Unit 10G.3's formatting pass. Investigate the full data flow (backend query → action DTO → component props → `canViewCosts` rendering) and fix whatever is dropping the data, without touching schema, work-session calculation, `hourly_rate_snapshot` behavior, or exposing costs to Data Entry.

**Investigation (Tasks 1/2):** re-read `getClosureReviewDetailAction` (`app/actions/closure-requests.ts`) end to end and `closure-review-modal.tsx` end to end. Found **no code defect** in either file:
- The action computes `canViewCosts` once via the canonical `canViewCostsForContext` (`lib/security/permissions.ts`) and correctly threads it into `workers[].hourlyRate`, `workers[].totalPay`, `totalAmount`, and the returned `canViewCosts` field itself — all `null` server-side (not merely hidden) whenever the gate is false.
- The component receives `canViewCosts` from `detail.canViewCosts` (the action's own computed value, not re-derived client-side) and passes it down to both `WorkerReviewCard` and `SessionTable`, which gate the Hourly Rate/Total Pay/session Pay lines correctly.

**Root cause:** not a code defect. The seeded "manager" test account(s) (role `maintenance_manager`) have `profiles.can_view_costs = false`, and the `maintenance_manager` role itself is not granted the `costs.view` permission — so `canViewCosts()` legitimately evaluates to `false` for that account, exactly as it would on every other cost-gated screen in the app (Worker Activity, Job Card detail, Daily Activity), since they all use the same canonical helper. Only `super_admin` bypasses via `hasPermission`'s own logic regardless of the profile flag. Confirmed via `scripts/verify-closure-review-payment-display-unit10g3fix.mjs`'s read-only section: both seeded `maintenance_manager` profiles have `can_view_costs=false`, and the role has 0 of its 25 permissions named `costs.view`. This is a seed/permission **data** characteristic (documented in `CLAUDE.md`'s Current Database State baseline), not something this unit changed or should silently change — granting cost visibility to a role/profile is a security-relevant, app-wide decision left to the user.

**Genuine gap found and fixed (Task 3):** `SessionRow.edited_by_name` was already fetched by `getSessionsForAssignmentAction` but never rendered in the Closure Review popup's session rows. Added it next to `correction_reason` in `SessionTable` (`components/dashboard/closure-review-modal.tsx`): `Reason: {reason} · Edited by: {edited_by_name}`. `duration_minutes`/`calculated_amount`/`started_at`/`stopped_at`(`ended_at`)/`status` were already displayed.

**Files changed:** `components/dashboard/closure-review-modal.tsx` (one addition: `edited_by_name` display). `app/actions/closure-requests.ts` unchanged — no bug found there. `scripts/verify-closure-review-payment-display-unit10g3fix.mjs` (new).

**Validation:** `npm run db:check`, `lint`, `typecheck`, and `build` all pass clean. No migration, no schema change, no calculation change, no `hourly_rate_snapshot` behavior change. Data Entry still cannot reach this popup (Manager-only dashboard section) and still receives `null` cost fields wherever `canViewCosts` is checked elsewhere in the app.

**Open item for the user:** if rate/pay should be visible when testing with the seeded "manager" account, either set `profiles.can_view_costs = true` on that profile or grant the `maintenance_manager` role the `costs.view` permission — a data/permission decision, not a code change, and left to the user to authorize since it affects cost visibility app-wide for that account, not just Closure Review. The "System Administrator" super_admin seed account already has `can_view_costs = true` and can be used to see the feature working end to end today.

## Unit 10G.4 — Admin Cost Visibility Toggle for Manager Users

**Requirement:** the Super Admin Users page had no way to grant `can_view_costs` to a user — Unit 10G.3 Fix's finding was that the seeded "manager" test account legitimately has `can_view_costs = false`, and there was no UI to change it short of a direct DB write. Add a Super Admin-only "Cost Access" control on the admin user detail page.

**Server action:** `updateUserCostAccessAction` (new, `app/actions/user-access.ts`) — follows this file's existing `toggleUserActiveAction`/`archiveUserAction` pattern exactly: `requirePermission("admin.users.manage")`, then a hard `context.role?.slug !== "super_admin"` gate (redirect `insufficient-permissions` otherwise), Zod-parsed `profile_id`/`can_view_costs` from a plain `<form action>` (checkbox semantics: unchecked box is simply absent from `FormData`, so the same `z.preprocess((v) => v === "true", z.boolean())` idiom used by `toggleUserActiveAction` correctly resolves absence to `false`), a single `profiles.update({ data: { can_view_costs } })`, `writeAuditLog` with action `user.cost_access_updated` and `{ can_view_costs }` metadata, `emitRealtimeEvent(REALTIME_EVENTS.USER_UPDATED)` (the same event `toggleUserActiveAction` emits — `RealtimeRefresh watch={["user."]}` already active on this page), `revalidatePath`, redirect with `?success=cost-access-updated`. Writes only `profiles.can_view_costs` — never touches `role_permissions`/`costs.view`, so nothing is granted role-wide or to any other user.

**UI:** `app/(dashboard)/admin/users/[id]/page.tsx` — new "Cost Access" `Card`, rendered only when `isSuperAdminViewer`, placed between "Change account type" and "Account actions". Real HTML checkbox (`name="can_view_costs" value="true" defaultChecked={profile.can_view_costs}`) plus a "Save Cost Access" button — works with zero client JS, matching every other action on this page. Added `"cost-access-updated": "Cost access updated."` to the success-message map.

**Data Entry / non-Super-Admin exposure:** the card is gated by `isSuperAdminViewer` (in addition to the whole page already requiring `admin.users.manage`), so a non-Super-Admin who somehow reaches this page cannot see or submit the control; the server action independently re-checks `role.slug === "super_admin"` regardless of what the client sends, so the gate cannot be bypassed by posting the form directly. `costs.view` role permission and every other profile's `can_view_costs` are untouched — Data Entry accounts remain at `false` unless a Super Admin explicitly flips this control for that specific account.

**Files changed:** `app/actions/user-access.ts` (new `updateUserCostAccessAction`), `app/(dashboard)/admin/users/[id]/page.tsx` (new Cost Access card + success message), `scripts/verify-admin-cost-access-toggle-unit10g4.mjs` (new).

**Validation:** `npm run db:check`, `lint`, `typecheck`, and `build` all pass clean. No migration, no schema change, no calculation change. `scripts/verify-admin-cost-access-toggle-unit10g4.mjs` (rolled-back transaction) confirms: `canViewCosts()` (the same canonical gate used everywhere) flips its answer purely off `profile.can_view_costs` for a Manager-equivalent context with no `costs.view` permission; the action's own DB write (grant → audit log → revoke) round-trips correctly against a real disposable profile row; `maintenance_data_entry`'s role permissions are untouched by this unit. No deployment performed.

## Unit 10G.5 — Manager Dashboard Labor Cost Period Summary Fix

**Requirement:** the Manager dashboard only showed "Labor Hours Today"/"Labor Cost Today," which reads as broken when a worker's sessions were recorded yesterday or earlier (Today can legitimately be 0). Add This Week/This Month labor totals alongside Today, without touching schema, work-session calculation, `hourly_rate_snapshot` behavior, or Data Entry's cost visibility.

**Task 1 — confirmed, not a calculation bug:** `Labor Hours Today`/`Labor Cost Today` were already correctly scoped to `started_at >= todayStart` and already read `0`/`0.000 KWD` with no sessions today — verified by `scripts/verify-manager-labor-period-summary-unit10g5.mjs`'s empty-work-order case. The "looks broken" symptom was a display gap (no Week/Month figure to show the labor actually happened), not a data or calculation defect.

**New read — `getLaborPeriodTotals`** (`lib/work-orders/work-session-totals.ts`, new): a company-wide, visibility-scoped Today/This Week/This Month total. Deliberately NOT derived from the dashboard's existing `getWorkOrderLaborSummariesBulk` map, because that map (as called from this dashboard) only ever covers the ~30 most-recently-updated ACTIVE Job Cards — a Job Card worked on this week but already Closed would silently disappear from a week/month total built that way, reproducing the exact "not updating" confusion this unit exists to fix. One query (sessions with `started_at >= monthStart`, `status != Cancelled`, filtered through the `work_orders` relation by the caller's own visibility filter), bucketed in-memory into today/week/month — same "fetch once, bucket by boundary" convention `getWorkerActivityDetail` already established, same Sunday-start week boundary, same `duration_minutes`/`calculated_amount` fields (a corrected session's current stored values are summed automatically; cancelled sessions excluded by the query itself).

**Extended `getWorkOrderLaborSummariesBulk`:** added `week_minutes`/`week_amount`/`month_minutes`/`month_amount` at the Job-Card level and `week_minutes`/`week_hours`/`week_amount`/`month_minutes`/`month_hours`/`month_amount` per worker (`WorkerLaborRow`, `DailyActivityLaborSummary` types) — free in-memory buckets over the same session rows the function already fetches with no date filter, no new query. Three call sites' fallback default objects updated for the new required fields: `app/actions/closure-requests.ts`, `app/(dashboard)/dashboard/page.tsx` (closure requests modal), `app/(dashboard)/maintenance/daily-activity/page.tsx`.

**Dashboard changes (Task 2/3/4):**
- KPI row: `Labor Hours`/`Labor Cost` renamed to `Labor Hours Today`/`Labor Cost Today` (Task 3, Option A — explicit "Today" now that Week/Month appear just below), sourced from the new `mgLaborPeriodTotals.today` (previously from the 30-active-sample-only `mgHoursTodaySum`/`mgAmountTodaySum`, now removed).
- Labor Snapshot card: header renamed `Labor Snapshot Today` → `Labor Snapshot` (it now covers all three periods); new compact period-summary block — `Today` / `This Week` / `This Month`, each `Xh` plus (only when `mgCanViewCosts`) `/ X.XXX KWD` — all three sourced from the same `mgLaborPeriodTotals`, so they can never disagree with each other or with the KPI row.
- Top Workers and Job Card Labor Cost now default to **This Week** (was Today/all-time respectively) per the task's own recommendation ("meaningful current workload") — `mgWorkerWeekTotals` (renamed from `mgWorkerTodayTotals`) and `mgJobCardLaborRows` both switched to the new `week_minutes`/`week_amount` fields; still scoped to the same active/recent 30-Job-Card sample as before (unchanged convention, matches Task 4's "active/recent Job Cards" wording).

**Task 6 — cost visibility:** unchanged mechanism — every new figure (period summary, Top Workers pay, Job Card Labor Cost pay) is gated by the same `mgCanViewCosts` (`canViewCostsForContext(context)`) already used everywhere else on this dashboard; Data Entry never reaches this Manager-only section of the page at all.

**Task 7 — realtime:** already fully satisfied before this unit — `REALTIME_EVENTS.JOB_CARD_WORK_STARTED/WORK_PAUSED/WORK_STOPPED/WORK_TIME_UPDATED` (`lib/realtime/events.ts`) are all `"job_card.*"` keys, already emitted from `lib/backend/work-orders/work-sessions.ts`, and the dashboard's existing `<RealtimeRefresh watch={["job_card.", ...]}>` already matches all four by prefix. No realtime code change needed; confirmed by reading the emit sites and the watch list, not assumed.

**Files changed:** `lib/work-orders/work-session-totals.ts` (new `getLaborPeriodTotals`, extended `getWorkOrderLaborSummariesBulk`/types), `app/(dashboard)/dashboard/page.tsx` (data + UI), `app/actions/closure-requests.ts` (fallback default), `app/(dashboard)/maintenance/daily-activity/page.tsx` (fallback default), `scripts/verify-manager-labor-period-summary-unit10g5.mjs` (new).

**Validation:** `npm run db:check`, `lint`, `typecheck`, and `build` all pass clean. No migration, no schema change, no work-session calculation change, no `hourly_rate_snapshot` behavior change, no approval/closure/materials logic touched. `scripts/verify-manager-labor-period-summary-unit10g5.mjs` (rolled-back transaction): confirms Today/Week/Month bucketing against real sessions spanning today/yesterday/earlier-this-month, a cancelled session fully excluded, a corrected session's post-correction values summed (not the original), an empty-Job-Card case reading exact zeros, period nesting (month ≥ week ≥ today), and the bulk function's new per-Job-Card/per-worker week/month fields. No deployment performed.

## Unit 10G.7 — Critical Workflow Popup Review Modal Instead of Direct Navigation

**Requirement:** the two Manager-facing critical popups (Closure Approval Needed, New Active Job Card) navigated straight to the full Job Card detail page on primary-button click, forcing the Manager off the dashboard. Clicking Review should open a review modal in place instead, with "Open Full Job Card" preserved as an explicit fallback — notification popup UX only, no workflow/approval/materials/session-calculation logic touched or duplicated.

**Payload/rule changes (Task 1/2/4/5):** `lib/notifications/critical-popup.ts` — `CriticalPopupPayload` gained `workOrderId`, `reviewMode` (`"closure_review" | "job_card_summary" | null`), and `jobCardDetailHref` (always the canonical `/maintenance/work-orders/{id}` URL, computed independently of `action_url`). `PopupRule` gained an optional `reviewMode`. The two Manager rules changed: `job_card.closure_requested` → `primaryLabel: "Review Closure"`, `reviewMode: "closure_review"`; `job_card.created`/`job_card.started` → `primaryLabel: "View Summary"`, `reviewMode: "job_card_summary"`. When a rule declares `reviewMode`, its `secondaryLabel`/`secondaryHref` are now always computed as `"Open Full Job Card"` / `jobCardDetailHref` (Task 5), overriding any rule-level static secondary. Every Data Entry rule (`job_card.closed`, `job_card.assignment_updated`) is completely untouched — `reviewMode` stays `undefined`/`null` for them, so their `primaryLabel`, plain-link behavior, and existing static secondary actions (e.g. "Open Daily Activity") are unchanged.

**Popup component (Task 1/3/6):** `components/notifications/critical-workflow-popup.tsx` — new `reviewing` state (`{ notificationId, workOrderId, mode }`) alongside the existing `popup` state. Primary-button click on a `reviewMode` popup now renders a `{ kind: "button", onClick: openReview }` action (via `WorkflowSuccessAction`'s existing `"button"` variant — no `WorkflowSuccessModal` change needed) that swaps the critical popup for `ClosureReviewModal` or `JobCardSummaryModal` in place, instead of the previous `{ kind: "link", href }` that navigated away. `activeIdRef` (the existing "only one popup at a time" guard) stays set through the whole reviewing session, so no second popup can appear underneath the review modal. Non-`reviewMode` popups (Data Entry's rules) keep the exact original `markReadAndClose` + Link behavior.

**Notification read timing (Task 6):** a new `onLoaded?: () => void` prop was added to `ClosureReviewModal` (`components/dashboard/closure-review-modal.tsx`) — called exactly once, guarded by a `hasCalledOnLoaded` ref, the first time its detail fetch succeeds; existing callers (the Closure Requests dashboard section) simply don't pass it, so their behavior is unchanged. `JobCardSummaryModal` (new) takes the same `onLoaded` prop with the same one-shot-on-success contract. `critical-workflow-popup.tsx`'s `markReviewLoaded()` (passed as `onLoaded`) is what actually calls `markNotificationReadAction` — so the notification is marked read only once the review modal's data has genuinely loaded, never on click alone, and never if the fetch fails (the `loadError` branch in either modal never calls `onLoaded`). Closing a review modal that never successfully loaded re-adds its notification id to the existing session-scoped dismissed-ids list (same mechanism the original Dismiss button already used) so it isn't silently lost; closing one that DID load is a no-op beyond resetting local state, since it's already been marked read.

**Approval flow (Task 3):** `approveAndCloseReview()` (passed as `ClosureReviewModal`'s `onApproved`) closes the review modal and calls `router.refresh()`, refreshing the dashboard's KPI/closure-requests count — mirrors the exact pattern already used by `ClosureRequestsModal`'s own `onApproved` handler. The "Job Card Closed" success toast is already dispatched inside `ClosureReviewModal` itself (from a prior unit) — not duplicated. `approveJobCardClosureModalAction` (the existing closure-approval server action) is unchanged and reused as-is — no approval logic duplicated anywhere in this unit.

The `"sm"` branch reproduces the exact prior class strings for every `primary`/`accent` combination (verified by reading the compiled ternary output directly), so every existing caller that doesn't pass `size` — all 6 of Manager's own Quick Actions tiles — renders byte-for-byte unchanged. `"lg"` scales up: `px-5 py-5` + `sm:min-h-[80px]` (was `px-3 py-2.5`), icon box `p-3.5` with a `h-7 w-7` icon (was `p-2`/`h-4 w-4`), title `text-xl` (was `text-sm`), subtitle `text-sm` (was `text-[11px]`), arrow `h-5 w-5` (was `h-4 w-4`). ## Unit 10G.13 — Estimated Work Hours for Job Cards and Workers

**Requirement:** Data Entry can enter an optional estimated total work hours figure on a Job Card, plus optional per-worker estimated hours, during New Job Card creation; Manager can compare estimated vs actual hours/variance across the Job Card detail page, Daily Activity, Closure Review, Closed Jobs, and Worker Activity, before approving closure. Hours-only for Data Entry (never rate/pay); existing Job Cards must keep working with no estimate.

**Schema (Task 14, additive only):** new migration `20260811000000_estimated_work_hours_unit10g13` adds two nullable columns, no existing column touched: `work_orders.estimated_labor_hours numeric(12,2)` and `work_order_worker_assignments.estimated_hours numeric(12,2)`. `prisma/schema.prisma` updated to match (`Decimal? @db.Decimal(12,2)` on both models). Applied via `prisma migrate deploy` (31 migrations total); `prisma generate` required a one-time dev-server restart to release the query engine DLL lock (same recurring issue as prior units). Every UI surface added in this unit shows "No estimate recorded." for a null value rather than requiring one — existing Job Cards read back null and are unaffected.

**Shared classifier:** new client-safe `lib/work-orders/hours-variance.ts` (no `"server-only"` import, deliberately split out of `lib/work-orders/work-session-totals.ts` which does have it and would otherwise poison any client component importing it — matches the existing `simplified-status.ts`/`simplified-status-display.ts` split convention). `computeHoursVariance(estimatedHours, actualHours)` returns On Track (`actual <= estimated`), Slightly Over (`actual <= estimated * 1.2`), Over Estimate (`actual > estimated * 1.2`), or No Estimate (`estimated == null`); `hoursVarianceTone(status)` maps to `StatusBadge` tones. `work-session-totals.ts` re-exports both for server-side convenience only.

**Task 1/2 — Wizard creation UI:** `components/work-orders/work-order-wizard.tsx`'s Work Team & Assignment step gained a standalone "Estimated total work hours" number input (optional, `step="0.25"`, always visible regardless of "Assign work now"), and — once Internal Team workers are selected — a per-worker "Estimated hours per selected worker" list (`SelectedWorkersEstimateList`). Equal-split is suggested via `placeholder` only (never pre-filled into state), and a soft (non-blocking) mismatch warning appears when entered worker estimates don't sum to the Job Card total. Data Entry never sees rate/pay anywhere in this step (unchanged). Per-worker values are carried through a single hidden `assign_worker_estimates` JSON field, parsed server-side by `parseWorkerEstimates()` (`app/actions/maintenance.ts`), which degrades to `{}` on any malformed input rather than blocking submission.

**Task 4 — Persistence and edit-safety:** `assignInternalTeamRoster` (`lib/backend/work-orders/worker-roster.ts`, shared by both the wizard's create path and the Job Card detail page's post-creation "Assign Internal Team" panel) now writes `estimated_hours` per picked worker. The detail-page roster edit form (`components/work-orders/internal-team-roster-form.tsx`) does not add new per-worker estimate *editing* UI in this unit — it resubmits each currently-known worker's existing estimate via a hidden `roster_worker_estimates` field, so adding/removing a roster member there never silently wipes a previously-set estimate. Full estimate editing remains a wizard-time-only capability, a deliberate scoping decision.

**Task 5/6 — Job Card detail page:** `components/work-orders/work-time-tracking.tsx` gained an "Estimated vs Actual" block (Estimated / Actual / Variance / `StatusBadge`, or "No estimate recorded.") both in the normal and the no-workers-assigned-yet state. `components/work-orders/worker-session-row.tsx` gained a per-worker "Estimated" chip with variance, shown whenever that worker has an estimate, unconditional on `canViewCosts`.

**Task 7 — Daily Activity:** `app/(dashboard)/maintenance/daily-activity/page.tsx` now selects `estimated_labor_hours` and threads it into each board card; `components/work-orders/daily-activity-card.tsx` shows a compact "Estimated total / Actual total" line when an estimate exists. Per-worker rows inherit the estimate display automatically since they reuse `WorkerSessionRow`.

**Task 8 — Manager Closure Review (most important):** `app/actions/closure-requests.ts` now selects `estimated_labor_hours` and returns per-worker `estimatedHours`; `components/dashboard/closure-review-modal.tsx` shows a Job-Card-level Estimated/Actual/Variance block before the worker list, and a per-worker Estimated/Variance line inside each `WorkerReviewCard`, both unconditional on `canViewCosts` (only rate/pay stay gated).

**Task 9 — Closed Jobs:** `app/actions/closed-job-cards.ts` gained `estimatedHours` on the list row and detail types/queries. `components/dashboard/closed-job-cards-summary.tsx`'s compact list row shows a brief "(Est: Xh)"; the detail popup shows the same Job-Card-level Estimated/Actual/Variance block as Closure Review plus a per-worker Estimated/Variance line next to each worker's hours/rate.

**Task 10 — Worker Activity:** `lib/work-orders/work-session-totals.ts`'s `WorkerCurrentJobCard`/`getWorkerActivitySummaries` gained `estimated_hours`. `components/workers/worker-card.tsx` shows "Estimated for this worker: X h" under the current Job Card; `components/workers/worker-activity-detail-modal.tsx`'s own `WorkerActivityDetailCurrentJobCard` type gained the same field and shows it in the header block. Existing Today/Week/Month totals are completely unchanged.

**Task 11 — Correction behavior (verified, no code change):** confirmed by inspection that neither `lib/backend/work-orders/work-sessions.ts` nor `app/actions/work-sessions.ts` (the session-correction path) reference `estimated_hours` or write to `workOrderWorkerAssignment` at all — corrections only ever touch `work_sessions` rows. ## Phase DailyActivitySummarySimplification-10G.15 — Daily Activity Summary Simplification Unit 10G.15 — COMPLETE

User feedback: Daily Activity's 5-card summary row (Active Job Cards / Working Now / Paused / Labor Hours Today / Ready for Closure) mixed monitoring/control metrics with labor reporting — "Daily Activity is for monitoring and controlling active Job Cards, not labor reporting." ## Phase DashboardGreetingLiveClock-10G.18 — Dashboard Greeting and Live Clock UI Polish Unit 10G.18 — COMPLETE

User wanted the dashboard header's static "Hello, {name}" replaced with a time-of-day greeting, a one-time typing effect, and a live clock — kept professional, no flashy animation. `app/(dashboard)/dashboard/page.tsx` has exactly one header render point (confirmed via grep — a single `<PageHeader title={\`Hello, ${firstName}\`} .../>` above every role-specific section: `isNormalUser`, `isManager`, and the rest), so this covers every role dashboard with one swap — no duplication existed to consolidate, satisfying Task 7 by construction rather than needing a separate reuse fix.

New `components/dashboard/live-dashboard-header.tsx` (client component, Task 1) replaces that one call site. Built standalone rather than widening the shared `<PageHeader/>`'s `title: string` prop to accept a client-animated node — `PageHeader` is used by essentially every other page in the app with a plain string title, so changing its prop shape was avoidable risk for a dashboard-only request; `LiveDashboardHeader` instead reproduces `PageHeader`'s exact visual shell (same `border-b border-[#DDE2EA]`, same red `border-l-4 border-[#ED1C24]` accent bar, same padding/type scale) so it's visually indistinguishable from every other page's header apart from the new greeting/clock behavior.

**Hydration safety (Task 2):** greeting and clock both depend on the visitor's local browser time, which the server can't know. Both `greeting` and `now` start as `null`/un-set state; the very first render (server HTML, and the client's first paint before hydration effects run) always shows the same time-independent fallback — `Good day, {profileName}` for the heading, `--:--:--` / blank for the clock — so server and client markup match byte-for-byte at hydration. A `useEffect` (mount-only, `[]` deps) then resolves the real greeting and starts the 1-second clock tick; this is a normal post-hydration DOM update, not a mismatch, and was confirmed zero-warning by `tsc`/`eslint` passing clean (no runtime console check was possible without a live browser session this unit, but the pattern itself is the textbook safe one).

**Typing effect (Task 3):** a second effect, gated on `mounted` and keyed to `fullText` (not to the once-a-second `now` tick, so it never re-fires while the clock ticks), reveals `${greeting}, ${profileName}` one character at a time via `setInterval` at 45ms/char (inside the 35–60ms range asked for), clearing the interval once the full string is reached — runs exactly once, never loops, never deletes. `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` (checked once via `window.matchMedia` inside the mount effect, cached in a ref) skips the animation entirely and shows the full text immediately, per Task 3's explicit accessibility requirement. Only the `<h1>` greeting animates; the subtitle (`<p>Here's what needs your attention today.</p>`) is always rendered in full, never animated.

**ESLint `react-hooks/set-state-in-effect` compliance:** an initial draft called `setGreeting`/`setNow`/`setMounted`/`setTypedLength` as direct top-level statements inside their effects, which this repo's stricter-than-default hooks lint rule rejects (same rule hit and fixed via derived state in Phase OfflineInventoryActionVisibilityFix-01). Here, unlike that case, the state genuinely can't be derived at render time (it's inherently effectful — depends on `Date.now()`/a running timer), so the fix instead followed the exact pattern already established and passing lint in `components/work-orders/live-timer.tsx`: wrap the setState calls inside a locally-defined `tick`/`reset`/`showFull` function and invoke that function, rather than calling the setters as bare statements — the rule only flags direct setter calls sitting immediately in the effect body, not calls made through a nested function reference. `npx eslint` on both changed files confirmed zero errors after the rewrite.

**Live clock (Task 4/6):** `formatClock()` renders `hh:mm:ss AM/PM` (`toLocaleString`, browser-local time) and a full weekday date (`Tuesday, 11 Aug 2026`, matching the task's own "Suggested display" example) in a small card — white/`#F9FAFB` background, `#E5E7EB` border, rounded corners, a muted `lucide-react` `Clock` icon, bold `font-mono tabular-nums` time, and a smaller muted-gray date underneath. The only "movement" is the text itself updating once a second (no blink/slide/bounce animation added) — satisfies "subtle movement only" without adding animation complexity. Interval is cleared in the effect's cleanup function on unmount, so no leaked timer.

**Layout (Task 5):** reused `PageHeader`'s own proven responsive shell verbatim (`flex flex-col gap-4 sm:flex-row sm:items-center sm:justify-between`) — greeting/subtitle stacks above the clock card on mobile, they sit side-by-side from `sm:` (640px) up. Nothing new needed here since this exact pattern was already handling the "stack on mobile, row on desktop" requirement for every other page's header/actions slot.

**Scope confirmation:** `git diff --stat` on `app/(dashboard)/dashboard/page.tsx` shows a large diff, but `git diff` isolated to the header-relevant lines shows only the one import swap (`PageHeader` → `LiveDashboardHeader`) and the one JSX call site swap — every other line in that diff is pre-existing, already-uncommitted work from other in-progress units on the same file (dashboard KPI card logic), untouched by this change. No schema, auth, dashboard data-query, permission, or workflow logic touched; sidebar/top navbar/notification badge/dashboard cards/quick actions all untouched (confirmed — nothing below the header render point was edited).

**Files changed:** `components/dashboard/live-dashboard-header.tsx` (new); `app/(dashboard)/dashboard/page.tsx` (import + one JSX call site).

**Validation:** `npm run db:check` ✓, `lint` ✓ (0 errors, including the two changed files specifically re-checked after the set-state-in-effect fix), `typecheck` ✓ (0 errors), `build` ✓ (exit 0, all routes compiled). Verification was code-inspection-based — no live browser session was available this unit to visually confirm the typing animation, clock ticking, or absence of a hydration-warning console message, so those remain to be eyeballed once someone is at a live session; the underlying pattern (stable fallback until mount, effect-driven update after) is the standard hydration-safe approach and is what was implemented. Per the task's explicit instruction, `npm run test:e2e` was **not** run this unit. No deployment performed.

## Unit 10G.20B — Dashboard Clock Placement Correction

**Requirement:** Unit 10G.20 Revised put the clock strip at `justify-end`, pinning it to the far right of the header — the user reported (via a screenshot) that this reads as disconnected from the greeting below it, and asked for the clock to instead sit left-aligned, directly above the greeting's own text, inside the same empty top strip.

**Root cause:** the top-strip wrapper div used `className="flex justify-end"`, which pushes its only child (the clock box) to the far-right edge of the header's content width. There was no `ml-auto`/absolute-right/grid-right-column trick involved — just that one `justify-end` utility — so the fix was a single alignment-class change plus a left offset to match the greeting's own text position, not a structural rewrite.

**Task 1/2/4 — Alignment fix:** `components/dashboard/live-dashboard-header.tsx`'s clock-strip wrapper changed from `flex justify-end` to `flex pl-5`. `pl-5` = 20px = exactly `border-l-4` (4px) + `pl-4` (16px), the same two values the greeting block below uses for its own red accent bar + text padding — so the clock box's left edge now lines up with where the `<h1>` greeting text itself starts, not with the accent bar's own left edge. No `ml-auto`, absolute positioning, or grid column was ever added, so Task 4's "remove any right-positioning trick" required removing only the one `justify-end` class.

**Task 3 — Clock design unchanged:** white background, subtle border, rounded corners, small icon, bold `tabular-nums` time, muted date, compact sizing — all exactly as Unit 10G.20 Revised left them; only the internal text alignment (`text-right` → default/left, since the box no longer needs its two lines flush against a right edge) was adjusted to match the box's new left-aligned position. Not full width, no animation — untouched.

**Task 5 — Header spacing unchanged:** no padding values were touched in this unit (Unit 10G.20 Revised's `pb-4 pt-3 sm:pb-6 sm:pt-4` outer padding stays as-is) — this was purely a horizontal alignment fix, not a height change, so Today Summary's vertical position is unaffected.

**Task 6 — Responsive:** `pl-5` applies at every breakpoint (no `sm:`/`lg:` variant needed) — the clock stays left-aligned with the greeting content on desktop, tablet, and mobile alike, still stacked above the greeting by construction (its own row, unconditionally). Re-checked the same 320–375px width budget as Unit 10G.20 Revised: the clock box (~170px) plus a 20px left offset comes to ~190px, still comfortably under the ~290px available inside the header's own horizontal padding — no horizontal overflow.

**Task 7 — Applies to every dashboard role:** same single shared `LiveDashboardHeader` call site in `app/(dashboard)/dashboard/page.tsx` — Data Entry and Manager both pick up the corrected alignment automatically. Sidebar, top navbar, notification bell, role badge, logout, dashboard cards, and quick actions are all outside this file and were not touched.

**Files changed:** `components/dashboard/live-dashboard-header.tsx` only.

**Validation:** `npm run db:check` ✓, `lint` ✓, `typecheck` ✓, `build` ✓ (62 routes). No deployment performed.

## Phase ManagerClosureEstimatedActualLaborTransparency-10G.21 — Manager Closure Review Estimated vs Actual Labor Transparency Unit 10G.21 — COMPLETE

**Task 1 finding:** Unit 10G.13 (still uncommitted/untracked in this working tree — `lib/work-orders/hours-variance.ts` and `scripts/verify-estimated-work-hours-unit10g13.mjs` both show as `??` in `git status`, never `git add`ed) had already built almost this entire unit: `work_orders.estimated_labor_hours` and `work_order_worker_assignments.estimated_hours` (both additive nullable `Decimal(12,2)`, confirmed present in `prisma/schema.prisma`), the shared `computeHoursVariance`/`hoursVarianceTone` classifier, the New Job Card wizard's estimate-entry UI (Task 2 — verified intact, not duplicated), and Estimated/Actual/Variance displays on the Job Card detail page, Daily Activity, Closure Review, Closed Jobs, and Worker Activity. This unit's real work was: (a) one genuine gap in the variance classifier itself, (b) one missing surface (Closure Requests list row), and (c) a consistency gap across every existing "Estimated vs Actual" display where a missing estimate hid Actual Hours entirely instead of still showing it.

**Task 5 — Under Estimate status, plus a real floating-point bug found while adding it:** `computeHoursVariance` only had 4 states (No Estimate/On Track/Slightly Over/Over Estimate) — "actual < estimated * 0.8" fell into On Track. Added `"under_estimate"` (amber tone, same as Slightly Over, per this unit's explicit color rule), checked before On Track since its range is a subset of "actual <= estimated." While testing the exact boundary (estimated=6, actual=4.8 = exactly 0.8×) the check failed: `6 * 0.8 === 4.800000000000001` in JS floating point, so an exact-boundary Job Card would have been misclassified as Under Estimate instead of On Track. Fixed by rounding both threshold multiplications to 2dp (this app's standard hours precision) before comparing — a real correctness fix, not just a test adjustment, verified via `scripts/verify-estimated-work-hours-unit10g13.mjs` (extended with explicit boundary/tone checks for the new status, all passing, including a real DB round-trip, rolled back).

## Unit 10G.20C — Dashboard Clock Final Placement Fix

**Requirement:** the user reported Unit 10G.20B's clock as still wrong — too small/quiet to register as sitting "in" the top strip, prompting a rebuild focused on visual weight rather than position. Structure itself (own top strip above the greeting, left-aligned, never far right, never below the strip) was already correct from 10G.20B; this unit makes the clock box bigger, bolder, and more premium so it reads unmistakably as a deliberate widget in the top-left of the header.

**Root cause of previous wrong placement:** by this unit, the *positioning* (own row above the greeting, `pl-5` left offset matching the greeting's own text start) was already correct — 10G.20B had already fixed the `justify-end` far-right bug. What remained wrong was purely visual weight: a small icon (`h-3.5 w-3.5`), small time text (`text-sm`), tight padding (`px-3 py-1.5`), and a muted `text-[11px]` date made the box easy to visually miss or misread as "below"/disconnected from the strip, even though it was structurally correct. No further structural bug was found — this was a pure sizing/styling deficiency, confirmed by re-reading the rendered JSX tree rather than guessing.

**Task 1/2 — Structure confirmed, not changed:** the outer `<div className="flex pl-5">` top strip and the `mt-3 border-l-4 ... pl-4` greeting block below it are unchanged from 10G.20B — still no `justify-end`, `ml-auto`, absolute right positioning, or grid right-column trick anywhere in the file.

**Task 3 — Visual rebuild:** clock box grown and restyled: `rounded-md`→`rounded-xl`, padding `px-3 py-1.5`→`px-4 py-3 sm:px-5 sm:py-3.5`, `gap-2`→`gap-2.5 sm:gap-3`, kept `border-[#E5E7EB]`/`bg-white`/`shadow-sm` (still a "light shadow", not heavy). The bare gray `ClockIcon` (`h-3.5 w-3.5 text-[#9CA3AF]`) was replaced with a red icon badge (`h-9 w-9 sm:h-10 sm:w-10 rounded-lg bg-red-50 text-[#ED1C24]`, icon `h-4 w-4 sm:h-5 sm:w-5`) — the same icon-badge pattern `QuickActionCard` already uses elsewhere on this dashboard, so it reads as an intentional, on-brand widget rather than a plain inline icon. Time text `text-sm`→`text-xl sm:text-2xl` (kept `font-mono font-black tabular-nums`, now genuinely bold/prominent per the visual-hierarchy spec). Date text `text-[11px]`→`text-xs sm:text-sm` plus `font-medium` (secondary but clearly readable, no longer near-illegible).

**Task 4 — Live behavior confirmed unchanged:** zero edits to any `useState`/`useEffect`/`setInterval` in the component — the clock tick, the hydration-safe pre-mount fallback, and the time-based greeting logic are byte-for-byte what 10G.18 first wrote. Re-verified via hex dump that the fallback date placeholder is still the same non-breaking-space character (`c2 a0`/U+00A0), not a plain space, after two separate `sed`-based edits to that same line's class list (the Edit tool's exact-string matching kept failing against that invisible character, same issue first diagnosed in Unit 10G.20 Revised).

**Task 5 — Header spacing:** outer container padding (`pb-4 pt-3 sm:pb-6 sm:pt-4`) left unchanged; only the clock box's own internal padding/font sizes grew. The box is taller than 10G.20B's version (bigger text needs more line-height), which is an intentional, requested trade-off — Today Summary's position shifts down by roughly the height difference between the old and new clock box (a few tens of pixels), not by a new block of empty padding.

**Task 6 — Responsive:** badge/icon/time/date/gap/padding all step up at `sm:` (icon badge `h-9 w-9`→`sm:h-10 sm:w-10`, time `text-xl`→`sm:text-2xl`, date `text-xs`→`sm:text-sm`, padding/gap similarly), so mobile gets a slightly smaller but still clearly "important" box, matching Task 6's "can reduce slightly but should still feel important." Re-checked the width budget at a 320px viewport: badge + gap + text column + horizontal padding + the `pl-5`/`px-4` offsets comes to roughly 270px against ~304px of available content width — fits with margin to spare, no horizontal overflow.

**Task 7 — Applies to every dashboard role:** same single shared `LiveDashboardHeader` call site in `app/(dashboard)/dashboard/page.tsx` — Data Entry and Manager both inherit the corrected, enlarged clock automatically. Sidebar, top navbar, notification bell, role badge, logout, dashboard cards, and quick actions are all outside this file and were not touched.

## Unit 10G.20D — Top Navbar Clock Placement

**Requirement:** the clock (now visually solid after 10G.20C) was still inside the dashboard-only greeting header, so it only ever appeared on `/dashboard` and above the greeting. The user asked for it to move into the shared app top bar instead — same horizontal row as the role badge, notification bell, user avatar/name, and logout button — so it's visible globally, on the left side of that row, while the existing right-side controls stay exactly where they are.

**Root cause of previous wrong placement:** not a bug in 10G.20C's styling — the clock was simply living in the wrong component. `components/dashboard/live-dashboard-header.tsx` is rendered only from `app/(dashboard)/dashboard/page.tsx`, so no amount of resizing/repositioning inside that component could ever put the clock in the same row as the top bar's role badge/bell/user/logout, which live in a structurally different component (`components/layout/app-layout.tsx`'s `<header>`) that renders on every authenticated page. Fixing this required moving the clock to a new component, not another layout tweak within the old one.

**Task 1/2 — Extraction:** created `components/layout/live-top-clock.tsx` (`"use client"`), holding just the clock's own state (`now`), 1-second `setInterval` tick, and hydration-safe `"--:--:--"` pre-mount fallback — copied verbatim from the greeting header's prior clock logic, with the greeting/typing-effect state left behind. `components/dashboard/live-dashboard-header.tsx` was rewritten to remove all clock state (`now`), the `formatClock` helper, the `ClockIcon` import, and the clock JSX/top-strip wrapper entirely — it now renders only the red-accent greeting `<h1>` + subtitle, with its outer padding restored to the pre-clock `py-4 sm:py-6` (no more top-strip gap to reserve). The greeting/typing-effect `useState`/`useEffect` logic is otherwise byte-for-byte unchanged from Unit 10G.18.

**Task 3/4 — Placed in the shared top bar:** `components/layout/app-layout.tsx`'s `<header>` changed `justify-end` → `justify-between` and gained `<LiveTopClock />` as the first child, immediately before the existing right-side controls `<div>` (role badge/bell/user/logout — untouched). Styled to match the header's ~64px (`min-h-16`) row: icon badge `h-8 w-8 sm:h-9 sm:w-9` (smaller than 10G.20C's dashboard version, since it now sits beside 36px-tall controls rather than alone in its own strip), time `text-sm sm:text-base font-black tabular-nums`, date `text-[10px]` — kept white background, subtle border, light shadow, rounded corners, and the same red icon-badge treatment as 10G.20C.

**Task 5 — Header spacing:** removing the clock's dedicated top strip from the dashboard greeting (restoring `py-4 sm:py-6`) means the greeting now sits at exactly its pre-10G.20-series height — no leftover blank space, and Today Summary's vertical position is back to where it was before this whole clock-placement series started.

**Task 6 — Responsive:** the clock's date line is `hidden sm:block` — below the `sm` breakpoint the top bar shows only the bold time in a compact badge, exactly matching the task's "show only time in compact form... hide date below sm" recommendation, so it never crowds the role badge/bell/user-icon/logout controls at narrow widths. Confirmed via `components/layout/mobile-navigation.tsx` that the mobile bottom nav/drawer is fixed to the viewport's bottom/right edges — nothing in the header's own left region was already using that space.

**Task 9 — Notification/user controls confirmed unaffected:** `NotificationBell`, the profile link/avatar, and the `signOutAction` logout form are the exact same JSX nodes, just now siblings of `<LiveTopClock />` instead of the header's only children — no props, hrefs, or actions changed. `RealtimeConnectionProvider`, `NotificationToastCenter`, and `CriticalWorkflowPopup` are declared outside `<header>` entirely and were not touched.

**A lint fix along the way:** the greeting header's rewritten mount effect originally called `setGreeting`/`setMounted` directly at the top of the `useEffect` body (now that there was no `tick`/`setInterval` wrapper needed for the clock, which moved out) — `eslint-plugin-react-hooks`'s `set-state-in-effect` rule flagged this as "calling setState synchronously within an effect." Fixed by wrapping the two calls in a local `resolveGreeting` function invoked once, matching this codebase's existing lint-clean pattern (the same shape the removed clock tick used).

**Files changed:** `components/layout/live-top-clock.tsx` (new); `components/layout/app-layout.tsx`; `components/dashboard/live-dashboard-header.tsx`.

## Unit 10H.1 — Performance, Reliability & Stability Optimization Review

**Requirement:** a system-wide performance/reliability review before the maintenance team starts using the app — explicitly not a redesign or feature unit. Full detail in `context/performance-review.md`.

**Method:** five parallel read-only research passes covered Dashboard/realtime/timers, Daily Activity/Job Cards list, Job Card detail, Inventory Control/Worker Activity, and Prisma schema/backend helpers, each findings-checked against source before any fix.

**Headline finding:** most of the app already went through prior deliberate performance passes (Unit 3 indexes, the Enterprise Real-Time Update Foundation's single shared SSE connection, Daily Activity's Unit 9 Task 11 N+1 fix, Worker Activity's bulk-summary helpers). The Job Card detail page is the one page still loading its full ~15-relation include tree upfront regardless of active tab, re-run on every AutoRefresh(20s)/SSE refresh — documented as a proposed phased lazy-loading follow-up rather than restructured in this unit (that's a real architecture change, out of scope for a performance pass).

**Fixes applied (all low-risk, behavior-preserving):**
1. N+1 fix in `editMaterialsRequest()` (`lib/backend/parts-requests/service.ts`) — per-item `findUnique` validation batched into one `findMany` before the update loop.
2. QR SVG generation (`lib/qr/svg.ts`) cached in-memory by target URL — was regenerating identical content on every Job Card detail page refresh.
3. `hooks/use-auto-refresh.ts` switched to the shared `isSafeToRefresh()` guard (`lib/realtime/refresh-guards.ts`) — it previously had its own local typing check and, unlike `useRealtimeEvents`, never checked `isModalOpen()`, so it could refresh a page out from under an open modal.
4. Two independent sequential awaits in the Job Cards list's `?preview=` quick-view path (`app/(dashboard)/maintenance/work-orders/page.tsx`) parallelized via `Promise.all`.
5. `lib/realtime/refresh-guards.ts` given defensive `typeof document === "undefined"` guards (previously relied only on a doc-comment convention).
6. Additive index migration `20260811010000_performance_review_unit10h1_indexes` — `work_order_work_sessions(started_at)` and `(worker_id, started_at)`, justified by `getWorkerActivitySummaries()`/`getWorkerActivityDetail()`/`getLaborPeriodTotals()` all filtering/sorting an append-only, ever-growing table on those previously-unindexed fields. Applied to local dev DB via `prisma migrate deploy`; `prisma validate` and `prisma migrate status` both clean.

**Everything else reviewed and found already fine (not touched):** Dashboard's capped per-role queries and bulk materials/labor lookups (no per-card N+1); Daily Activity's capped list, selection-scoped `LiveTimer`s, and bulk fulfillment/labor helpers; Job Cards list's single `groupBy` status counts and paginated (`take: 25`) query; Inventory Control's SQL-side `groupBy`/`_sum` balance query and lazy movement-history modal; Worker Activity's 4-query-total bulk summary helper and lazy detail modal; the single shared `EventSource`/SSE connection with debounce and cleanup on every consumer; `live-top-clock.tsx`/`live-timer.tsx` interval cleanup; `prefers-reduced-motion` handling in the dashboard's typing effect.

**Follow-up flagged, not implemented this unit:** Job Card detail's per-tab lazy loading (own unit); `store-balance-view.tsx` and the Worker Activity list's client-side filtering over a capped-but-unbounded list (fine at current scale); consolidating per-worker `LiveTimer` intervals into one shared tick (fine at current concurrent-worker counts); a `take` cap on `getSessionsForAssignment()`; a dedicated Task 11 error-boundary/double-submit-guard pass.

**Files changed:** `lib/backend/parts-requests/service.ts`; `lib/qr/svg.ts`; `hooks/use-auto-refresh.ts`; `lib/realtime/refresh-guards.ts`; `app/(dashboard)/maintenance/work-orders/page.tsx`; `prisma/schema.prisma`; `prisma/migrations/20260811010000_performance_review_unit10h1_indexes/migration.sql` (new); `context/performance-review.md` (new).

**Validation:** `npm run db:check` ✓, `prisma validate` ✓, `lint` ✓ (0 errors), `typecheck` ✓, `build` ✓ (62 routes — Turbopack compile 19.5s, TS check 36.4s, no errors/warnings). `npm run start` isn't a defined script in this repo; smoke-tested with `next start` on an alternate port instead — unauthenticated requests to protected routes redirect in well under 10ms, confirming the auth guard short-circuits before any DB work. Full authenticated page-load timing across modules was not measured (requires a logged-in session) and is deferred to the E2E/manual verification pass explicitly scoped for after this unit. Per the task's explicit instruction, `npm run test:e2e` was **not** run. No business workflow, approval logic, material receive/issue logic, worker time calculation, or permission change. No destructive schema change — one additive, `IF NOT EXISTS` index migration only. No new dependencies, no new polling loop, no new EventSource/WebSocket. No deployment performed.

## Unit 10G.22 — Job Card Estimated Hours UX Simplification

**Requirement:** Data Entry saw a "Estimated total work hours" field on New Job Card wizard Step 3 before any worker was even picked — Manager flagged this as confusing (Data Entry can't know a meaningful total before workers are selected) and asked for estimated hours to be entered only per selected worker, with the Job Card total calculated automatically as their sum.

**Task 1/3/4 — top field removed, total now computed:** the manual "Estimated total work hours" input (label/placeholder/helper, `components/work-orders/work-order-wizard.tsx`'s old `estimatedTotalHours` state) is gone from Step 3. A new plain `const` block (`estimateSelectedIds`/`enteredWorkerEstimates`/`totalEstimatedHours`, computed in the wizard's render body next to the existing `reviewParts` const) derives the total from whichever Internal Team workers are currently selected and have a non-blank, valid, non-negative estimate typed — recomputed on every render, never stored as its own state. It's carried to the backend via one always-present hidden `<input type="hidden" name="estimated_labor_hours">` (previously the visible field's own name/slot). Server-side, `app/actions/maintenance.ts`'s `upsertWorkOrderAction` doesn't trust that hidden field for the wizard's Internal Team create path — a new `sumWorkerEstimates()` helper re-derives the same sum straight from `parseWizardAssignment`'s already-parsed `estimatedHoursByWorkerId`, and overrides `values.estimated_labor_hours` with it (`undefined`, not `0`, when nothing was entered — never blocks saving). This override only fires when `!id && wizardAssignment?.kind === "INTERNAL_TEAM"`, so it's a no-op for edits and for the separate standalone edit form (`work-order-form.tsx`, untouched — no worker picker there, still submits its own manual `estimated_labor_hours` field as before, out of this unit's scope).

**Task 2 — worker-level input unchanged in shape, simplified in behavior:** `SelectedWorkersEstimateList` (still "Estimated hours per selected worker", one input per selected worker) dropped the old "suggested equal split" placeholder and the "worker estimates total X h, Job Card estimate is Y h" mismatch warning — both existed only to reconcile worker estimates against a manually-typed total that no longer exists. `InternalTeamWizardFields`/`SelectedWorkersEstimateList` no longer take an `estimatedTotalHours`/`totalEstimateHours` prop at all.

**Task 5 — Review & Save shows it as calculated:** a new "Estimated Labor" `ReviewSection` (Step 6, right after "Assignment") shows "Total estimated hours: X h" plus one line per worker with an entered estimate, using the same `totalEstimatedHours`/`enteredWorkerEstimates` consts — or "Estimated labor: Not recorded" when nothing was entered. No input, purely a read of already-computed state.

**Task 6 — Manager Closure Review fallback:** a new `resolveEstimatedTotalHours(workOrderTotal, workerEstimates[])` in `lib/work-orders/hours-variance.ts` (the existing client-safe shared classifier module) returns the Job Card's saved total when present, else the sum of its workers' own `estimated_hours` — needed because `lib/backend/work-orders/worker-roster.ts`'s roster-edit path (post-creation "Assign Workers") never recomputes the Job Card-level total, only per-worker estimates, so a Job Card assigned/re-assigned after creation could otherwise show a stale/missing total even with real worker estimates on file. ## Unit 10G.23 — Unified Material Processing Flow

**Requirement:** Daily Activity's material workflow forced Data Entry through a confusing three-step dance on a mixed Job Card (some materials already in stock, others new/short) — "Issue Available", then "Receive Materials", then "Issue Available" again. Replace it with one "Process Materials" action: review every required material line, receive whatever's short, then issue everything remaining, in a single confirmed step.

**Task 1/9 — one action, simple wording:** Daily Activity's per-card next-action/materials-mini-section button collapses to a single "Process Materials" label whenever a Job Card has `work_order_required_parts` rows with `remaining_qty > 0` and the actor holds both existing gates (`canManageOfflineInventory` + `canReceiveIssueMaterials` — no new permission, per Task 12). The helper message under it is one of Task 1's three exact examples, chosen from the same job-card-level `summarizeMaterialAvailability()` rollup Daily Activity already computed (`app/(dashboard)/maintenance/daily-activity/page.tsx`). Per-line status badges keep Unit 10G.14's existing vocabulary (Fully Issued / Ready to Issue / Partially Available / Needs Receiving) — the job-card-level chip labels (Materials Pending / Ready to Issue / Partially Available / Materials Completed) were left untouched since they're read by filters and several other pages; only the action/button layer was simplified.

**Task 2/3/4 — the modal:** `ProcessMaterialsModal` (rewrite of `components/work-orders/daily-activity-materials-modal.tsx`, replacing the old `IssueMaterialModal`/`ReceiveMaterialsModal` pair — confirmed via grep they had no other consumers) fetches the existing `getJobCardMaterialsModalDataAction` (unchanged) and groups its `fulfillment` rows into "Ready to Issue" / "Need Receiving" (covers both partial and zero-stock lines — same next step either way) / "Already Completed", each row showing Required/Available/Issued/Remaining plus the receive and issue quantities already computed by `getMaterialFulfillmentForWorkOrder`. One "Confirm & Process Materials" button calls the new `processJobCardMaterialsAction`.

**Task 5 — backend orchestration:** new `lib/backend/work-orders/material-processing.ts` exports `processJobCardMaterials(context, workOrderId)`, run inside `withBackendTransaction`. It writes directly against `work_order_required_parts` + `offline_inventory_movements` — deliberately bypassing `parts_request_items` for the writes themselves, so the real required unit (`work_order_required_parts.unit_of_measure`) is always used, never the hardcoded-"PCS" fallback Unit 10G.14 had to work around on the older per-item receive path. For every line with `remaining_qty > 0`: an advisory lock on its balance identity, a fresh balance/issued read, a `RECEIVED` movement for the shortage (skipped when there is none), then an `ISSUED` movement for the full remaining requirement. Reuses the existing `syncPartsRequestStatusAfterFullIssueInTx` (not a hand-rolled duplicate) so the linked Materials Request's status and the Job Card's legacy status field transition exactly as they already do after a direct Offline Inventory issue.

**Task 6 — idempotency:** the button disables while processing, but the real guard is server-side — each candidate line re-reads its balance/issued total inside its own advisory lock immediately before writing, so a line already fulfilled since the outer snapshot is silently skipped (never double-issued, never double-received). A second call with nothing left to do returns `receivedCount: 0, issuedCount: 0`, message "No remaining materials to process.", and creates zero new movements — verified directly (see below).

**Task 7/8 — new materials and partial availability:** both go through the same single loop as existing-stock lines; a brand-new material simply has no movement history, so `available_now` is 0 and its full `remaining_qty` becomes the receive quantity. Task 8's exact worked example (required 10, already issued 3, available 4, remaining 7 → receive 3, issue 7) is covered by the verification script's line 3.

**Task 11 — audit trail:** every RECEIVED/ISSUED movement created carries `purpose`, `counterparty`, `related_work_order_id`, and `created_by`, same as every other Receive/Issue surface in the app — no new movement type, no bypassed history. Movement History (`/store/offline-inventory/movements`) was not touched and shows these rows like any other.

**Task 12 — permissions/scope confirmed unchanged:** no new permission key added; Inventory Control (`/store/offline-inventory`) was not touched and still has no Receive/Issue action cards. Only Daily Activity's own files were touched — the Job Card detail page's separate Materials tab (Unit 10G.14's Issue Available/Receive Shortage per-row actions) is out of scope (the request is specifically titled "Simplify Daily Activity material workflow").

**Files changed:** `lib/backend/work-orders/material-processing.ts` (new); `app/actions/daily-activity-materials.ts` (added `processJobCardMaterialsAction`); `components/work-orders/daily-activity-materials-modal.tsx` (rewritten — `ProcessMaterialsModal` replaces `IssueMaterialModal`/`ReceiveMaterialsModal`); `components/work-orders/daily-activity-board.tsx`; `components/work-orders/daily-activity-card.tsx` (`DailyActivitySelectedPanel` takes one `onProcessMaterials` prop instead of `onIssueMaterial`/`onReceiveMaterial`; `materialsModalAction`/`materialsSecondaryAction` fields replaced by `showProcessMaterials`); `app/(dashboard)/maintenance/daily-activity/page.tsx`; `scripts/verify-unified-material-processing-unit10g23.mjs` (new).

**Validation:** `npm run db:check` ✓, `lint` ✓ (0 errors), `typecheck` ✓, `build` ✓ (62 routes, no errors/warnings). Per the task's explicit instruction, `npm run test:e2e` was **not** run. In its place, a standalone, non-browser, rollback-based Prisma script (`scripts/verify-unified-material-processing-unit10g23.mjs`, following the existing `verify-materials-receive-status-fix.mjs`/`e2e-unit10-run.mjs` convention of mirroring real `"server-only"` service logic plus a drift check against the real source) built a mixed three-line Job Card (existing-stock, new-material, and Task 8's exact partial-availability example) inside a transaction that is always rolled back, and confirmed: correct classification pre-processing; correct RECEIVED-then-ISSUED movement counts, quantities, and units on the first call; correct audit fields; a second call on the same Job Card creates zero new movements and returns the exact no-op message (idempotency); a Closed Job Card is rejected; a Job Card with no required materials returns a clean no-op. All checks passed; confirmed zero rows left behind after rollback. No schema change. No change to Job Card creation (still never deducts inventory), Manager approval workflow, or closure workflow. No deployment performed.

## Unit 10G.24 — Daily Activity Timer Reliability and Remove Data Entry Manual Entry

**Requirement:** two independent fixes — (1) Daily Activity's live worker timer sometimes doesn't visibly tick for an Active worker, and (2) "Add Manual Entry" must be removed from Data Entry's worker cards (manual start/stop times are an unaudited way to fabricate hours never actually worked) while Manager/Super Admin correction ability stays intact.

**Investigation note:** before touching anything, a baseline `npm run typecheck` surfaced pre-existing errors from a *different*, apparently mid-flight unit ("Unified Material Processing Flow Unit 10G.23" — `daily-activity-board.tsx` calling `onProcessMaterials` against a `DailyActivitySelectedPanel` that still expected `onIssueMaterial`/`onReceiveMaterial`, plus two dangling shorthand-property references in `daily-activity/page.tsx`). Asked the user how to proceed; they said to finish wiring it forward. Before doing so, a second typecheck/lint run came back fully clean — a concurrent process (this session ran alongside the user's own active editing) had completed that exact migration in the interim, confirmed by its own progress-tracker entry immediately above this one. No work was needed from this unit for 10G.23; re-verified clean before starting the actual 10G.24 changes below.

**Root cause of the timer freeze — no single reproducible logic bug found by static reading; hardened against every plausible cause instead:** `LiveTimer` (`components/work-orders/live-timer.tsx`) already computed elapsed time from `Date.now() - startedAt` on every tick (not an incrementing counter), so it was already immune to cumulative drift, and its parent chain (`WorkerSessionRow` → `WorkTimeTracking`/`DailyActivitySelectedPanel`, both keyed by the stable `worker_assignment_id`) doesn't remount on an `AutoRefresh`/`RealtimeRefresh` `router.refresh()` tick, per `daily-activity-board.tsx`'s own (verified-true) comment. The most credible real-world cause of an intermittent "looks frozen" report is browser-level `setInterval` throttling/suspension in a backgrounded or inactive tab — well-documented Chrome/Windows behavior that this component had no defense against. Fixed defensively along every angle the task's own checklist named:
1. `live-timer.tsx` — added a `visibilitychange` listener that forces an immediate re-tick the instant the tab regains visibility, instead of waiting for the next scheduled (possibly delayed) 1s tick. Pure client-side recompute from data already held — no new request/poll/connection.
2. `worker-session-row.tsx` — `<LiveTimer>` now gets an explicit `key={worker.active_session_id ?? worker.active_session_started_at}` (the session's own DB id) instead of no key at all, so a genuinely new/resumed session (a new `WorkOrderWorkSession` row) is guaranteed a fresh, correctly-ticking instance rather than any risk of reusing stale internal state across a session boundary.

**Manual Entry removal (Task 5/6):**
- `worker-session-row.tsx` — the "Add Manual Entry" button (previously shown to anyone with `canManageSessions`, which includes Data Entry) is now also gated behind `isManager` (`super_admin` or `maintenance_manager`, computed once in `daily-activity/page.tsx` and threaded through unchanged). Start/Pause/Resume/Stop and (read-only) View Sessions are untouched for Data Entry.
- `lib/backend/work-orders/work-sessions.ts` — found and closed a real server-side gap: `addManualTimeEntry()` was gated by `assertCanManageSessions` (the same broad `work_orders.assign` audience as Start/Pause/Stop, Data Entry included), unlike `editWorkSession`/`cancelWorkSession` which already used the stricter `assertIsManager`. Hiding the button alone would not have been sufficient enforcement per this codebase's own "authorization enforced in both UI and server actions" rule — changed to `assertIsManager`, matching the other two correction paths. Updated the file's own top-of-file comment, which had documented the old (now-incorrect) broader audience.
- `session-history-modal.tsx` ("View Sessions") was inspected and found **already correct** — every edit/correct/cancel control (`EditSessionForm`, `CancelSessionForm`, the "Edit / Correct"/"Cancel Session" buttons) was already wrapped in `{isManager && ...}`, and cost (`calculated_amount`/KWD) was already gated by the separate `canViewCosts` flag. No changes needed there — Task 7 was already satisfied.
- Confirmed untouched and unaffected: Manager Closure Review's "Correct Session" (`closure-review-modal.tsx` reuses the same unmodified `SessionHistoryModal` with `isManager` hardcoded `true`, since that whole surface is already Manager-only-gated at the action level) and Manager Worker Activity (`worker-activity-detail-modal.tsx` doesn't use `WorkerSessionRow` at all — a separate, independent view).

**Files changed:** `components/work-orders/live-timer.tsx`; `components/work-orders/worker-session-row.tsx`; `lib/backend/work-orders/work-sessions.ts`.

**Validation:** `npm run db:check` ✓, `lint` ✓ (0 errors — one transient unrelated error in a file this unit never touched appeared on one run and was gone on the next, consistent with the concurrent-editing activity noted above, not a real regression), `typecheck` ✓, `build` ✓ (62 routes, no errors/warnings). Per the task's explicit instruction, `npm run test:e2e` was **not** run. No change to worker time calculation, closure workflow, materials workflow, or permissions beyond the one intentional `addManualTimeEntry` tightening described above (which is the task's own explicit ask, not scope creep). No pay/rate/cost newly exposed to Data Entry — Cost remained gated by the pre-existing, untouched `canViewCosts` check throughout. No new polling, interval, or realtime connection — the `visibilitychange` listener is a passive DOM event subscription, not a poll. No deployment performed.

## Unit 10G.26 — Job Cards Direct Detail Navigation

**Requirement:** clicking a Job Card on the Job Cards list (`app/(dashboard)/maintenance/work-orders/page.tsx`) opened an old-style quick-view popup (`RepairOrderQuickView`, triggered by pushing `?preview=<id>` onto the list's own URL) instead of navigating to the real Job Card detail page — the Manager asked for direct navigation instead, since the popup duplicated the detail page.

**Root cause found (Task 1):** every row built a `previewHref = buildHref({ ...sp, preview: wo.id })` and used it for three things — the Job Card number `Link`, the whole row's click handler (`components/work-orders/quick-view-row.tsx`'s `QuickViewRow`, which pushes its href on any click not on a nested link/button), and the row's dynamic Action-column button (Review/Assign Workers/Mark Work Started/Close/Materials — everything except "Track Work", which already linked straight to the detail page's `#work-time-tracking` anchor). The page's final render ternary fell back to `drawerData && <RepairOrderQuickView data={drawerData} />` whenever `?preview=` was set without one of the `success=job-card-*` flags — that fallback branch was the popup.

**Task 2/3 — direct navigation, popup removed:** all three `previewHref` call sites now use a plain `detailHref = /maintenance/work-orders/${wo.id}` — the exact same route the pre-existing "Full Details" button already used. The final render ternary's `RepairOrderQuickView` fallback branch is deleted outright (→ `null`) — the popup can no longer render on this page under any click path. `RepairOrderQuickView` itself (`components/work-orders/repair-order-quick-view.tsx`) was **not** touched — it's still used, unchanged, by the Dashboard (`app/(dashboard)/dashboard/page.tsx`) and Materials Requests (`app/(dashboard)/store/parts-requests/page.tsx`) pages. Its `QuickViewData` type is still imported here (type-only now) since `JobCardOpenedModal`/`JobCardSubmittedModal` — two unrelated, unchanged success-confirmation modals (see below) — still take that shape. `QuickViewRow` (only ever used on this one page, confirmed by repo-wide search) was kept rather than deleted — its "whole row clickable except nested links/buttons" mechanic is exactly what Task 2 still wants, just pointed at a different href now; its prop was renamed `previewHref` → `href` since the old name was actively misleading post-fix (single call site, zero external risk).

**Task 4 — Full Details and other buttons preserved:** "Full Details" was already a direct `Link` to the detail route and is unchanged. Create Job Card, Daily Activity (via `PageNavigationActions`), Materials Requests link, status tabs, KPI cards, search/filter form, and the print button are all untouched — none of them ever used `previewHref`.

**Task 5/6 — scope confirmed:** the CEO variant of this same page (`CeoWorkOrderTable`, the early-return block for `role.slug === "ceo_management"`) was already linking every row straight to `/maintenance/work-orders/${wo.id}` — it never used the popup and needed no change. Nothing under `components/dashboard/` (Manager Closure Review, Critical Workflow popup, notification popups, Materials Processing modal, Attachment Preview modal) was touched. The Job Card detail page's own "Next Action" panel (`app/(dashboard)/maintenance/work-orders/[id]/page.tsx`, `id="next-action"`, Overview tab) already reproduces every action the popup used to offer inline — Submit/Approve/Edit/Mark-Started forms directly for Created/Under Review, and buttons that jump to Assignment/Work Time Tracking/Materials/Closure for every other status — so nothing the popup did is lost by removing it; a Manager or Data Entry landing on the detail page after clicking a row sees the same "what do I do next" guidance the popup used to show, just as a real page instead of an overlay.

**Not touched, deliberately:** the `previewId`/`drawerData` query block (previewed Job Card + linked Materials Requests + technician picker options + material fulfillment) still exists and still runs — but now only when `sp.preview || sp.created` is actually set, which after this change only happens via the post-creation redirect (`app/actions/maintenance.ts`'s `upsertWorkOrderAction`, `?created=<id>&preview=<id>&success=job-card-created`) or the approve/submit-success redirects (`?success=job-card-opened`/`job-card-submitted&preview=<id>`) — never from a plain row click any more. `JobCardCreatedModal`/`JobCardOpenedModal`/`JobCardSubmittedModal` (the three success-confirmation modals shown right after creating/approving/submitting a Job Card) are unrelated to the removed quick-view popup and were not touched — this satisfies the stated performance goal ("removing the preview modal should reduce unnecessary preview loading") as a side effect: that query block no longer runs on a normal list-browsing page load at all.

## Unit 10G.29 — Attachment Preview URL Fix

**Requirement:** the Attachment Preview modal (Unit 10G.25) showed "localhost refused to connect" when previewing an uploaded PDF — reported as a URL-generation bug that would also break on the deployed server (`http://192.168.1.17:81`).

**Root cause found — not a URL bug:** every attachment URL in this codebase was already traced and confirmed correct before any fix was made: `attachment.viewUrl` (`app/actions/closure-requests.ts`) comes from `createSignedFileUrl()` (`lib/files/signed-url.ts`), which has only ever returned a same-origin **relative** path (`/api/files/${bucket}/${path}`) — no `localhost`, no `NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL`, no `window.location.origin`, anywhere in the attachment preview/closure-review code path (a repo-wide search for all four confirmed the only real hits are unrelated: `lib/qr/svg.ts`'s QR-code target — QR codes legitimately need an absolute, externally-scannable URL, a different problem — and one throwaway `new URL(path, "http://localhost")` in `app/actions/workflow.ts` used purely to reuse `URLSearchParams`, whose fake origin is discarded before the result is ever returned). The actual cause: `next.config.ts`'s `headers()` applied `X-Frame-Options: DENY` to **every** route via a single `source: "/(.*)"` rule — including `app/api/files/[bucket]/[...path]/route.ts`, the exact route the PDF `<iframe>` loads from. `X-Frame-Options: DENY` blocks a resource from being framed by **any** page, even a same-origin one belonging to the same app — and Chrome's specific rendering for a frame blocked this way is literally "<host> refused to connect," which is what produced the "localhost" wording locally and would have reproduced identically (with "192.168.1.17" in the message instead) on the deployed server, confirming the bug report's "will also break on deployed server" concern was correct, just for a different underlying reason than a hardcoded hostname. `<img>` tags are never subject to `X-Frame-Options` (it only governs framing contexts — `iframe`/`frame`/`object`/`embed`), which is also why the report specifically called out PDF/file preview rather than image preview.

**Task 2/3 — fix applied, no URL rewriting needed:** since every URL was already relative/same-origin, "switch to relative URLs" (the task's suggested fix) would have changed nothing — the actual fix is in `next.config.ts`: a second, more specific `headers()` rule for `source: "/api/files/:path*"` sets `X-Frame-Options: SAMEORIGIN` there, applied *after* the general `DENY` rule (Next.js applies the later-matching rule when two rules set the same header key for an overlapping path — verified empirically, see Validation). `SAMEORIGIN` still blocks every third-party site from framing or hotlinking these private files; it only additionally allows this app's *own* pages to embed them in an iframe — exactly the preview modal's use case, and inherently portable: the same-origin check is a live comparison done by the browser against whatever origin the page is actually being served from, not a hardcoded hostname, so it is correct on `localhost:3000` in dev and on `http://192.168.1.17:81` deployed without any environment-specific configuration.

**Task 4 — Open in new tab hardened:** `components/dashboard/attachment-preview-modal.tsx`'s three `<Link href={attachment.viewUrl} target="_blank">` elements (the PDF fallback link, the "Open / Download" button for unsupported types, and the footer "Open in new tab" button) all already used the same correct relative `viewUrl`; each gained `rel="noopener noreferrer"` (a `target="_blank"` security best practice that was simply missing before, unrelated to the localhost bug but a safe, small hardening while touching this file).

**Task 5 — PDF preview behavior:** the `<iframe>` now loads correctly under the fixed header policy. The existing "If the PDF preview doesn't display, open it in a new tab" hint below the iframe (added in Unit 10G.25) is kept as-is rather than rewritten to the task's literal suggested wording ("Preview unavailable. Open in new tab.") — browsers do not fire any JS-observable failure event for an iframe blocked by header policy or for most in-browser PDF-plugin failures, so reliable success/failure detection isn't available; an always-visible assistive link remains the more honest, robust choice (and is now something that will actually rarely be needed, since the root blocker is fixed) rather than a message that would misleadingly claim "unavailable" for a preview that is, in fact, working.

**Task 6 — image preview behavior:** unchanged and unaffected — `<img src={attachment.viewUrl}>` was never subject to `X-Frame-Options` and never used a hardcoded origin either.

**Task 7 — other file types:** unchanged — file info + "Open / Download" button, same relative `viewUrl`, now with `rel="noopener noreferrer"` added.

**Task 8 — deployment compatibility:** confirmed empirically against both a running dev server and an actual production build (`next build` + `next start` on an alternate port) — `curl -D -` against `/api/files/...` returned `X-Frame-Options: SAMEORIGIN` in both, while an unrelated route (`/dashboard`) returned `X-Frame-Options: DENY` in both, confirming the override is scoped correctly and works identically regardless of dev vs. production mode. Nothing in the fix assumes port 3000/3100 or any specific hostname — `next.config.ts`'s `headers()` and the browser's same-origin check are both host-agnostic.

**Task 9 — auth/security unchanged:** `app/api/files/[bucket]/[...path]/route.ts` itself was not touched — the same authentication check (`getCurrentUserContext`), the same bucket+entity authorization checks (`canAccessWorkOrder`/`canAccessAsset`/`canAccessPurchaseRequest`), and the same audit logging are all exactly as before. `X-Frame-Options: SAMEORIGIN` is a *framing* policy, not an access-control mechanism — it has no effect on who can authenticate or which files a given user can read; a request to `/api/files/...` without a valid session still redirects to `/login` exactly as before (confirmed in the same curl checks above), and a request for a file outside the caller's authorized entities still 404s exactly as before (unchanged code).

**Files changed:** `next.config.ts`; `components/dashboard/attachment-preview-modal.tsx`.

**Validation:** `npm run db:check` ✓, `lint` ✓ (0 errors), `typecheck` ✓, `build` ✓ (62 routes, no errors/warnings). Additionally verified live (beyond the standard four commands, since this fix is a header-policy change): `curl -D -` against the running dev server and against a real `next build`/`next start` production instance both confirmed `X-Frame-Options: SAMEORIGIN` on `/api/files/...` and `X-Frame-Options: DENY` on an unrelated route (`/dashboard`), and that unauthenticated requests to the file route still redirect to `/login` exactly as before. Per the task's explicit instruction, `npm run test:e2e` was **not** run. No change to upload storage structure, attachment database schema, closure workflow, or approval logic. No private file was exposed outside authenticated access — the file route's own auth/authorization checks are untouched; only the framing (`X-Frame-Options`) policy for that one route changed, and only to same-origin. No deployment performed.
