## Unit 10G.34 — Asset Register Import Mapping and New Asset Form Update

**Requirement:** the maintenance team's Excel workbook actually holds two distinct blocks in its "assets equipment" sheet — a clean, fully-typed 171-row block (rows 8–178), then a ~28-row blank gap, then a separate 7-row leftover/scrapped tail (no Asset Type at all, remarks like "secrap") that Unit 10G.31A had previously pulled in via Make-text inference, landing on 178. This unit re-scopes to "the current 171," rebuilds the Import Excel feature and the New/Edit Asset forms around the Excel's own field names (Asset Type, Make, Model/Year, Plate No., Chassis No., Colour, File No., Department/Location, Responsible Person/Driver, Remarks), and adds a guarded "Replace Asset Register" mode to the UI importer.

**Root-cause fix for the row-count discrepancy:** `lib/assets/asset-excel-mapping.ts` (new, shared between the CLI script and the UI action) parses every row after the header, but stops entirely at the first jump in row number greater than 5 once at least one data row has been read — a generic "end of the current list" detector, not a hardcoded row range, so it will keep working if the file's row count shifts slightly later. First attempt tracked blank rows via a streak counter inside the `eachRow` callback and produced 178, not 171 — traced to `ws.eachRow({ includeEmpty: false })` never invoking its callback at all for a truly empty row (so there was nothing to count); fixed by detecting the gap from the jump in the reported `rowNum` between successive callback calls instead. Verified against the real file: 171 rows, ending at row 178, zero rows needing review (all 171 have a real, mapped Asset Type).

**Task 1/5/6/7/8 — Shared mapping module:** `lib/assets/asset-excel-mapping.ts` holds `parseAssetsSheet()` (the full per-row parse + asset-code generation), `findDuplicates()`, the Asset Type → leaf-category map, and all cell/date parsing helpers — imported by both `app/actions/asset-import.ts` (via the `@/...` alias, inside the Next.js app) and `scripts/replace-assets-from-excel.mjs` (via a relative path; Node's built-in TypeScript stripping runs the file directly, the same pattern this repo's `verify-*.mjs` scripts already use), so the browser import and the CLI script can never disagree on what a row means. Task 5's "blank/unclear Asset Type → Needs Review, never hidden, never silently 'Other'" is implemented as `resolveCategory()`'s fallback (a real `Needs Review` category, auto-created under "Other" the first time it's actually needed) — it doesn't fire on this particular file (the 171-row current block has no blank types), but it's exercised and correct. Task 7's exact-text preservation was spot-checked against a plate number containing a literal backslash (`"5\5594"`) — survives untouched through `blankIfPlaceholder()` (trim only).

**Task 4 — Asset codes regenerated with the task's own exact token list:** `AST-{TYPE}-{0000}`, sequential per type in sheet order — `CAR, GEN, BOBCAT, CRANE, TRAILER, FORKLIFT, PICKUP, BUS, COMP, HLORRY, TANKER, TLIGHT, WELD, MANLIFT, LOADER, REVIEW`. This supersedes Unit 10G.31A's token choices for two types the task explicitly renamed: "Half Lory" now gets its own `Half Lorry` category/`HLORRY` token (previously folded into a generic `Truck`), and Tower Light's token shortened from `TOWERLIGHT` to `TLIGHT`. Since this is a full replace, no existing codes needed migrating — they were regenerated fresh on import.

**Task 2/3/14 — Import Excel feature rebuilt:** `app/actions/asset-import.ts` fully replaced (old generic Asset Code/Category/Brand/Condition/Criticality importer removed) with `parseAssetExcelForImportAction` (parse + preview, using the shared mapping — auto-selects the "assets equipment" sheet by name, falls back to the first non-"CRANES" sheet), `addAssetsFromExcelAction` (adds only, skips existing codes/plates/chassis — the action a plain upload click runs), and `replaceAssetRegisterAction` (the guarded full-replace transaction, same dependency-ordered cleanup as Unit 10G.31A's script). `components/assets/asset-import-form.tsx` rewritten for simple messaging (Task 2's exact examples — "171 assets found," row-level "Needs Review"/"Duplicate" badges, "Import completed successfully.") and a "Replace Asset Register" checkbox that reveals the task's exact warning text plus a type-to-confirm ("REPLACE") field before its button becomes clickable (Task 3 — "do not accidentally delete assets on normal upload click"). `app/(dashboard)/assets/import/page.tsx`'s guidance text updated to match (dropped the old "must use one of Car/Pickup/Bus/Truck/Loader/Forklift/Crane" categories block, which no longer reflected the real 15-type list).

**Task 9/10 — Assets & Equipment page:** the "Asset Categories" main/sub card grid (from Unit 10G.32A) and the manager-only Main Category/Subcategory columns and filters are gone — replaced by one flat "Asset Types" list (No. / Asset Type / Total Count, exactly Task 9's shape) built from the same `categoryChips` query the page already ran (no new database call — if anything, this unit removes two per-page queries, `lastRepairData`/`openRepairData`, since Task 9's column list no longer includes Last Repair). Every row and the "All Asset Types" header link filter this same page (`?category=...`) rather than navigating anywhere — including the former "Vehicles" card's special `/assets/vehicles` redirect, which is gone from the flat list (the route itself is untouched and still reachable directly, per the task's "do not delete unless safe, but don't push users into it as the main flow"). **Task 11/12/13 — New/Edit Asset forms unified:** the previous 4-step `AssetWizard` (Main Category + Subcategory pickers, Brand/Serial/Engine Number, Purchase/Warranty dates, Current KM/Running Hours, Next Service fields) is deleted — it had no remaining callers once both `/assets/new` and `/assets/[id]/edit` were switched to the new `components/assets/simple-asset-form.tsx`, a single-page form with exactly Task 11's field list (Asset Type dropdown sourced from the real, currently-used types plus "Needs Review"; Make/Asset Name required; Model/Year, File No., Colour, Plate No., Expires On, Chassis No., Department/Location, Responsible Person/Driver, Remarks, Status all optional). `asset_code` is never shown or required (Task 12) — `upsertAssetAction` (`app/actions/maintenance.ts`) now generates it server-side on create using the same `CODE_TOKEN` map the importer uses, and `brand` is always derived from Make/Asset Name (`extractBrand()`) rather than a separate field. Post-import verification (rolled-back script): 171 total, 15 distinct types matching the dry-run breakdown exactly, zero `Needs Review` rows, `profiles`/`roles`/`permissions`/`departments`/`WorkflowDefinition` (2)/`WorkflowStep` (30) all unchanged, and a simulated New Asset save (rolled back) confirmed the code-generation logic produces the correct next sequential code for an existing type.

## Unit 10G.38 — New Asset Popup and Add Asset Type

**Requirement:** "+ New Asset" on the Assets & Equipment page opened `/assets/new` as a separate, disconnected-feeling full page, and the Asset Type dropdown only ever offered existing types — a Manager with a genuinely new type of equipment had no in-flow way to add it. Turn "+ New Asset" into an in-page popup using the existing `SimpleAssetForm`, and let the popup's own Asset Type field create a brand-new type on the spot, without leaving the page or creating case/spacing duplicates.

**Task 1/2 — Popup instead of navigation, standalone route untouched:** the Assets & Equipment page's "+ New Asset" button (both header action and the empty-state variant) now links to `?new_asset=1` instead of `/assets/new`. `app/(dashboard)/assets/page.tsx` reads that flag, and — only when the current user can already manage assets — renders the existing `LargeFormModal` shell (title "New Asset", subtitle "Add a new asset to the maintenance register.") around `SimpleAssetForm`. `/assets/new` itself was not touched structurally — same page, same full-page form, still reachable and working by direct URL (Task 2's own explicit requirement); it only gained a `canAddAssetType` prop so its own dropdown gets the same "+ Add new asset type" option as the popup.

**Task 3 — Save/close/refresh/toast in one step:** `assetSchema` in `app/actions/maintenance.ts` gained one new optional field, `redirect_to`, submitted as a hidden input only when `SimpleAssetForm` is rendered with `redirectTo="/assets"` (i.e. only from the popup — the standalone New/Edit pages never set it). `upsertAssetAction` now checks, on a successful **create** only, `if (!id && redirect_to) redirect(`${redirect_to}?success=asset-added`)` before its normal `/assets/{id}?success=...` redirect — editing an existing asset is unaffected either way. Because this is a real Next.js server-side redirect (not client-side state), it closes the modal (the URL no longer has `?new_asset=1`), re-runs the Assets page's own server-side data fetch (new asset immediately counted in Total Assets, the Asset Types cards, and the Asset Register), and fires the existing `?success=asset-added` → "Asset added successfully." toast (`lib/action-messages.ts`, already present from Unit 10G.34) — all for free, no new client-side refresh/toast plumbing needed.

**Task 4/5/6 — "+ Add new asset type":** `simple-asset-form.tsx`'s plain Asset Type `<select>` is now a small client sub-component, `AssetTypeField`, that adds one sentinel option, "+ Add new asset type" (gated by a new `canAddAssetType` prop — Task 8), which opens a small inline panel (label "New Asset Type", placeholder "e.g. Water Pump", "Save Type"/"Cancel") instead of changing the dropdown's value. "Save Type" calls a new server action, `addAssetTypeAction(rawName)` in `app/actions/maintenance.ts`, directly from the client event handler (no `<form>`/page reload) — it re-checks the Super Admin/Maintenance Manager permission server-side, trims and title-cases the name (a small local `titleCase()` helper — "water pump" / "WATER PUMP" / "  Water   Pump " all normalize to "Water Pump", matching every existing type's naming style), does a case-insensitive `asset_categories.name` lookup, and either returns the existing row (`alreadyExisted: true`, no write) or creates a new leaf row under the same "Other" parent category the Excel importer already auto-creates unknown types under (Task 8's "use the existing asset category system," reused exactly, not reinvented). On success the field's local `types` state gets the new/existing name appended (if not already present) and the `<select>` is immediately set to it — Task 5's "add it to the dropdown and auto-select it," entirely client-side, no page reload needed since the value just needs to exist as an `<option>` in time for the eventual asset-save submission.

**Task 6 — Duplicate handling:** when `addAssetTypeAction` reports `alreadyExisted: true`, the inline panel swaps to a small notice ("This asset type already exists." + "'{name}' has been selected for you." + an OK button) instead of creating a second row — verified against the live `asset_categories` table that a case-insensitive `equals` lookup (`mode: "insensitive"`) correctly catches "water pump"/"WATER PUMP"/"Water Pump" as the same existing row, so three submissions of that name in different cases collapse to one save call on the very first one and two no-op lookups after.

**Task 7 — Asset Types section reflects new types automatically:** no changes were needed in `components/assets/asset-type-cards.tsx` — its `categoryChips` data is a fresh `GROUP BY category` query on every server render, and the Task 3 redirect-to-`/assets` mechanism already forces exactly that fresh render on save, so a newly-added type with its first asset appears in the cards (e.g. "Water Pump — 1 asset") with zero extra code; a type with 0 assets structurally cannot appear since the query only ever returns categories that have at least one row.

## Unit 10G.41B — Worker Salary Breakdown and Manager Labor Cost View

**Requirement:** `worker_profiles` only ever had one pay-related column, a single `hourly_rate` Data Entry could set at creation. Replace that with a real salary breakdown (Basic Salary, Transport/Accommodation/Food Allowances, Total Salary, Monthly Working Hours, Hourly Rate) that only Manager/Super Admin can see or edit, with Hourly Rate auto-calculated from the breakdown and used everywhere labor cost is already shown.

**Scope clarification (asked before touching the schema):** the task's Manager/Data-Entry form field lists also named Job Title, Work Location, Reporting Manager, and Nationality as if they already existed on `worker_profiles` — inspection showed none of the four exist there (Job Title exists only on the unrelated `profiles` login-account table). Asked the user whether to scope this unit to the salary breakdown alone or also add those 4 fields; **decision: add all 4 as new nullable columns too**, matching the task's explicit form field lists literally.

**Task 1 — Schema, additive only:** `prisma/migrations/20260829000000_worker_profiles_salary_breakdown_unit10g41b/migration.sql` adds 10 nullable columns to `worker_profiles` — `job_title`, `work_location`, `reporting_manager`, `nationality` (all `text`), and `basic_salary`/`transport_allowance`/`accommodation_allowance`/`food_allowance`/`total_salary` (`numeric(12,3)`, default 0) plus `monthly_working_hours` (`numeric(12,2)`, default 260) — no existing column touched, renamed, or made required. Applied directly against the local DB via `prisma.$executeRawUnsafe` (this repo has no `prisma migrate deploy` script; matches the hand-written-migration convention every prior schema unit in this session has used), then `npx prisma generate` — the regenerate initially failed with `EPERM` because a leftover `npm run dev` process from an earlier session had the query-engine DLL locked; stopped that process (with the user's explicit approval, since killing processes needed sign-off) and regenerated successfully. Verified against a live row: existing pre-unit workers now read `basic_salary: 0, total_salary: 0, monthly_working_hours: 260`, exactly the additive defaults Task 1 specified — nothing broke for existing data.

**Task 1 — Hourly rate math, one shared module:** new `lib/backend/workers/salary.ts` (deliberately not `"server-only"`, same rationale as `lib/assets/asset-excel-mapping.ts` — its `isSalaryPending`/`DEFAULT_MONTHLY_WORKING_HOURS` are needed by client components too, only `computeSalary`/`noSalary` are actually called server-side). `computeSalary()` always recomputes `total_salary` from its four parts (never trusts a submitted total, so it can't drift), then `hourly_rate = total_salary ÷ monthly_working_hours` — falling back to 0 whenever either is missing/zero (Task 1's exact rule) — unless the caller supplied a different, positive hourly rate, which is kept as-is (Task 3's "Manager can override"). `noSalary()` is the all-zeros/260-hours shape a Data-Entry-created profile always gets. `isSalaryPending(w)` is `total_salary === 0 || hourly_rate === 0`, the single definition every "Salary Pending" badge in this unit calls.

**Task 2/3 — One form, gated by role, not by mode:** `components/admin/worker-profile-form-modal.tsx` rewritten with a new `canManageWorkerProfiles: boolean` prop (replacing its old `canViewCosts` prop entirely — the Salary Details section is gated by the same `isManagerRole()` check the server re-verifies, not the broader/separate cost-visibility flag, so client and server can never disagree about who gets to fill these fields in). Employee ID, Worker Name, Worker Type, Division, Job Title, Work Location, and Mobile No. now show for every role that can reach "Add Worker" (Mobile No. used to be edit-only/Manager-only — Task 2 explicitly puts it on Data Entry's create form too). Reporting Manager, Nationality, a read-only Status badge, and the whole "Salary Details" card (Basic Salary/Transport/Accommodation/Food, a read-only computed Total Salary, Monthly Working Hours defaulting to 260, and an editable Hourly Rate) render only when `canManageWorkerProfiles` is true — for both Add and Edit, since a Manager can fill in salary at creation too, not only later. The Hourly Rate field auto-recalculates via a `useEffect` on the four salary inputs + hours (skipped on the very first render so an existing manual override isn't silently overwritten just by opening the form) but stays a plain editable number input, so typing over it directly is the override path Task 3 asks for. Helper text: "Hourly Rate is used to calculate labor cost from Job Card work time." Notes stayed exactly as before (edit-mode-only) — it's in neither Task 2 nor Task 3's field lists, so it wasn't touched.

**Task 2/10 — Security is enforced in the service layer, not the form:** `lib/backend/workers/service.ts`'s `createWorkerProfile` now computes `canSetSalary = isManagerRole(context)` and uses `computeSalary(...)` only when true, `noSalary()` otherwise — regardless of what a hand-crafted form submission contains, a Data-Entry-authenticated request can never write a non-zero salary/hourly-rate, and `reporting_manager`/`nationality` are silently dropped to `null` the same way. `updateWorkerProfile` was already 100% Manager/Super-Admin-only end to end (`assertCanEditWorkerProfile`, unchanged, predates this unit) so it always trusts `computeSalary(...)`. `workerProfileSchema` (`lib/backend/workers/validators.ts`) made `hourlyRate` optional (Data Entry's form no longer submits it at all) and added the 8 new optional fields; `total_salary` is deliberately NOT an accepted schema field at all — it only ever exists as something the server computes.

**Task 4 — "Salary Pending":** shown wherever `isSalaryPending(worker)` is true, gated to Manager/Super Admin (`canManageWorkerProfiles`/`isManager`) at every site: a new "Salary Status" column in the Worker Profiles table (`worker-profiles-view.tsx`), a badge inside the Salary Details card on the edit form, a badge next to the worker's name on their Worker Activity card (`worker-card.tsx`), and — worded as "Rate not set" per Task 9's own phrasing for that surface — inside `WorkerActivityDetailModal` and `ClosureReviewModal` wherever a rate of exactly 0 would otherwise have displayed as a real (if oddly zero) number. Data Entry never sees any of these: the Worker Profiles/Worker Activity pages gate the columns/badges with `canManageWorkerProfiles`, and Closure Review is already Manager/Super-Admin-only end to end (`assertIsManagerRole` at the top of `getClosureReviewDetailAction`).

**Task 5 — Table columns:** `worker-profiles-view.tsx`'s header/rows now show Work Location for every role (new, common column), plus Job Title and Salary Status for Manager/Super Admin only (new, gated by `canManageWorkerProfiles`) alongside the pre-existing Hourly Rate column — left gated by `canViewCosts`, unchanged, per Task 10's explicit "cost visibility still respects canViewCosts where the app already uses it." Net result matches Task 5's two lists exactly: Data Entry sees Employee ID/Worker Name/Worker Type/Division/Work Location/Status; Manager additionally sees Job Title/Salary Status/Hourly Rate.

**Task 6/7/8 — Labor cost calculation, Job Card/Worker Activity views:** verified by inspection that this was already fully correct before this unit and required no logic changes (Task 9's "do not change worker timer logic" and Task 6's "do not change closure approval logic" both explicitly forbid touching it anyway) — `lib/backend/work-orders/work-sessions.ts`'s `computeAmount()` already does `(duration_minutes/60) × hourly_rate_snapshot`, a value frozen onto the assignment/session at the moment a worker is assigned (never re-read from the live profile afterward, so a later salary edit never retroactively changes an already-worked Job Card's cost). `lib/work-orders/work-session-totals.ts` already aggregates Today/Week/Month totals, worker-wise, and Job-Card-wise for the Worker Activity page/detail modal, the Manager Dashboard Labor Snapshot, and Closure Review — every dollar figure across all of them was already `canViewCosts`-gated (verified directly in `worker-session-row.tsx`, `worker-card.tsx`, `worker-activity-detail-modal.tsx`, `closure-review-modal.tsx`, `dashboard/page.tsx`). This unit's only change to that whole chain is the two "Rate not set" additions described under Task 4 above.

**Task 10 — Extra defense beyond UI hiding:** added `stripSalaryForNonManager()` (`lib/backend/workers/service.ts`) and applied it in the two Server Components that hand a full `WorkerProfileRow[]` to a Data-Entry-reachable client component — `app/(dashboard)/admin/worker-profiles/page.tsx` and `app/(dashboard)/maintenance/assignments/page.tsx` — so the salary breakdown/reporting_manager/nationality are zeroed out of the actual page payload for non-Managers, not just hidden by conditional rendering (the pre-existing, accepted pattern this codebase already used for the single `hourly_rate` column was left as-is, per Task 10's explicit instruction to keep respecting `canViewCosts` where already used; a full salary breakdown is materially more sensitive than one rate number, so this unit adds the stronger guarantee only for the new fields). The 8-9 other `listWorkerProfiles()`/`getActiveWorkerProfilesForAssignment()` call sites that feed Job Card worker-assignment pickers were left alone — they only ever render `name`/`worker_type`, and reworking every one of them was out of this unit's scope.

**Files changed:** `prisma/schema.prisma` (10 new `WorkerProfile` fields); `prisma/migrations/20260829000000_worker_profiles_salary_breakdown_unit10g41b/migration.sql` (new); `lib/backend/workers/salary.ts` (new); `lib/backend/workers/validators.ts`; `lib/backend/workers/service.ts`; `app/actions/workers.ts`; `components/admin/worker-profile-form-modal.tsx` (rewritten); `components/admin/worker-profiles-view.tsx`; `components/workers/worker-card.tsx`; `components/workers/worker-activity-detail-modal.tsx`; `components/dashboard/closure-review-modal.tsx`; `app/(dashboard)/admin/worker-profiles/page.tsx`; `app/(dashboard)/maintenance/assignments/page.tsx`.

**Verification:** confirmed via direct DB read that the migration applied cleanly and existing rows got exactly the specified additive defaults. Confirmed by code inspection that `computeSalary`'s formula matches Task 1's literal rule, that `createWorkerProfile`/`updateWorkerProfile` gate salary/reporting_manager/nationality on `isManagerRole`, and that every existing cost-figure call site in the labor-cost chain (worker sessions, Worker Activity, Closure Review, Dashboard) remained `canViewCosts`-gated and untouched. A live authenticated browser walkthrough of the 17-item manual checklist (both as Data Entry and as Manager) was not performed this session — no browser was available; verification here is code-level.

**Validation:** `npm run db:check` ✓, `lint` ✓ (0 errors), `typecheck` ✓, `build` ✓ (62 routes; `/admin/worker-profiles`, `/maintenance/assignments`, and `/dashboard` all unchanged in the route list). Per the task's explicit instruction, `npm run test:e2e` was **not** run. No change to Job Card workflow, worker timer logic, closure approval logic, or the asset module. No deployment performed — a leftover local dev server was stopped (with explicit user approval) only to unblock `prisma generate`, not as part of any deployment step.

## Unit 10G.41C — Worker Type and Division Form Clarification

**Requirement:** normal Data Entry users should clearly understand the difference between Worker Type (simple system role group), Job Title (actual HR job title), and Division (work team/skill area) on the Add Worker form, and Division needed to be clearly visible after Worker Type.

## Quality and performance assessment — 2026-09-13

Requested enterprise codebase assessment for 50–100 concurrent users on a Windows office-server VM. Added `docs/quality-audit-20260913.md`, raw measurement/security-probe JSON artifacts, and two reproducible audit scripts. No application behavior, schema, job cards, worker records, inventory, or feature flags changed. Browser logins created ordinary local auth/session/audit activity; the office VM was not accessed.

Verified current local DB: 11 profiles, 0 work orders, 171 assets, 2 worker profiles, 0 work sessions, 21 offline inventory movements; inventory check remains disabled. These figures supersede historical recovery baseline assumptions for this local audit only. Current package is Next.js 16.2.7, and the active layout uses a build-time Google Inter font. Context documentation contains older architecture/workflow descriptions; consult current implementation and the audit for these discrepancies.

Checks: db:check, lint, typecheck and production build pass. Initial restricted build could not fetch Google Fonts; permitted retry passed. Both full and production-only npm audits report zero known vulnerabilities. Existing Playwright permission suite: 2 pass / 1 fail (hardcoded AST-VEH-0043 picker fixture unavailable). Authenticated probes confirmed salary/hourly-rate disclosure in Data Entry payloads. Pure-helper probes reproduced a cost-deny bypass and file-path containment failures. Code review found additional entity authorization, report status, timer/closure, SSE session lifetime, and error-disclosure issues; see report for evidence and priorities.

Performance: 320/320 concurrent-read probe responses were HTTP 200. At 100 simultaneous requests, p95 was 2,178 ms for Data Entry and 1,736 ms for Manager. These short local production-mode bursts reused a session per role and ran against zero work orders; they do not establish capacity for 100 users on a populated office VM. Full mutating lifecycle tests, representative sustained load, and restore verification remain outstanding. No deployment or remediation was performed.

## Worker Timer and Closure Logic Hardening (Unit 10G.53) — 2026-09-16

Root cause: `assertNoActiveWorkSessions` (the only server-side closure guard) checked exclusively for a currently-running ("Active") session — a Paused or never-started assigned worker never blocked closure at all. Separately, `startWorkSession` had no cross-Job-Card check, so the same `worker_profiles` row could be started on two Job Cards at once. `LiveTimer`'s initial `useState` computed `Date.now()` during render — identical to the exact anti-pattern `components/layout/live-top-clock.tsx`'s own comment already documents and fixes elsewhere in this codebase — causing an SSR/hydration mismatch that is the most likely explanation for "the live counter sometimes does not update after deployment" (imperceptible on localhost, real over network latency in production).

**New "finished" assignment state** — no schema change: `work_order_worker_assignments.status` has no DB check constraint, so `"finished"` is a new application-level value alongside the existing `"active"`/`"removed"`, meaning "done working on this Job Card, still shown everywhere, cannot be re-timed" (`loadActiveAssignment`'s existing `status === "active"` gate rejects it for free, same as it already rejects `"removed"`). Added `deriveSimpleWorkerState()` + `SimpleWorkerState` ("Not Started"/"Working"/"Paused"/"Finished") to `lib/work-orders/hours-variance.ts` (client-safe, re-exported from `work-session-totals.ts`) — the one place every surface derives the plain 4-state model from `(assignment_status, session_status)`. `WorkerLaborRow` gained `assignment_status`; `getWorkOrderLaborSummary`/`getWorkOrderLaborSummariesBulk` widened their roster query from `status: "active"` to `status: { in: ["active", "finished"] }` (finished workers keep showing with real hours) — the Job Card detail page's plain Assignment-tab roster query was deliberately left `"active"`-only (it's a current-team-membership view, not a time-tracking view).

**Finish Work** (`finishWorkSession` in `lib/backend/work-orders/work-sessions.ts`, `finishWorkSessionAction`): ends any Active session exactly like the old Stop did, then sets `assignment.status = "finished"`. `components/work-orders/worker-session-row.tsx` now shows Start (Not Started) / Pause+Finish Work (Working) / Resume+Finish Work (Paused) / read-only (Finished) — plain "Stop" is gone from the UI (function kept, just unused by this row) since Finish Work replaces it.

**Closure guard** (`lib/work-orders/closure-readiness.ts`, new client-safe `checkWorkersReadyForClosure()`): ready only when no worker is Working, Paused, or Not Started. Enforced server-side in all three real closing paths — `requestJobCardClosure`, `closeWorkOrder` (Manager direct close), and `approveJobCardClosure` (Manager approving a pending request — a worker can still be started/resumed while a request sits pending review, so this needed the same re-check, not just request-time). Mirrored read-only in: Daily Activity board (`workTimeChip`/`closureReasons`/Next Action wording), Job Card detail page's Closure panel, the Request Closure modal ("All workers finished" + named paused/working/not-started warnings), the Manager Dashboard's Data-Entry-facing Needs Attention panel (`app/(dashboard)/dashboard/page.tsx` — same "Not Started slipped through as Ready" bug existed there too), and the Closure Review modal (worker badges now read "Finished" instead of stale "Completed").

**Cross-Job-Card guard**: `startWorkSession` now blocks Start/Resume when the same `worker_id` has an Active session on a *different* Job Card, naming that Job Card's number in the error; a Paused session elsewhere is explicitly allowed (task's own "preferred" rule).

**`LiveTimer` fix**: initial render now shows a fixed "00:00" placeholder (same pattern as `LiveTopClock`) instead of a `Date.now()`-derived value; the real elapsed time is set from inside `useEffect` on mount — a post-hydration update, never a mismatch. Duration math (`Date.now() - new Date(startedAt).getTime()`, recomputed every tick from the DB's own ISO timestamp) was already correct and untouched.

**Verification:** no browser available. Built a temporary route (`app/api/test-harness-10g53-temp`, deleted before finishing) that calls the real `startWorkSession`/`pauseWorkSession`/`finishWorkSession`/`requestJobCardClosure` functions through the real auth/transaction stack, driven by a minted session cookie against the already-running dev server. All 6 of the task's manual-check cases (A–F) passed, including the exact cross-Job-Card block message. Separately seeded a Job Card with one Finished + one Working worker and fetched `/maintenance/work-orders/[id]/print` — confirmed "Finished" and "In Progress" both render correctly with hours/start/end. All seeded data, sessions, and the temporary route were removed immediately after.

**Validation:** `npm run db:check` ✓, `lint` ✓ (0 errors), `typecheck` ✓, `build` ✓ (62 routes — unchanged; no test route leaked into the build). Per the task's explicit instruction, `npm run test:e2e` was **not** run. No database schema change. No change to Job Card creation workflow, material issue/receive workflow, or auth/login. No deployment performed.

## Daily Activity Closure Requested Visibility (Unit 10G.54) — 2026-09-16

Root cause: `app/(dashboard)/maintenance/daily-activity/page.tsx`'s `where` clause only ever matched `ACTIVE_JOB_CARD_STATUSES` (never included "Closure Requested") plus one exception for a Job Card with a currently-running work session. Unit 10G.53 made "every worker Finished" a precondition for requesting closure, so by definition a Closure Requested Job Card can never have a running session anymore either — the exception that used to accidentally keep some of these visible stopped firing, and the Job Card vanished from Data Entry's own working page the instant they submitted it.

**Visibility fix**: added `{ status: CLOSURE_REQUESTED_STATUS }` to the query's OR clause — Closure Requested Job Cards are always included now, same as before Unit 10G.53 inadvertently broke it.

**Read-only display once requested**: new `isClosureRequested` flag computed per card, checked first in `priorityBucket` (new `"waiting-approval"` bucket, so its materials/worker state — which will always otherwise evaluate "ready" — never sorts/labels it as "Ready for Closure" again) and used to gate every mutating action for that Job Card: `showRequestClosure`, `showAssignWorkers`, `showProcessMaterials`, and `canManageSessions` (which alone hides Start/Pause/Resume/Finish Work inside `WorkerSessionRow` for free — that component needed no changes). `nextAction.message` for this state is now the task's exact combined wording ("Waiting for Manager approval. This Job Card has been submitted for closure approval. The Maintenance Manager will review and close it."), with no button — the panel's own fallback then renders "Open Job Card" automatically. `components/work-orders/daily-activity-card.tsx`'s list row swaps its usual 3 mini-chips for a plain "Waiting for Manager approval" line for this state, so it never again reads as actionable.

**New KPI + filter**: "Waiting Manager Approval" summary card (amber `Hourglass` icon, not green) and a matching `waiting-approval` `FilterChip`/`STATUS_FILTERS` entry, both counting/filtering on `isClosureRequested`. The existing "Ready for Closure" card/filter was fixed to exclude an already-requested Job Card (previously double-counted/double-listed under both, since `closureReady` alone doesn't know a request already went out).

## Job Card Print Signature Bottom Alignment (Unit 10G.57A) — 2026-09-16

`app/(dashboard)/maintenance/work-orders/[id]/print/page.tsx` only — pure print-CSS change, no data/query/section content touched (Material Used, sources, and every other Unit 10G.57 fix are untouched).

**Technique**: the standard "sticky footer" CSS pattern, applied print-only (screen preview stays plain document flow, unaffected). `.print-sheet` becomes `display: flex; flex-direction: column; min-height: 281mm` (297mm A4 height − 8mm top margin − 8mm bottom margin — the sheet already prints with zero of its own padding, so this is the exact one-page content height). The Signatures `<section>` gets a new `print-signatures` class with `margin-top: auto` in print. When content is short, the flex box is exactly one page tall and the auto margin absorbs the leftover space, pushing Signatures to the bottom; when content is longer than one page, the box simply grows past 281mm (min-height is a floor, not a ceiling) and the auto margin resolves to zero, so Signatures sits immediately after the last content block and flows onto page 2 exactly as in plain block layout. No absolute positioning anywhere — flex-direction: column keeps every child's own stacking/`avoid-break`/page-break behavior identical to normal block flow; the only change is the last child's vertical position when there's spare room.

## Job Card Print Signature Pagination Fix (Unit 10G.57B) — 2026-09-16

`app/(dashboard)/maintenance/work-orders/[id]/print/page.tsx` only — pure print-CSS value change, no data/section/content touched.

**Root cause:** Unit 10G.57A's `.print-sheet` used `min-height: 281mm` — the full A4 printable height (297mm − 8mm top − 8mm bottom margin) — as the flex column's floor, bottom-aligning Signatures (via `margin-top: auto`) flush against the exact page-1/page-2 boundary with zero clearance. Print rendering doesn't guarantee pixel-perfect mm-to-px conversion, so a box computed to be "exactly" one page tall can render a hair taller than the true printable area. Because `.print-signatures` also carries `.avoid-break` (`page-break-inside: avoid`, required so the three signature boxes are never sliced apart), the first sign of overflow relocated the *entire* signature block to page 2 — and the leftover space the auto margin had already spent pushing it down stayed empty on page 1, since nothing else exists to reflow into that gap. Net effect: short Job Cards showed a large blank gap on page 1 with Signatures alone on page 2, exactly as reported. No stray `page-break-before`/`break-before` rule was found (checked and confirmed clean); the flush-to-the-literal-edge min-height was the sole cause.

**Pagination fix behavior:** `.print-sheet`'s min-height was reduced from `281mm` to `271mm` (a 10mm safety buffer — comparable to the page's own 8mm margin) and marked `!important` for cascade safety; `box-sizing: border-box` was added explicitly to the same rule (belt-and-braces alongside the pre-existing zeroed padding/border, so the box's height can never be inflated by box-model differences, addressing the task's explicit ask). This keeps the exact same flex-column + `margin-top: auto` "sticky footer" technique (still no absolute/fixed positioning anywhere), but the signature block's computed bottom now always lands a few millimeters clear of the true page boundary — eliminating the flush-edge failure mode while Signatures still reads as "near the bottom" of page 1 for short and normal Job Cards. Multi-page behavior for long Job Cards is unaffected: `min-height` remains a floor, not a ceiling — content taller than 271mm still grows the box and pushes Signatures to flow naturally after all content, onto page 2, exactly as designed in 10G.57A.

**Verification:** no browser available in this environment (same limitation as 10G.57A — Chrome's own print-preview pixel rendering could not be directly inspected), so verification was structural: seeded two real Job Cards via a throwaway Prisma script — Case A (2 workers, 2 materials, matching the reported bug screenshot) and Case D (6 workers, 12 materials, a large/multi-page case) — and fetched both live print pages via an authenticated `Invoke-WebRequest` session. Confirmed in both cases' rendered HTML: `min-height: 271mm` present, `box-sizing: border-box !important` present on `.print-sheet`, `.print-signatures { margin-top: auto !important; }` unchanged, the old `min-height: 281mm` value is gone, the `print-signatures` class is correctly wired to the rendered `<section>`, and Signatures/Work Team and Time/Material Used all still render (Material Used was not removed or altered). `screen-only`/`no-print` hiding of Status History and Approval and Closure sections (established in prior units, out of scope for this fix) confirmed still present and untouched. Seeded work orders, worker profile, and the auth session were deleted immediately after; both temporary scripts were deleted; no script left behind.

**Validation:** `npm run db:check` ✓, `lint` ✓ (0 errors), `typecheck` ✓, `build` ✓ (62 routes, unchanged — print route unaffected). Per the task's explicit instruction, `npm run test:e2e` was **not** run. No database schema change. No change to Job Card workflow, closure approval logic, Daily Activity workflow, worker timer logic, material issue/receive workflow, print data sources, or auth/login. Material Used was not removed; signatures were not hidden from print. No deployment performed.

## Job Card Print Signature Page-1 Fix (Unit 10G.57C) — 2026-09-16

`app/(dashboard)/maintenance/work-orders/[id]/print/page.tsx` only.

**Why the flex approach failed:** the user confirmed in real Chrome print preview that Signatures could still land on page 2 with a large blank gap on page 1 even after 10G.57B's 271mm buffer. Flexbox fragmentation across a print page boundary, combined with Signatures' required `page-break-inside: avoid` (the three boxes must never be sliced apart), was not reliable — any relocation of that block due to overflow leaves the space `margin-top: auto` already spent pushing it down empty on page 1, since nothing follows Signatures to reflow into the gap. The underlying mechanism (flex + auto-margin bottom alignment fragmenting across a real print page break) was the actual problem, not the specific min-height value, so 10G.57B's buffer only reduced — it could not eliminate — the risk.

**Fix:** replaced the flex/margin-auto "sticky footer" entirely with a plain static spacer. `.print-sheet` is back to ordinary block flow in print (`display: flex`, `flex-direction: column`, and `min-height` all removed — no page-fragmentation-sensitive layout involved anymore). A new `.signature-spacer` block element is rendered once, directly before the Signatures `<section>`, sized from real content counts computed in the component body: `workerCount = workerRows.length`, `materialCount = materials.length`, and a combined `operator_complaint` + `description_of_work` character length. Tiers (worker/material thresholds taken directly from the task's suggested rules): `workerCount > 5 || materialCount > 10` → no spacer rendered at all (large Job Card — content must flow naturally); `workerCount > 4 || materialCount > 6 || complaint text > 400 chars` → `signature-spacer-small` (15mm); otherwise → `signature-spacer-normal` (35mm). A plain block element can never itself force or prevent a page break, so this carries none of the flex approach's boundary risk — worst case it only adds harmless blank space above Signatures; it never pushes real content anywhere. Signatures keeps `page-break-inside: avoid` (now declared directly on `.print-signatures` too, not only via the pre-existing `.avoid-break` class) so the three boxes still never split across a page, and a genuinely large Job Card (no spacer) still flows Signatures onto page 2 exactly as before with no overlap risk. No absolute or fixed positioning was used anywhere, per the task's explicit constraint. The 35mm/15mm values are a best-effort first cut chosen conservatively (erring toward *not* creating a page 2, per the task's own stated priority) since — as below — no real browser was available to tune them against actual Chrome print preview; the task itself anticipated this ("tune height based on real Chrome print preview").

**Verification:** no browser available in this environment (same disclosed limitation as 10G.57A/10G.57B — this task explicitly required real Chrome print-preview confirmation, which could not be performed here). Verification was structural instead: seeded four real Job Cards via a throwaway Prisma script — Case A (2 workers/2 materials, the reported bug case), Case B (1 worker/0 materials), a boundary case (5 workers/7 materials), and Case D (6 workers/12 materials) — and fetched all four live print pages via an authenticated `Invoke-WebRequest` session. Confirmed in the rendered HTML: Case A and Case B correctly render a `signature-spacer-normal` div and nothing else; the boundary case correctly renders `signature-spacer-small`; Case D renders no spacer div at all; all four have the old `display: flex !important`/`margin-top: auto` rules completely gone from the stylesheet; all four have the new `.print-signatures { break-inside: avoid; page-break-inside: avoid; }` rule; the `print-signatures` class remains correctly wired to the rendered `<section>`; and Material Used, Work Team and Time, and Signatures all still render correctly in every case. Seeded work orders, worker profile, and the auth session were deleted immediately after; the temporary script and fetched HTML files were deleted; no script left behind. **A real Chrome print-preview check by the user (A4, Portrait, Default scale) is required before this can be considered fully verified** — this environment cannot confirm actual pixel/page-break behavior, only that the intended CSS and conditional markup are correctly generated.

**Validation:** `npm run db:check` ✓, `lint` ✓ (0 errors), `typecheck` ✓, `build` ✓ (62 routes, unchanged — print route unaffected). STORED` column (same pattern as `parts_request_items.total_price`), so Quantity × Unit Price = Total is always DB-accurate, never computed twice. Numbering reuses the existing `numbering_sequences` table (already live, already used by the Job Card/Purchase Request numbering triggers) via an atomic `upsert`/`increment` in application code — no new or modified DB trigger, and the opaque, untracked `set_parts_request_number` trigger the Job Card flow depends on was not touched. Implemented as a query-param step (`&type=job_card`/`&type=general`) rather than client-only state, so it composes cleanly with this app's existing plain-redirect/query-param conventions and lets error messages survive a server-action round trip. A deep link that already names a Job Card (`?jobCardId=`, e.g. "Request Materials" clicked from inside a specific Job Card) skips the selector entirely and goes straight to the existing wizard — the type is already implied there, so showing the selector would only be a regression in that flow's existing UX.

Submits via `app/actions/general-inventory-requests.ts`'s `createGeneralInventoryRequestAction`, a plain FormData-POST-and-redirect action mirroring `createPartsRequestAction`'s own convention, backed by `lib/backend/general-inventory-requests/service.ts`'s `createGeneralInventoryRequest` (Zod-validated, permission-gated identically to Job Card Materials Request creation per Task 11 — `parts_requests.create`/`work_orders.manage`/super_admin, no new permission).

## General Inventory Request Unit, Price, and Conversion Polish (Unit 10G.58A) — 2026-09-17

Follow-up polish on the Unit 10G.58 General Inventory / Stock Request form: default row count, a real unit dropdown (with custom-unit support), and an optional per-item purchase-unit → inventory-unit conversion for bulk materials (oil, chemicals, diesel, etc.) so future inventory valuation is never wrong. Job Card Materials Requests untouched throughout.

**Database (additive, same still-uncommitted migration extended rather than a second one):** `prisma/migrations/20260916000000_general_inventory_requests_unit10g58/migration.sql` (Unit 10G.58's migration — confirmed still uncommitted in this repo, so extending it in place keeps one clean history for a feature that hasn't shipped yet) gained 4 new columns on `general_inventory_request_items`: `inventory_unit` (nullable text — the stock/issue unit, only set when conversion is used), `conversion_quantity` (nullable `numeric(12,4)`, CHECK `> 0` when present), and two new `GENERATED ALWAYS AS (...) STORED` columns, `inventory_quantity_to_add` (`quantity_requested * COALESCE(conversion_quantity, 1)`) and `unit_cost` (`unit_price / COALESCE(conversion_quantity, 1)`, NULL when `unit_price` is NULL) — same generated-column pattern as `total_price`. The NULL-means-1 rule means a plain PCS/BOX/etc. item (no conversion) simply has `inventory_quantity_to_add == quantity_requested` and `unit_cost == unit_price`, so nothing that reads these two columns needs to special-case "no conversion." Applied directly to the dev DB (`prisma db execute`, same no-shadow-DB reasoning as 10G.58) and `prisma/schema.prisma`'s `general_inventory_request_items` model updated + client regenerated. No existing table (`parts_requests`, `work_orders`, or any other) touched.

**Files changed:** new `components/store/general-inventory-units.ts` (shared unit list + `CUSTOM_UNIT_VALUE` sentinel); rewritten `components/store/general-inventory-request-form.tsx` and `components/store/general-inventory-request-quick-view.tsx`; updated `lib/backend/general-inventory-requests/service.ts` and `app/actions/general-inventory-requests.ts`; updated `prisma/schema.prisma` and the 10G.58 migration file. No Job Card file touched.

**Default row behavior:** the form now starts with exactly one item row (`rowSlots = [0]`), replacing the previous default of 3. "Add Row" appends a new row; each row past the first gets a "Remove" button (real removal from a small slot-index array, not just hiding a trailing count) — the last remaining row can never be removed (button is hidden once only 1 row is left), matching Task 1's "do not allow removing the last row."

**Unit dropdown behavior:** the Purchase Unit column is now a `<select>` (`components/store/general-inventory-units.ts`'s `GENERAL_INVENTORY_UNIT_OPTIONS`, the task's exact 24-value list) defaulting to PCS, plus an "OTHER / CUSTOM" option. The same dropdown is reused for the conversion section's Inventory Unit, so the two never drift out of sync.

**Custom unit behavior:** selecting OTHER / CUSTOM reveals a plain text input for that row; `app/actions/general-inventory-requests.ts`'s new `resolveUnit()` helper reads the real typed value at submit time and that's what gets saved — the literal sentinel value is never written to the database (confirmed: a "Bundle" custom unit saved as `unit: "Bundle"`, not "OTHER / CUSTOM"). An empty custom-unit field is caught both client-side (blocks submit) and server-side (the resolved empty string fails the existing `unit` min-length Zod rule with the same "Unit is required" message).

**Purchase price calculation behavior:** unchanged Quantity × Unit Price = Total, still DB-computed (`total_price` generated column), still 3-decimal-place KWD formatting; a clarifying line ("Unit Price means price for one selected purchase unit…") now sits under each row, plus the two general helper lines from Task 11 under the whole table.

**Conversion behavior:** a new "Use different inventory stock unit" checkbox per row (Task 5/7's exact wording) reveals Inventory Unit + Conversion quantity fields plus a live-computed "Inventory Quantity = … / Unit Cost = …" preview box. Validation (`lib/backend/general-inventory-requests/service.ts`'s `generalRequestItemSchema`, via a `superRefine`) requires inventory unit and conversion quantity to be either both present or both absent — enabling the checkbox but leaving either blank is rejected client-side and server-side with the task's stated rule. Verified directly against the schema: quantity 0, empty purpose, empty custom unit, conversion-enabled-with-only-one-of-the-two-fields, and negative unit price are all correctly rejected; a fully-specified conversion (BARREL → 200 LITER) is accepted.

**Receive form consistency:** the receive form (inside `GeneralInventoryRequestQuickView`) now shows Purchase Qty/Unit alongside editable Received Qty/Unit Price, and a live "Inventory Qty / Unit Cost" column that recalculates as the user types (controlled inputs + a small per-item draft state), using the item's own `conversionQuantity`/`inventoryUnit` — exactly mirroring the create form's own live-preview math so the two never disagree.

**Inventory movement behavior:** `receiveGeneralInventoryRequest` now branches per item — no conversion: movement quantity = received quantity, movement unit = purchase unit, reference = the plain request number (unchanged from 10G.58). Conversion enabled: movement quantity = received quantity × conversion quantity, movement unit = the inventory unit, and the reference is extended to `"<request number> — <purchase qty> <purchase unit> received"` (e.g. `REC/MAT/GEN/0003 — 1 BARREL received`) so the original purchase quantity/unit is still visible even though the movement itself is now recorded in the inventory unit. Verified directly: a 1-BARREL/200-LITER-conversion item produced an `offline_inventory_movements` row with `quantity: 200`, `unit: "LITER"`, `reference_number: "REC/MAT/GEN/0003 — 1 BARREL received"`. Still no stock deducted, still no Job Card touched.

**Future inventory value support:** every value Task 10 asked for is available without any extra storage beyond the 4 new columns — purchase quantity/unit/price/total already existed (`quantity_requested`/`unit`/`unit_price`/`total_price`), and the new `inventory_unit`/`conversion_quantity`/`inventory_quantity_to_add`/`unit_cost` cover the rest, all DB-consistent (the last two are generated columns, never independently computed and liable to drift).

**Existing Job Card flow unchanged confirmation:** `components/store/parts-request-wizard.tsx` and `lib/backend/parts-requests/*` were not touched. Confirmed live: `?type=job_card` still renders Select Job Card / Requested Materials / Attachments steps, the Job Card item table's `unit_of_measure_${i}` field is still a plain text input (not the new dropdown), and no General Inventory conversion wording leaked into that flow.

**Manual check results (Cases A–I):** A/B confirmed live (only 1 default row renders; Add Row/Remove wiring present). C/D/E/F confirmed via direct DB transaction using the same logic as the service: Oil filter (PCS, no conversion) → Total 12.500, inventory qty 5 PCS; Engine Oil (BARREL, no conversion) → Total 25.000, inventory qty 1 BARREL; Engine Oil (BARREL + 200 LITER conversion) → Total 25.000, inventory qty 200.000 LITER, unit cost 0.125; custom unit "Bundle" → Total 12.000, unit saved as literal "Bundle". G confirmed against the real Zod schema (8 validation scenarios, all correct — see above). H confirmed: receiving the conversion item produced exactly the expected movement (200 LITER, reference mentioning "1 BARREL received"). I confirmed live (Job Card wizard unchanged). All test data deleted immediately after each check; one pre-existing General Inventory request (unrelated, created by a real user session before this unit started, purpose "new stock") was found during cleanup and deliberately left untouched rather than assumed to be test data.

**Validation:** `npm run db:check` ✓, `npm run lint` ✓ (0 errors), `npm run typecheck` ✓, `npm run build` ✓ (62 routes, unchanged). Per the task's explicit instruction, `npm run test:e2e` was **not** run. No change to Job Card material request workflow, Daily Activity material workflow, Job Card required materials logic, material issue/receive logic for Job Cards, or auth/login. No deployment performed.

A new `unitSelectValue()` helper decides whether to show a fixed option or the custom slot selected, so a unit value that doesn't match any fixed option (e.g. one filled in via the existing "select an Offline Inventory suggestion" autocomplete, which can carry over whatever free-text unit a Store Keeper originally typed) is never silently lost or coerced — it shows up correctly as an editable custom value instead.

## New Job Card Smart Meter Field (Unit 10G.60) — 2026-09-17

Replaced New Job Card → Step 2's always-both Running Hours + Kilometers fields with a single, asset-type-driven field (vehicles show only Kilometers, equipment shows only Running Hours, anything else falls back to an explicit "Meter Reading Type" chooser), plus auto-filling Job location from the selected asset's own Current Location.

**Files changed:** `components/work-orders/work-order-wizard.tsx` only. No schema change — `work_orders.running_hours`/`kilometers` were already nullable with zero required-field validation (client or server), so simply not rendering/submitting the irrelevant one was sufficient. `app/actions/maintenance.ts` (the create action, `workOrderSchema`) was not touched — confirmed by reading it first that both fields are generic optional-number Zod fields with no dependency on which one is present. The Edit Job Card form (`components/work-orders/work-order-form.tsx`) is a fully separate component (not shared with the wizard) and was deliberately left untouched, matching the task's explicit "New Job Card" scope — editing a Job Card after creation still shows both fields plainly, a known, accepted gap outside this unit.

**Vehicle kilometer behavior:** `VEHICLE_ASSET_TYPES` (Car, Pickup, Bus, Half Lorry, Tanker, Trailer — the exact leaf strings from `lib/assets/asset-excel-mapping.ts`'s `ASSET_TYPE_DISPLAY_ORDER`, confirmed as the real values asset rows carry, not guessed) → only "Current Kilometer Reading" renders, mapped to the existing `kilometers` field, with the task's exact placeholder/helper text. The Running Hours input is not rendered at all for these types, so it's never present in the submitted form data.

**Equipment running-hours behavior:** `EQUIPMENT_ASSET_TYPES` (Generator, Bobcat, Crane, Forklift, Compressor, Tower Light, Welding Machine, Manlift, Loader) → only "Current Running Hours" renders, mapped to `running_hours`, same pattern in reverse.

**Unknown asset fallback behavior:** any category outside both lists (custom asset types, "Needs Review", null/blank category) shows a "Meter Reading Type" dropdown (Not Applicable / Kilometers / Running Hours), defaulting to Not Applicable, which then reveals the matching single field — never both. The dropdown's own selection resets back to "Not Applicable" whenever the selected asset changes (via React's "adjust state during render" pattern — comparing the new `selectedAssetId` against a `lastSyncedAssetId` state and calling `setState` directly in the render body — not a `useEffect`, since this project's ESLint config enforces `react-hooks/set-state-in-effect` as an error and flagged the first attempt), so a stale choice from a previously-selected unknown-type asset never carries over to a newly selected one.

**Job location auto-fill:** Job location became a controlled input (`jobLocation`/`jobLocationTouched` state). Whenever the selected asset changes, if the user hasn't typed into the field yet, it's auto-filled from `selectedAsset.location` (available directly on the asset picker's own option data — no extra query needed); the field's own `onChange` (the only place a real keystroke reaches) sets `jobLocationTouched`, and the asset-driven autofill calls `setJobLocation` directly rather than simulating an input event, so it can never itself mark the field "touched" — meaning once a user types anything, autofill permanently stops for that field for the rest of the session, exactly per Task 6. Placeholder updated to "Auto-filled from asset location, or enter site/building/area."

**Review/detail/print compatibility:** the Review & Save step's Request Details card gained a conditional row (Kilometers if present, else Running Hours if present, else nothing — never both, never an empty placeholder) reading from the same `reviewData` FormData snapshot already used for every other field in that step; since only one of the two inputs is ever actually rendered/submitted, this needed no extra logic beyond the simple either/or check. The Job Card detail page and the Unit 10G.57 print page already only display whichever of the two fields is populated (confirmed by reading both before changing anything — detail page uses `!= null`, print page uses a truthy check, both pre-existing and unmodified) — verified live with two seeded Job Cards (kilometers-only and running-hours-only) that both displayed correctly on the detail page's Overview and on the print page's Job Card Details grid, with the other field's row absent in both places, no raw/undefined values, and Unit 10G.57's print work untouched.

**Existing workflow unchanged confirmation:** no changes to `app/actions/maintenance.ts`, asset import logic, Daily Activity, material workflow, or closure logic — the entire change is confined to Step 2's JSX/local state in the wizard component.

**Manual check results:** the meter-field/autofill logic (Cases A–F) is driven entirely by client-side React state changes from selecting an asset — with no browser available in this environment, these could not be exercised interactively (the same disclosed limitation as every other UI-interactive unit this session); verified instead by careful code reading (classification lists match the real, exhaustive set of asset category strings; the render-time state-sync pattern is the officially correct effect-free way to reset state on a changing id; the touched-flag logic is watertight since programmatic `setJobLocation` calls never pass through the input's `onChange`) and by a live structural fetch of the wizard's default (no-asset-selected) state, which correctly showed the Meter Reading Type fallback dropdown defaulted to Not Applicable, with neither "Current Kilometer Reading" nor "Current Running Hours" rendered, and the old always-both plain fields completely gone. Case G (save behavior) was verified directly and does not depend on browser interaction: two Job Cards seeded with only `kilometers`/only `running_hours` set (mirroring exactly what the wizard would submit for a vehicle vs. an equipment asset) both round-tripped correctly through the real, unmodified detail and print pages — confirming Task 9's "no raw/undefined values" and "no regression to Unit 10G.57 print work" directly. All seeded data deleted immediately after.

**Validation:** `npm run db:check` ✓, `npm run lint` ✓ (0 errors — one `react-hooks/set-state-in-effect` error was caught and fixed by switching to the render-time state-sync pattern before this was reported clean), `npm run typecheck` ✓, `npm run build` ✓ (62 routes, unchanged). ## Inventory Cost and Stock Value Foundation (Unit 10G.61) — 2026-09-17

Adds unit cost and stock value visibility to Offline Inventory Control (formal name for what the task calls "Inventory Control" — confirmed via audit to be the correct target, not the separate Store > Parts catalog which already has its own unrelated `unit_price` field), General Inventory / Stock Request receiving, and Add New Material — gated behind the existing `canViewCosts()` permission. Job Card Required Materials remain price-free by explicit decision, untouched.

**Inventory cost model decision:** "simple last unit cost method" (Task 9), computed at read time — no persistent "material master" row exists for Offline Inventory materials today (a material is just a recurring identity, `part_id` or `manual_material_name`+`unit`, across `offline_inventory_movements` rows; confirmed via `buildBalanceKey()`), so rather than add a new master table to store `last_unit_cost`, it's derived as *the `unit_cost` of that material's most recent movement that actually recorded one* (any movement type). Stock Value = Balance × that last unit cost, except a negative or unpriced balance always shows 0 (never a negative or fabricated number) with a "Review required" note (Task 10). This needed no new table — only two new nullable columns on the existing ledger table. `parts.unit_price` (Store > Parts' own, pre-existing, unrelated cost field) was confirmed untouched.

**Files changed:** `prisma/migrations/20260917000000_inventory_cost_foundation_unit10g61/` (+ `prisma/schema.prisma`), `lib/store/offline-inventory-data.ts`, `app/actions/offline-inventory.ts`, `components/store/add-new-material-form.tsx`, `components/store/material-detail-modal.tsx`, `components/store/store-balance-view.tsx`, `components/store/offline-inventory-types.ts`, `app/(dashboard)/store/offline-inventory/page.tsx`, `.../add-material/page.tsx`, `.../movements/page.tsx`, `lib/backend/general-inventory-requests/service.ts`. No Job Card Required Materials, Daily Activity, closure, worker-timer, or auth file touched.

**Schema/migration:** additive only — `offline_inventory_movements` gains `unit_cost numeric(14,6)` and `total_cost numeric(14,3)`, both nullable (CHECK `>= 0` when present). Every existing row is unaffected (both columns simply null). No other table changed.

**Add New Material cost behavior:** an optional "Opening Unit Cost (KWD)" field (shown only when `canViewCosts`, mirroring the exact established pattern already used by `new-part-wizard.tsx`'s own Unit Price field) plus a live, client-computed "Opening Stock Value" preview (Initial Quantity × Opening Unit Cost). Saved onto the same `OPENING_STOCK` movement `addNewMaterialAction` already creates. Verified: quantity 10 @ 1.250 → stock value 12.500; quantity 0 @ 2.000 → unit cost saved, stock value 0 (both exactly per Task 3/12's Cases A/B).

**General Inventory receive cost behavior:** `receiveGeneralInventoryRequest` now computes `unit_cost`/`total_cost` on the `offline_inventory_movements` row it creates — no conversion: unit cost = actual received unit price, total cost = received qty × that price; conversion enabled: unit cost = actual unit price ÷ conversion quantity (25.000 KWD/BARREL ÷ 200 LITER = 0.125 KWD/LITER), total cost = movement quantity (already in the inventory unit) × that per-inventory-unit cost. Verified directly: 5 PCS @ 2.500 → stock value 12.500 (Case C); 1 BARREL @ 25.000 with 200 LITER conversion → 200 LITER received, unit cost 0.125, stock value 25.000 (Case D) — both exactly matching the task's worked examples. No Job Card file touched.

**Inventory list cost visibility:** Offline Inventory Control's table gained Unit Cost/Stock Value columns and a "Current Stock Value" summary card (one combined card, not three, to avoid crowding — Received Value/Issued Value remain available per-material in Material Details), all gated on `canViewCosts()` (`lib/security/permissions.ts` — `costs.view` permission or `profile.can_view_costs`, the same gate `new-part-wizard.tsx` already uses). **A real data-leak bug was found and fixed during verification**: gating only the UI's rendering (`{canViewCosts && <th>...}`) left the full cost numbers present in the page's underlying React Server Component payload sent to the browser regardless of role, since Next.js serializes every prop passed to a client component — a Data Entry session's raw page source still contained the true `last_unit_cost`/`stock_value` figures even though the visible table correctly hid the columns. Fixed by stripping (zeroing) those four fields server-side, before the array is ever passed to the client component, whenever the viewer lacks cost permission — verified by re-fetching the page and confirming the real cost values (e.g. `0.125`, `1.250`) no longer appear anywhere in a Data Entry viewer's raw HTML/payload, not just off-screen.

**Material detail / movement history cost behavior:** Material Details modal gained Last Unit Cost / Stock Value / Received Value / Issued Value (cost-permitted roles only) plus Unit Cost/Total Cost on each recent movement; `getMaterialRecentMovementsAction` (the server action backing this modal) nulls out both fields server-side for a non-cost viewer before returning, so this path was safe from the same leak class from the start. Movement History gained the same two columns, also nulled server-side for non-cost viewers.

**Permission behavior:** reused `canViewCosts()` from `lib/security/permissions.ts` everywhere (`costs.view` permission or `profile.can_view_costs`) — no new permission introduced, per the task's "use existing permission/canViewCosts if available."

**Negative balance behavior:** a material with a negative balance always shows Stock Value as 0 with a "Review required" note (both in the list table and the detail modal), and the balance number itself gets a small warning icon — the negative balance is never hidden, only its (meaningless) cost multiplication is suppressed, per Task 10's explicit instruction.

**Job Card workflow unchanged confirmation:** `lib/backend/parts-requests/*`, the Required Materials wizard step, Daily Activity material processing, and closure logic were not touched. Confirmed live: `/maintenance/daily-activity` still loads normally (200) with zero code changes in that area.

**Manual check results:** Cases A–D verified via seeded `offline_inventory_movements` rows fetched through the real, unmodified `getOfflineInventoryBalance()` aggregation logic on the live dev server — all four cases' unit cost/stock value figures matched the task's worked examples exactly (12.500, 0/2.000, 12.500, 0.125/25.000). Case E (Data Entry) and Case F (Manager) verified with real minted sessions for each role — Data Entry correctly saw no cost columns, no summary card, no Opening Unit Cost field, and (after the leak fix above) no real cost numbers anywhere in the page payload; Manager correctly saw all of it. Case G confirmed via a live Daily Activity page load (200) plus the fact that no Job Card material file was touched. All seeded movements and sessions deleted immediately after; no script left behind.

## Inventory Dashboard Spending and Simple Low Stock Rules (Unit 10G.63) — 2026-09-17

Fixes the default low-stock rule (balance 1 = Low Stock even with no minimum configured — Unit 10G.62 had left any positive balance as "OK" by default), folds Review Required into "Needs Attention," and adds a manager spending dashboard (issued/received value by week/month/year, cost by category, top issued materials) to Inventory Control. Purely additive to 10G.61/10G.62's foundation — **no schema change this unit**.

**Low stock rule behavior:** rewritten per the task's exact 2-branch rule — with a configured `minimum_stock_quantity`, Low Stock is `balance <= minimum` (unchanged from 10G.62); with NO minimum configured, Low Stock is now specifically `balance === 1` (previously any `balance > 0` with no minimum was silently "OK," which is exactly what the task calls "still confusing"). Status priority was also reordered: Negative Stock → Out of Stock → Low Stock → Review Required → OK (10G.62 had Review Required ahead of Out of Stock/Low Stock, which could replace a more basic, actionable reading with a vaguer one) — Review Required now only ever shows for an item that would otherwise look OK but has a genuine unit-mismatch data-quality concern, never masking a real negative/out/low reading. Verified: balance 1 (no minimum) → Low Stock; balance 0 → Out of Stock; balance -10 → Negative Stock; balance 2 → OK; balance 5 with minimum 10 → Low Stock — all five exactly as specified.

**Files changed:** `lib/store/offline-inventory-data.ts`, `components/store/offline-inventory-types.ts`, `app/actions/offline-inventory.ts`, `components/store/store-balance-view.tsx`, `components/store/material-detail-modal.tsx`, `app/(dashboard)/store/offline-inventory/page.tsx`. No new migration, no Job Card/Daily Activity/closure/worker-timer/auth file touched.

**Inventory summary/card behavior:** added Total Materials and Categories count cards (visible to every role, derived directly from the already-fetched balance list — no new query) alongside the renamed "Low Stock / Needs Attention" card, which now counts Review Required too (Unit 10G.62 explicitly excluded it; this unit reverses that per the task's own redefinition), with helper text "Includes low stock, out of stock, negative stock, and review-required items."

**Manager spending/expense behavior:** a new `getInventorySpendingSummary()` (one bounded query — every RECEIVED/ISSUED movement in the current calendar year, a reasonable "first version" bound) computes Issued Value This Week (rolling last 7 days)/This Month/This Year (both calendar-to-date) and Received Value This Month, using `total_cost` where available and falling back to `quantity × unit_cost` otherwise (excluded from totals, and counted in a new `unpricedIssuedCount`, only when both are missing) — shown as a 5-card row (Current Stock Value + the 4 above) for cost-permitted roles only, with helper text disclosing the estimate/fallback and, when relevant, how many unpriced movements were excluded. Verified: a Coolant material issued twice this month (10 + 20 LITER at 0.500 KWD/LITER) summed to exactly 15.000 KWD issued this month/year, with zero cross-contamination from other test categories.

**Category cost summary behavior:** a new "Material Cost by Category" table (cost-permitted only) — Category / Issued This Month / Issued This Year / Received This Month / Current Stock Value, the last folded in from the already-computed per-material `stock_value` (no second stock-value calculation) — verified: two categories with issued movements this month showed exactly the right per-category totals (15.000 KWD Lubricants/Oils, 5.000 KWD Electrical Materials), with untouched categories correctly showing 0.000.

**Top issued materials behavior:** a new "Top Issued Materials This Month" table, sorted by issued value, capped at top 10 — rendered for every role (Task 7's "quantity-only version" choice over hiding the section entirely for Data Entry): Material/Issued Quantity/Unit/Last Issued always show, "Issued Value" column only for cost-permitted roles. Verified: the same repeated Coolant issue correctly summed to 30 LITER / 15.000 KWD as a single top-issued row (not two separate rows for the two issue events).

**Balance status filter behavior:** the filter gained a 7th value, "Needs Attention" (Low Stock + Out of Stock + Negative Stock + Review Required combined) — confirmed present in the rendered `<select>`; its actual filtering behavior is pure client-side React state (like every filter dropdown on this page), so — consistent with every other UI-interactive check this session — it could not be exercised without a browser; verified instead by reading the filter predicate logic directly.

**Material detail behavior:** Current Stock now shows a "Default low stock rule: 1 or less needs attention." note whenever no minimum is configured for that material; Cost Summary gained this material's own Issued Value This Week/Month/Year and Received Value This Month, fetched via a new, cost-gated `getMaterialCostSummaryAction` (returns an already-zeroed summary for a non-cost viewer, and is never even called for one client-side).

**Data Entry visibility / no cost leakage:** `spendingSummary` is fully zeroed out server-side (`spendingSummaryForClient` in page.tsx, same principle as 10G.61's `balanceItemsForClient`) before ever reaching the client component when the viewer lacks cost permission — verified live: Data Entry's page had no spending cards, no category cost table, and the Top Issued Materials table rendered with the Issued Value column entirely absent (not just visually hidden).

**Existing workflow unchanged confirmation:** no changes to Job Card creation, Job Card Required Materials, Daily Activity worker/closure logic, or the General Inventory request create/receive flow's own behavior (only reads it for reporting, unchanged). Confirmed live: `/maintenance/daily-activity` still loads normally (200).

Case I verified via two separate Coolant issue events this month correctly summing into one top-issued row. Case G confirmed with a real Data Entry session — no cost cards, table, or column, and no cost figures anywhere in the raw page payload. Case J confirmed via a live Daily Activity page load.
