## Asset Site Movement / Deployment Tracking (Unit 10G.65) — 2026-09-19

New, fully separate `asset_movements` table and workflow tracking when an asset/equipment (crane, loader, generator, vehicle, etc.) is sent to a work site and later received back — sent date, site, expected/actual return, days outside, overdue, current location, sent-by/received-by. Deliberately kept isolated from Job Card, Daily Activity, and Inventory: no file belonging to those workflows was touched this unit (confirmed via `git status` — only `app/(dashboard)/assets/[id]/page.tsx`, `app/(dashboard)/assets/page.tsx`, `components/assets/asset-type-cards.tsx`, and `prisma/schema.prisma` were modified; everything else new is additive).

**Files changed:** `prisma/schema.prisma` (new `asset_movements` model + back-relation on `assets`), `prisma/migrations/20260919000000_asset_movements_unit10g65/migration.sql`, `lib/assets/movement-status.ts` (new — plain day-count/badge helpers, shared by server and client code), `lib/assets/movements-data.ts` (new, `server-only` — queries), `app/actions/asset-movements.ts` (new — `sendAssetToSiteAction`/`receiveAssetBackAction`), `components/assets/asset-movement-forms.tsx` (new — the two forms), `app/(dashboard)/assets/[id]/page.tsx` (new "Site Movement" tab, header actions, Overview summary), `app/(dashboard)/assets/page.tsx` (Location badge, movement filter), `components/assets/asset-type-cards.tsx` (movement badge in the Asset Type popup).

**Schema/migration changes:** one new table, `asset_movements` — one row per deployment trip (not separate send/return event rows), starting `ACTIVE` on Send to Site and updated in place to `RETURNED` on Receive Back. `sent_by_user_id`/`received_by_user_id` are plain scalar `uuid` columns with no Prisma relation, matching the existing `assets.created_by`/`updated_by` and `general_inventory_requests.requested_by_id` convention — no existing table's columns changed. A partial unique index (`WHERE status = 'ACTIVE'`) enforces "at most one active deployment per asset" at the database level, not just in the UI. Applied via `npx prisma db execute` + `npx prisma generate` (dev server stopped first to release the Windows query-engine DLL lock, then restarted) — same procedure as every prior unit.

**Send to Site behavior:** button appears in the asset header action bar only when the asset has no active movement (Task 2). Form: To Location/Site (required), Sent Date (required, defaults today), Expected Return Date (optional), Responsible Person/Driver (optional, one combined field — the task's own form-field list names it as a single field even though the "suggested model" section lists Responsible Person and Driver Name separately; the single field is what's actually asked for and avoids an always-empty second column), Purpose/Work Description (optional), Remarks (optional). On submit: creates the `ACTIVE` movement row (`from_location` captured from the asset's location at that moment), sets `assets.location` to the new site, and does **not** touch `assets.status` (see below). Sent By is always the acting user, set server-side — never a spoofable form field.

**Receive Back behavior:** button appears only when an active movement exists. Form: Return Date (required, defaults today), Return Location (required, defaults to the movement's own `from_location`, falling back to "Factory" per the task's own suggestion), Remarks (optional, appended to the movement's existing remarks rather than replacing them). On submit: the movement is updated in place to `RETURNED` with `actual_return_date` set, `assets.location` is set to the return location, and Received By is always the acting user (server-side, same non-spoofable pattern as Sent By).

**Days outside / overdue behavior:** `lib/assets/movement-status.ts`'s `computeMovementDayInfo()` — calendar-day (UTC date-only) differences, matching the task's exact wording in every surface: "Sent N days ago" / "Overdue by N days" / "Returned after N days" on the Movements tab's active/history card, plus a plain "Days outside: N" line on the Overview summary. Verified live: a movement seeded 3 days ago showed exactly "Sent 3 days ago"; moving its expected-return date to yesterday showed exactly "Overdue by 1 day"; receiving it back produced "Days Outside" = 3 in the history row (sent 3 days prior to the return date).

**Asset detail movement tab behavior:** new "Site Movement" tab (Task 5) between Materials History and Service Contracts — active-deployment card (location, sent date, expected return, days outside, responsible person, purpose, Receive Back button) when deployed, an empty "Not deployed" state with a Send to Site button otherwise, and a full movement history table (To Location/Sent Date/Expected Return/Returned Date/Days Outside/Status/Sent By/Received By — Sent By/Received By resolved from `profiles` via `getUserNamesByIds()` since those columns carry no Prisma relation). The task's suggested "Action/View" history column was intentionally omitted — every field the task lists is already inline in the row, and a movement has no separate detail page to link to. The Overview tab gained one small "Current Deployment" block inside the existing Location & Responsibility section (Task 6's own "do not make overview too crowded" — no new top-level card was added).

**Asset list/status behavior:** the Assets & Equipment table's Location column now shows the active movement's site (falling back to the asset's own `location` column, which the Send/Receive actions already keep in sync) plus a compact "At Site"/"Overdue" badge next to it (Task 7) — computed from one lightweight `getActiveMovementsByAsset()` query joined in memory, not a per-row query. The same badge and current-site line were added to the Asset Type Cards popup (Task 8). A new "Site Movement" filter (All/Available/At Site/Overdue Return, Task 9) was added next to the existing Status filter, backed by a real `asset_movements` relation filter (`some`/`none`/overdue-date comparison) — verified live: "At Site/Deployed" returned exactly the one seeded deployed asset, "Available" returned all 170 others, and "Overdue Return" returned 0 before the expected-return date passed and exactly 1 after. `asset.status` itself (Active/Breakdown/Under Maintenance/etc., used by Job Card and CEO risk logic) was never touched by any of this — deployment state is shown only as this separate badge, per the task's own "do not break existing status values" instruction and its explicit "if adding a separate badge is safer" fallback.

**Permission behavior:** reuses the existing `assets.manage` permission for Send to Site/Receive Back (already held by Super Admin and Maintenance Data Entry) — no new permission, role, or migration grant added. `assets.view` alone (view-only roles) sees the movement status but not the action buttons, matching the same `canEdit` gate this page already used for Edit Asset.

**Main page card-first behavior:** the page now renders, in order: KPI cards (Total Assets | At Site | Overdue Return | Active Maintenance — unchanged from 10G.66 except only "Total Assets" is still a link, now to "View All Assets" rather than to a filter that no longer exists), the Asset Types heading with a new "View All Assets" action beside "Manage Categories", the card grid itself, and a closing helper line. No global search bar and no Status/Site Movement filter row render on the page body itself anymore.

The one exception kept is the existing "No assets or equipment found" onboarding empty-state (Import Excel/New Asset/Manage Categories buttons) for the true zero-assets case — not a register table, and needed so those two entry points stay reachable even before the first asset exists (Task 8).

**View All Assets behavior:** a compact link beside "Manage Categories" opens the exact same popup component used for a single Asset Type, just unscoped (`assets` passed through unfiltered) — driven by a `?asset_type=__all__` query param the page validates against the real category list (falling back to `null`/closed for anything unrecognized). Verified live: response size jumped from ~187KB (closed) to ~395KB (all 171 assets rendered in the popup table), with the correct "All Assets" / "Showing all registered assets." title and subtitle.

**Asset Type popup behavior:** each card's popup keeps its title/subtitle pattern (e.g. "Crane Assets" / "Showing assets under this type."), now also carrying enough page-level context (`asset_type=<category or __all__>`) that a Send to Site / Receive Back action taken inside it redirects back to the *same* popup rather than a bare main page — implemented via React's "adjust state during render" pattern (comparing the `initialOpenType` prop against its last-seen value and calling `setOpenType` directly during render when it changes), not a `useEffect`+`setState`, matching this codebase's established rule against `react-hooks/set-state-in-effect`. One real bug found and fixed during verification: `ALL_ASSET_TYPES_KEY` was first defined and exported from `asset-type-cards.tsx` (a `"use client"` file) and imported into the server page — Next.js resolves every export of a client module to an opaque client-reference stub when used outside JSX/props on the server, so the "View All Assets" href silently became `/assets?asset_type=function(){throw new Error(...)}` instead of `__all__`. Fixed by moving the constant into `lib/assets/movement-status.ts` (a plain, non-`"use client"` module already shared by both files) — confirmed via live fetch that the href and the resulting popup render correctly afterward.

**Popup search/filter behavior:** the popup gained Status and Site Movement `<select>` filters (Task 6) beside the existing search box, combined via one `useMemo` over the in-memory asset list — Site Movement options are All/Available/At Site/Overdue Return, with the same "an overdue asset still counts as At Site too" rule the removed page-level filter used. A Reset button clears all three at once. Filters apply only to whatever the popup is currently showing (one type, or all assets via View All Assets) — there is no cross-popup filter state.

View-only roles see the same popup/table/badges but never the Send to Site/Receive Back buttons — verified by code inspection (identical, already-proven `canManage` check), since no active profile for a view-only role exists in this recovered database.

Replaces 10G.64's bottom collapsed "Manager Insights" accordion with a top-level tab switcher (Inventory Register / Manager Insights) plus a compact always-visible preview line, so a manager notices Manager Insights without scrolling past the whole table first. Pure client-component UI reorganization — no calculation, query, or server-side stripping logic touched.

**Files changed:** `components/store/store-balance-view.tsx` only — no page.tsx/action/data-layer file touched, confirmed via `git status`.

**Tab layout behavior:** local `activeTab` state (`"register" | "insights"`, default `"register"`) replaces the old `insightsOpen` boolean. The tab bar itself (and the second tab) only renders at all for `canViewCosts` — a non-cost viewer has exactly one thing to look at, so no tab UI exists and the Register content (gated only on `activeTab === "register"`, which never changes for that viewer) is the only view, matching Task 5 exactly.

**Manager Insights preview behavior:** a compact one-line card ("Manager Insights: Issued this month X KWD · Received this month Y KWD · View details"), cost-permitted only, sits between the movement-totals line and the tab bar. "View details" just calls `setActiveTab("insights")` — no navigation, no new data. Verified live that its numbers are the exact same `spendingSummary` values the Insights tab itself renders (both read the same prop).

## Worker Salary Cost Method and Rate Calculation (Unit 10G.68) — 2026-09-19

Adds a Salary Cost Input Method (Yearly Cost / Monthly Cost / Manual Hourly Rate) to the Worker Add/Edit modal's Salary Details section — HR/management now enters one basis number for the method they choose, and the system calculates the rest (Monthly Cost, Daily Rate, Hourly Rate), instead of every field being independently editable and risking conflicting numbers. `hourly_rate` remains the one number every other part of the app (Job Card labor cost, worker session snapshots, closure review, reports) reads — untouched calculation logic there, confirmed via `git status`.

**Salary cost input method decision:** three methods, matching the task exactly — `yearly_cost` (default for a new worker), `monthly_cost`, `manual_hourly_rate`. Only the one "main" field for the active method is editable (Yearly Cost / Monthly Cost / Hourly Rate); Monthly Working Days and Monthly Working Hours are always-editable shared supporting inputs (used by every method's math); everything else in that method's group renders read-only. The legacy allowance breakdown (Basic Salary/Transport/Accommodation/Food) was moved into a collapsed "Salary Breakdown (optional)" sub-section — still saved for backward compatibility, but no longer drives Hourly Rate under Yearly/Monthly Cost (Task 5).

**Files changed:** `prisma/schema.prisma` + new migration; `lib/backend/workers/salary.ts` (rebuilt around the method); `lib/backend/workers/validators.ts`, `lib/backend/workers/service.ts` (new fields threaded through create/update + stripping); `app/actions/workers.ts` (form parsing); `components/admin/worker-profile-form-modal.tsx` (the method switcher UI — the bulk of this unit); `components/admin/worker-profiles-view.tsx` (Salary Method shown under Salary Status in the list).

**Schema/migration changes:** additive only on `worker_profiles` — `salary_input_method` (text, default `'yearly_cost'`, CHECK-constrained to the 3 real values), `yearly_cost`/`monthly_cost` (nullable numeric — the entered basis for whichever method is active; both null under `manual_hourly_rate`, whose Estimated Monthly/Yearly/Daily figures are computed on read, never persisted as if they were an entered value), `monthly_working_days` (nullable numeric, default 26), `manual_hourly_rate_reason` (nullable text). No existing column removed, renamed, or made required. The migration also does a one-time Task-8-shaped backfill (below) — verified live against the two real pre-existing workers in this database: one with `total_salary=350` was correctly bucketed to `monthly_cost`/`monthly_cost=350`; the other, with only `hourly_rate=2` and no salary breakdown, was correctly bucketed to `manual_hourly_rate`.

**Yearly Cost method behavior:** Monthly Cost = Yearly Cost ÷ 12; Daily Rate = Monthly Cost ÷ Monthly Working Days (computed on read, never stored — no `daily_rate` column exists); Hourly Rate = Monthly Cost ÷ Monthly Working Hours. Verified by direct execution of the real `computeSalary` function (Node's native TypeScript support, not a reimplementation) against the task's own example — Yearly Cost 3900 / 26 days / 260 hours → Monthly Cost 325.000, Daily Rate 12.500, Hourly Rate 1.250, exact match.

**Monthly Cost method behavior:** Yearly Cost = Monthly Cost × 12; Daily Rate and Hourly Rate as above. Verified the same way — Monthly Cost 325 / 26 / 260 → Yearly Cost 3900.000, Daily Rate 12.500, Hourly Rate 1.250, exact match.

**Manual Hourly Rate method behavior:** Hourly Rate is used directly (no division); Estimated Monthly Cost = Hourly Rate × Monthly Working Hours, Estimated Yearly Cost = that × 12, Estimated Daily Rate = that ÷ Monthly Working Days — all display-only. A required-reading warning ("Manual hourly rate will be used directly for Job Card labor cost.") shows only for this method, plus an optional Reason field. Verified — Hourly Rate 2.000 / 260 hours / 26 days → Estimated Monthly 520.000, Estimated Yearly 6240.000, exact match.

**Final hourly rate / Job Card compatibility:** `hourly_rate` is written by every method's branch in `computeSalary`/`createWorkerProfile`/`updateWorkerProfile`, exactly as before this unit structurally — only the calculation feeding it changed. Confirmed via `git status` that `lib/backend/work-orders/worker-roster.ts` (which snapshots `hourly_rate` at Job Card assignment time) and `lib/work-orders/work-session-totals.ts` (labor cost = snapshot × hours) were not touched at all.

**Existing worker compatibility:** `resolveSalaryMethod()` implements the task's exact three-rule fallback (real `total_salary` → Monthly Cost basis; else real `hourly_rate` → Manual Hourly Rate; else Yearly Cost with everything blank) for the rare case a row still has no method recorded, and the migration itself already applies the same three rules once to every existing row so the form never needs to fall back in practice. No NaN/undefined possible — every numeric input defaults to 0 via the same `positiveOrZero` guard already used before this unit.

**Permission and no-leak behavior:** unchanged gates — `isManagerRole` (Super Admin/Maintenance Manager) controls both seeing and editing the whole Salary Details section (server-enforced in `service.ts`, not just hidden in the UI); Data Entry can still create a profile but never sets salary. `stripSalaryForNonManager` now also zeroes/nulls the 5 new fields for a non-Manager's payload. Verified live: a Data Entry session's raw page payload shows `salary_input_method:null, yearly_cost:null, monthly_cost:null, monthly_working_days:0, manual_hourly_rate_reason:null` for every worker, while a Super Admin session sees the real values (`salary_input_method:"monthly_cost", monthly_cost:350`, etc.) for the same rows.

**Worker list/table behavior:** Salary Status (Set/Manual Rate/Salary Pending) and a small muted Salary Method line underneath it were added to the existing Salary Status cell (not a new column, so the table doesn't get any wider) — both still `canManageWorkerProfiles`-gated exactly as the pre-existing Salary Status column was; Hourly Rate stays gated on `canViewCosts`, unchanged.

**Manual check results:** Cases A/B/C/D/G verified by directly importing and executing the real `lib/backend/workers/salary.ts` module (Node 24's native TypeScript execution, not a browser, but genuinely the shipped code, not a reimplementation) against the task's exact numeric examples — all passed exactly, including Case D's zero/invalid inputs producing `hourlyRate: 0` and "Salary Pending" with no NaN/undefined anywhere, and Case G reproducing the real pre-existing worker's stored `hourly_rate` (1.346) byte-for-byte from its migrated `monthly_cost` basis. Case E (Data Entry, no leak) verified live via HTTP as described above. Case F (Job Card labor cost) verified by `git status` showing no work-session/timer file touched — the calculation path itself is provably unchanged, only where `hourly_rate` comes from. The full Add/Edit modal UI itself (the method switcher, live preview, badges) could not be exercised by clicking in a real browser — none is available in this environment — so its correctness rests on this passing typecheck/lint/build plus the underlying `computeSalary` calls it makes being independently verified above. All minted sessions and the one throwaway test worker profile (created and deleted via the real `createWorkerProfile`/`updateWorkerProfile` functions during an earlier exploratory check) were cleaned up; no temporary script left behind.

**Validation:** `npm run db:check` ✓, `npm run lint` ✓ (0 errors), `npm run typecheck` ✓, `npm run build` ✓ (62 routes, unchanged — no new routes). Per the task's explicit instruction, `npm run test:e2e` was **not** run. No change to Job Card workflow, worker timer/session logic, closure logic, Inventory logic, Asset logic, or auth/login. No deployment performed. **Migration bookkeeping resolved this unit:** unlike every prior unit this session, `npx prisma migrate resolve --applied <migration>` was **not** blocked this time — it succeeded for this unit's own migration, and was then also run successfully for all previously-outstanding migrations (10G.58, 10G.61, 10G.62, 10G.65) plus one earlier pre-session gap (10G.41B's salary-breakdown migration). `npx prisma migrate status` now reports "Database schema is up to date!" with all 38 migrations tracked — the long-carried outstanding item from every prior unit's report is now fully resolved.

## Closure Review Work and Material Cost (Unit 10G.72) — 2026-09-20

Gives the Manager Closure Review modal a complete Job Card cost picture before approval: Direct Labor Cost, a new one-time-per-Job-Card Indirect Cost (configured once in Worker Profile, read automatically — never entered per closure), Total Worker Cost, per-material Unit/Total Cost (using Offline Inventory's existing "last unit cost" method), and a Grand Total Job Cost — with strict cost-permission gating throughout.

**Files changed:** New migration `prisma/migrations/20260920020000_worker_indirect_cost_unit10g72/` (additive `worker_profiles.indirect_cost_per_job_card`/`indirect_cost_note`). Modified — `prisma/schema.prisma` (the two new columns), `lib/backend/workers/validators.ts`/`app/actions/workers.ts`/`lib/backend/workers/service.ts` (parse/gate/persist the two new fields, same Manager-only boundary as every other salary field), `components/admin/worker-profile-form-modal.tsx` (new "Indirect Cost per Job Card" subsection inside the existing Salary Details card), `lib/store/offline-inventory-data.ts` (new `getLastUnitCostsForIdentities` — additive read-only helper, no existing function touched), `app/actions/closure-requests.ts` (new cost fields on `ClosureReviewWorker`/`ClosureReviewMaterial`/`ClosureReviewDetail`, computed from existing data only), `components/dashboard/closure-review-modal.tsx` (worker cost columns, a new Job Card Cost Summary block, and a cost-permitted Materials cost table). No Job Card creation workflow, worker timer/session logic, closure approval action, or Inventory movement/stock calculation logic was touched.

**Schema/migration changes:** `worker_profiles.indirect_cost_per_job_card numeric(12,3) NOT NULL DEFAULT 0` and `indirect_cost_note text` (nullable) — additive only, applied via `db execute` + `prisma migrate resolve --applied`, `prisma generate` re-run after a dev-server stop/restart (Windows query-engine DLL lock). NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 (rather than nullable) was a deliberate choice so no calling code anywhere needs to null-coalesce this value, satisfying Task 10's "no NaN/undefined values" directly at the schema level.

**Worker indirect cost behavior:** a flat, one-time-per-Job-Card amount, deliberately kept OUT of `computeSalary()`/`ComputedSalary` (Unit 10G.68's hourly-rate salary method) — it is read automatically by Closure Review from `worker_profiles.indirect_cost_per_job_card`, never entered or overridable per Job Card (Task 1's own explicit rule, and there is no such option anywhere in this unit's UI). Manager/Super-Admin-only to set on both create and update, enforced in `lib/backend/workers/service.ts`'s existing `canSetSalary`/`assertCanEditWorkerProfile` gates (verified live: a Data Entry `createWorkerProfile` call that tried to set `9.999`/a note was saved as `0`/`null`; the same call as Manager saved the real values).

**Worker profile UI behavior:** "Indirect Cost per Job Card (KWD)" + optional "Indirect Cost Note", inside Salary Details (Manager/Super-Admin-only, same gate as Hourly Rate/Yearly Cost/etc.), with the exact required helper text ("Indirect Cost is optional additional worker cost added once per worker in Job Card Closure Review. It is not calculated per hour."). Data Entry's Add Worker form never renders or submits these fields (Salary Details is entirely absent for them, unchanged from every other salary field's own visibility rule).

**Closure Review worker cost behavior:** each worker's own card and the multi-worker comparison table now show Direct Labor Cost (actual hours × hourly rate, the same figure the old "Total Pay"/"Pay" fields already computed — renamed for Task 12's required wording), Indirect Cost (the worker's own saved value, defaulting to `0.000 KWD` rather than a dash or blank when unconfigured — never null/undefined while cost-permitted), and Total Worker Cost (their sum). All three are completely absent (not `0.000 KWD`) for a non-cost-permitted viewer.

**Material cost behavior:** each required material's Unit Cost/Total Cost uses a new `getLastUnitCostsForIdentities()` helper — the exact same Unit 10G.61 "last unit cost" method (Offline Inventory's own most-recent-priced-movement-per-identity read), scoped to only this Job Card's required materials rather than a full store-wide balance sweep. A material with no priced movement at all shows "Unpriced" (both `unitCost`/`totalCost` stay `null` — never `0`), matching Task 5's own "do not invent costs" rule exactly.

**Cost summary behavior:** replaces the old single "Labor Cost" standalone card with a Job Card Cost Summary block — Direct Labor Cost, Indirect Cost, Total Labor Cost, Material Cost, Grand Total Job Cost — satisfying Tasks 4 and 6 together as one combined summary rather than two separate blocks (Task 6's list is a strict superset of Task 4's). Indirect Cost is summed once per DISTINCT worker on the Job Card (not once per assignment row), matching the business rule's own "added once for that worker" wording even in the edge case of a worker holding two assignments on the same Job Card. Material Cost sums only priced lines; Grand Total = Total Labor Cost + Material Cost; the required "Grand total excludes unpriced material lines." note appears whenever any material lacks a recorded cost.

**Permission and no-leak behavior:** every new cost field (`directLaborCost`/`indirectCost`/`totalWorkerCost` per worker; `unitCost`/`totalCost`/`isUnpriced` per material; `directLaborCostTotal`/`indirectCostTotal`/`totalLaborCost`/`materialCostTotal`/`grandTotalJobCost`/`hasUnpricedMaterial` at the Job Card level) is zeroed/nulled at the data layer inside `getClosureReviewDetailAction` itself for a non-cost-permitted viewer — not just hidden by the modal's JSX — and the indirect-cost/unit-cost lookup queries are skipped entirely (never even run) when `!canViewCosts`. Verified live by temporarily flipping a real Manager profile's `can_view_costs` to `false` (Closure Review itself is already Manager/Super-Admin-only end to end, so this is the closest reachable equivalent to a "Data Entry view" of this specific screen): every cost field in the raw JSON response came back `null`/`false`, with hours/status/material-quantity fields still present — flag restored to `true` immediately after.

**Existing worker/job compatibility:** confirmed live against one of this database's real pre-existing "Closure Requested" Job Cards — both its real workers' new `indirectCost` read back as `0` (the migration's own default), so `totalWorkerCost` exactly equalled the pre-existing `directLaborCost`/`totalPay` figure, and the Job-Card-level `totalLaborCost` exactly equalled what `totalAmount` (the old "Labor Cost" card's own figure) already was — proving no existing Closure Review's totals changed and no backfill of old Job Cards was required.

**Manual check results:** all seeded via one temporary Job Card carrying two real workers (Worker A: hourly 1.250, indirect 5.000, 2h logged; Worker B: hourly 1.000, indirect 3.000, 1h logged) and three real required materials (two priced via real `offline_inventory_movements` unit_cost rows, one deliberately left unpriced), fetched through the actual `getClosureReviewDetailAction` server action (via a temporary, deleted-after-use verification route — no browser available in this environment to drive the Closure Review modal's own click path). Case A ✓ (Direct 2.500 / Indirect 5.000 / Total 7.500, exact). Case B ✓ (Direct total 3.500 / Indirect total 8.000 / Total Labor 11.500, exact). Case C ✓ (a separate single-worker Job Card, Indirect 0 / Total Worker Cost 2.500, exact). Case D ✓ (Material Cost 5.500 from the two priced lines). Case E ✓ (the third material showed `isUnpriced: true`, `unitCost`/`totalCost` both `null`, excluded from the 5.500). Case F ✓ (Total Labor 11.500 + Material 5.500 = Grand Total 17.000, exact). Case G ✓ (no-cost-view: every cost field `null`/`false` in the raw payload). Case H ✓ (a real pre-existing Job Card's totals unchanged). All seeded workers/Job Cards/movements/sessions and the temporary verification route/sessions were deleted immediately after.

**Validation:** `npm run db:check` ✓, `npm run lint` ✓ (0 errors), `npm run typecheck` ✓, `npm run build` ✓ (re-run after removing the temporary verification route, confirming no trace of it remained). ## Inventory Add New Material Cost and Unit Conversion UI (Unit 10G.73) — 2026-09-20

Reorganizes the Add New Material modal into 4 clear sections and adds a proper Purchase Unit → Inventory Unit conversion mechanism (e.g. 1 BARREL = 200 LITER), so a bulk-purchased material's stock balance and unit cost land correctly in whatever unit it is actually issued in.

**Files changed:** `components/store/add-new-material-form.tsx` (full rewrite into 4 sections) and `app/actions/offline-inventory.ts`'s `addNewMaterialAction` (new Purchase Unit/Purchase Quantity/Purchase Unit Cost/conversion fields, replacing the old single Unit/Initial Quantity/Opening Unit Cost fields — same movement-creation call, same duplicate-check helpers, just now keyed on the resolved Inventory Unit instead of one plain Unit). No schema change — `offline_inventory_movements` already had every column needed (`quantity`/`unit`/`unit_cost`/`total_cost`/`remarks`) to hold the final, already-converted values. No other file touched — `lib/store/offline-inventory-data.ts`'s balance/read logic, the General Inventory Request feature, and every other Offline Inventory form (Opening Stock, Receive Material, Opening Stock Import) are all unmodified, including the pre-existing `UNITS` constant they still use.

**Add New Material modal layout behavior:** four sections — 1. Basic Material Details (Material Name/Category/Part Number/SS Rec. Code, unchanged), 2. Stock Setup (Inventory Unit + a live, read-only "Opening Inventory Quantity" display + Minimum Stock/Reorder Quantity, unchanged), 3. Cost / Purchase Unit (Purchase Unit/Purchase Quantity/Purchase Unit Cost/"Use different inventory unit" toggle/Conversion/Inventory Unit Cost/Opening Stock Value), 4. Location / Notes (unchanged). Inventory Unit in Section 2 mirrors Purchase Unit automatically (shown as a disabled-look "(same as Purchase Unit)" box) until the toggle in Section 3 is switched on, at which point it becomes its own live dropdown — avoiding double-entry of the same unit in the common case while still giving Section 2 its own required field per the task's layout.

**Unit dropdown behavior:** both Purchase Unit and Inventory Unit reuse `GENERAL_INVENTORY_UNIT_OPTIONS`/`CUSTOM_UNIT_VALUE`/`DEFAULT_UNIT` from `components/store/general-inventory-units.ts` — the exact same list and OTHER/CUSTOM sentinel the General Inventory Request form already established (imported, not duplicated or modified) — rather than the older, narrower `UNITS` list in `offline-inventory-types.ts` (left untouched for its other existing callers). Both default to PCS.

**Normal item cost behavior:** when "Use different inventory unit" stays off, the conversion factor is implicitly 1, so Opening Inventory Quantity = Purchase Quantity, Inventory Unit Cost = Purchase Unit Cost, and Opening Stock Value = Purchase Quantity × Purchase Unit Cost — the exact same numbers the original single-unit form always produced, computed through the same one formula the bulk case uses (no separate code path). Verified live: 10 PCS at 1.250 KWD saved as quantity 10 / unit_cost 1.25 / total_cost 12.5, exactly.

**Bulk conversion behavior:** when the toggle is on, Opening Inventory Quantity = Purchase Quantity × Conversion Quantity, Inventory Unit Cost = Purchase Unit Cost ÷ Conversion Quantity, Opening Stock Value = Purchase Quantity × Purchase Unit Cost — computed server-side in `addNewMaterialAction`, never trusted from the client's own live preview. A clear audit note ("Opening stock — 1 BARREL converted to 200 LITER") is written into the movement's `remarks` whenever a real conversion actually applies. Verified live: 1 BARREL at 25.000 KWD converted at 1:200 saved as quantity 200 / unit LITER / unit_cost 0.125 / total_cost 25, with the exact required remarks text (confirmed byte-correct in the database, past a display-only PowerShell console encoding artifact); 5 BARREL at the same rate saved as quantity 1000 / unit_cost 0.125 / total_cost 125 — both exact.

**New material estimated cost behavior:** a material with no Offline Inventory match (or a matched one with no recorded cost) gets an editable "Estimated Unit Cost" input instead of a read-only figure — purely a planning number the user types in, with the required helper wording ("Estimated cost is for Job Card planning only. Estimated total excludes unpriced lines." note. ## Manager Job Card Creation and Page Crash Fix (Unit 10G.74) — 2026-09-20

Root-cause fix for the "This module could not load" crash reported for Manager Job Card creation, plus a full live-verified audit of the Manager create-to-closure lifecycle and every other candidate cause the task listed. The actual root cause, found in this session's own dev-server log from an earlier real interaction, was a Next.js Server Actions transport-layer limit — not a role/permission/data bug.

**Files changed:** `next.config.ts` (new `experimental.serverActions.bodySizeLimit: "60mb"`), `app/actions/system-health.ts` (`logClientModuleErrorAction` now also derives and logs a `module` label from the route). No other file touched — this unit needed no application-logic change at all; every other audited area (permissions, zero-data handling, 10G.73's cost columns, worker-profile nullable-safety) was already correct.

**Root cause of module crash:** this session's own `/tmp/dev-server.log` (accumulated across the whole session, from real prior browser interaction, not something this unit fabricated) contained a genuine, already-captured crash: `⨯ Error: Body exceeded 1 MB limit. To configure the body size limit for Server Actions, see: .../serverActions#bodysizelimit`, immediately followed by the client-side `[browser] Dashboard error` log showing `app/(dashboard)/error.tsx`'s exact title, **"This module could not load"** — the identical wording the task reports. Next.js Server Actions reject any request body over 1 MB by default; this project's own attachment upload path (`components/files/attachment-upload-fields.tsx`, shared by the New Job Card and Materials Request wizards, `MAX_ATTACHMENT_ROWS = 5`) and its own validation (`lib/files/validation.ts`'s `MAX_PRIVATE_FILE_SIZE` / the admin-configurable `app_settings.max_upload_size_mb`, both defaulting to 10 MB) already told users a single file up to 10 MB was fine — but `next.config.ts` had no `serverActions.bodySizeLimit` override at all before this unit, so any Job Card submitted with a real attachment over roughly 1 MB (a single modern phone photo, easily) would 413 and land on this exact error screen. This is not Manager-specific — it would affect any role attaching a large file — but matches the reported scenario exactly, since attaching a photo of the issue is a completely natural first thing to do when actually running the full create-to-close flow, which is what this task asked the Manager to newly attempt.

**Permission and non-attachment causes ruled out (Task 1's own checklist), each confirmed live:** Manager Job Cards list load (200, no crash) · Manager "Create Job Card" modal open (200) · Manager searching Required Materials (`searchOfflineInventoryMaterialsAction`, succeeds) · Manager saving a full Job Card (asset + worker assignment + required material, no attachment) via the real `upsertWorkOrderAction` — succeeded outright, creating a real Job Card (`REC/MD/MECH/JOB/0004`) with correct `created_by`/`ordered_by`/status · Unit 10G.72/72A's Closure Review cost fields (`hourlyRate`/`directLaborCost`/`indirectCost`) computed correctly with no undefined/NaN for that same Job Card · Unit 10G.73's Required Materials cost columns render correctly for cost-permitted users and are absent for Data Entry, with no `last_unit_cost` leak in the autocomplete payload · zero-data empty state (`?status=<non-matching>`) shows "No Job Cards found." cleanly, no crash. None of these showed any defect — the 1 MB body limit was the only real bug found.

**Manager Job Cards page behavior:** confirmed live — `/maintenance/work-orders` and `/maintenance/work-orders?new_job_card=1` both return 200 for a Manager session with no error boundary triggered; a filtered view with zero matching Job Cards shows "No Job Cards found." (pre-existing empty-state copy, already exactly matching the task's own requested wording — no change needed).

**Manager create Job Card behavior:** Manager successfully created a real Job Card end-to-end via the real `upsertWorkOrderAction` — one asset, one internal-team worker assignment (hourly rate correctly frozen from the worker's profile), one required material, no attachments. `created_by` was the Manager's own real profile id; `ordered_by` saved exactly what was typed (a plain editable text field, unchanged behavior); status followed the normal flow (`Approved`, the same status any role's "Start Job Card" submission produces).

**Manager full workflow compatibility:** the created Job Card appeared correctly in Daily Activity (live-confirmed, page loads with the Job Card's number and complaint text visible). Its full closure lifecycle was driven end-to-end through the real actions — `requestJobCardClosureModalAction` → `getClosureReviewDetailAction` → `approveJobCardClosureModalAction` — all three succeeded, with the Job Card's `status` confirmed `Closed` in the database afterward. No special-casing exists anywhere in this closure code for "who created the Job Card," so a Manager approving their own Manager-created Job Card's closure worked with zero new restriction and zero crash, satisfying Task 6 exactly as specified ("do not add a new approval restriction in this unit").

**Zero-data compatibility:** the real counts today are non-zero (work_orders: 3, parts_requests: 3, general_inventory_requests: 1 — the described cleanup has not actually been performed), so this was verified without deleting real data: a status filter matching zero rows reproduces the "Job Cards = 0 for this view" case cleanly (`EmptyState` renders "No Job Cards found.", no crash), and the Dashboard loads fine for the same session. No file needed to change for this — the existing empty-state handling already covers it.

**Required Materials estimated cost compatibility:** re-verified Unit 10G.73's own search action and column logic still behave correctly after this unit's changes (nothing in this unit touched that code) — cost-permitted sessions see `last_unit_cost` when present and correctly null when absent, Data Entry sessions always get `last_unit_cost: null` regardless, and the wizard's own `rowUnitCost`/`rowEstimatedTotal` helpers were re-confirmed null-safe by inspection (every `.toFixed()` call is guarded by a `!== null`/`.length > 0` check first) — no missing-`last_unit_cost`/missing-`unit` crash risk found.

**Permission behavior:** audited `upsertWorkOrderAction`'s own gate (`requirePermission("work_orders.manage")`) and `getCostViewPermissionAction`'s (same permission) — both already correctly allow Super Admin/Maintenance Manager/Maintenance Data Entry and correctly exclude Viewer/Auditor and non-maintenance roles; nothing here needed changing, matching the task's own "if permissions are already correct, do not change them."

**Manual check results:** Case A ✓ (Manager Job Cards page loads live, no crash). Case B ✓ (a zero-matching filter shows "No Job Cards found." live). Case C ✓ (Manager created a real Job Card — asset + worker + material — via the real save action; saved successfully). Case D ✓ (the Job Card appeared in Daily Activity live). Case E ✓ (full closure lifecycle — request → review → approve — succeeded live, ending in `status: "Closed"`). Case F ✓ (Data Entry's Job Cards list/New Job Card page both load live with zero cost text in the payload). Case G ✓ (Assets/Worker Profiles/Offline Inventory/Reports all return 200 live for both roles). All seeded test data (one Job Card and its assignment/session/materials-request), the temporary verification routes, and every minted test session were deleted immediately after.

**Validation:** `npm run db:check` ✓, `npm run lint` ✓ (0 errors), `npm run typecheck` ✓, `npm run build` ✓ (re-run after removing both temporary verification routes, confirming no trace remained). Per the task's explicit instruction, `npm run test:e2e` was **not** run. No change to worker timer logic, material issue/receive logic, closure approval logic (beyond nothing — no new restriction added), inventory cost logic, worker salary/indirect cost logic, or auth/login. No deployment performed.

**Known limitation, disclosed plainly:** the `bodySizeLimit` fix is Next.js's own officially documented remedy for the exact error captured in this session's logs, and the running dev server's own startup banner confirms the option is recognized (`- Experiments (use with caution): · serverActions`). However, synthetic raw-HTTP reproduction of the exact byte-counting enforcement in this no-browser, Turbopack-dev environment was inconclusive — hand-crafted large-body Server Action requests (both under and over the configured limit) did not reproduce the "Body exceeded" rejection either way, most likely because a hand-built request cannot fully replicate the real browser/React client's multipart wire protocol for a genuine file upload. This is a testing-environment limitation, not a sign the fix is wrong: the fix is the correct, documented one for the precisely observed error, and does not change any business logic.

## Job Card Level Indirect Cost Correction (Unit 10G.72B) — 2026-09-21

Corrects Unit 10G.72's mistaken design: Indirect Cost was implemented as a per-worker Worker Profile field, but the confirmed business rule is that it is a single, Job-Card-wide amount configured once by Super Admin/IT Admin/Maintenance Manager — never per worker, never per hour, never entered in Closure Review. Worker Profile's own indirect cost fields are removed from the UI/save path (columns left in the schema, unused); a new global setting replaces them as the one source of Indirect Cost for every Job Card's Closure Review.

**Previous mistake corrected:** Unit 10G.72 read `worker_profiles.indirect_cost_per_job_card` per assigned worker and summed it into the Job Card total (`indirectCostTotal`), and showed it as a per-worker column/figure in both the Worker Profile form and the Closure Review worker table. Both are now removed — Indirect Cost is read exactly once per Job Card, from one global setting, completely independent of which or how many workers are assigned.

**Files changed:** New — `prisma/migrations/20260921000000_job_card_indirect_cost_unit10g72b/` (additive `app_settings.job_card_indirect_cost`/`job_card_indirect_cost_note`), `lib/work-orders/job-card-indirect-cost.ts` (`getJobCardIndirectCostSetting`), `app/(dashboard)/admin/settings/job-card-cost/page.tsx` (its own small settings sub-page). Modified — `prisma/schema.prisma` (the two new `app_settings` columns), `lib/security/permissions.ts` (new `canManageJobCardIndirectCostSetting`), `app/actions/admin.ts` (new `updateJobCardIndirectCostSettingAction`), `app/actions/closure-requests.ts` (stops reading worker-level indirect cost; reads the global setting instead; `ClosureReviewWorker`/`ClosureReviewDetail` types corrected), `components/dashboard/closure-review-modal.tsx` (worker table/footer and Final Job Card Cost box corrected), `components/admin/worker-profile-form-modal.tsx` / `lib/backend/workers/service.ts` / `lib/backend/workers/validators.ts` / `app/actions/workers.ts` (Indirect Cost per Job Card / Indirect Cost Note fields fully removed from the Worker Profile create/edit UI and save path — the two `worker_profiles` columns are left in the schema, untouched, per Task 1's own "do not remove" instruction, simply no longer read or written by any code).

**Schema/migration changes:** additive-only — `app_settings.job_card_indirect_cost numeric(12,3) NOT NULL DEFAULT 0` and `job_card_indirect_cost_note text` (nullable), on the existing app-wide singleton row (the same row `lib/files/settings.ts` already reads for file-upload settings). `worker_profiles.indirect_cost_per_job_card`/`indirect_cost_note` from Unit 10G.72 are untouched — no column dropped, no data migrated, per Task 1/6's own explicit "do not remove" instruction.

**Global indirect cost setting behavior:** a new, dedicated settings sub-page at `/admin/settings/job-card-cost` — deliberately separate from the main `/admin/settings` page (which stays `admin.settings.manage`-only, Super Admin/IT Admin, unchanged) because Maintenance Manager does not have that permission and the task explicitly wants Manager to be able to configure this one setting without broadening the main Settings page's own access. Gated by a new `canManageJobCardIndirectCostSetting(context)` — Super Admin always allowed; IT Admin ("System Admin") and Maintenance Manager additionally need `canViewCosts`. Shows "Indirect Cost per Job Card (KWD)" (default 0.000) and an optional "Indirect Cost Note", with the exact required helper text. Verified live: Super Admin set it to 5.000 KWD, read it back correctly (5, with the note), then reset it to 0 — all through the real action.

**Worker Profile UI correction:** the "Indirect Cost per Job Card" subsection (added by Unit 10G.72 inside Salary Details) is removed entirely from `WorkerProfileFormModal` — no input, no label, no state. `createWorkerProfile`/`updateWorkerProfile` no longer read, validate, or write either field at all (removed from the Zod schema, the form-parsing action, and both Prisma `data: {}` objects) — the two columns simply keep whatever value they already have (0 for a new worker, via the column's own default), completely decoupled from any form submission. Verified live: the real Worker Profiles page for a Manager session contains no "Indirect Cost per Job Card" text and no `indirect_cost_per_job_card`/`indirect_cost_note` field names anywhere in the payload.

**Closure Review worker table correction:** `ClosureReviewWorker` no longer has `indirectCost`/`totalWorkerCost` fields at all. The per-worker card and the multi-worker comparison table (plus its own totals footer) now show only Worker/Estimated Hours/Actual Hours/Direct Labor Cost/Status, with the footer showing Total Actual Hours and "Total Direct Labor Cost" (no Indirect Cost, no Total Worker Cost anywhere near a worker). Verified live: a real Closure Review payload's `workers` array now contains only `hourlyRate`/`totalPay`/`directLaborCost` as cost fields — no `indirectCost` or `totalWorkerCost` property exists on any worker object at all.

**Final Job Card Cost behavior:** the Final Job Card Cost box now shows exactly four tiles — Direct Labor Cost, Material Cost, Indirect Cost (the one global setting, read once), Grand Total Job Cost — with Grand Total = Direct Labor Cost + Material Cost + Indirect Cost (the old "Total Labor Cost = Direct + Indirect" concept from Unit 10G.72 no longer exists anywhere). Verified live against a real Job Card with Direct Labor Cost 0.055 and Material Cost 0 (all its required materials unpriced): with the global setting at 5.000 KWD, Grand Total came back exactly 5.055; with the setting reset to 0, Grand Total came back exactly 0.055 — both matching the task's own worked examples exactly, confirming existing Job Cards' totals are unaffected when the global setting is 0.

## Job Card Indirect Cost Sidebar Visibility (Unit 10G.72D) — 2026-09-21

Unit 10G.72C made the Job Card-level indirect cost setting discoverable via a Super Admin Settings card and a Manager Dashboard quick action, but Maintenance Manager still had no *stable* sidebar entry point, and the wording "Job Card Cost Settings" read as broader than the setting actually is (one global, once-per-Job-Card amount, not a general settings area). This unit added a dedicated Manager sidebar item and standardized the wording to "Job Card Indirect Cost" everywhere the setting is surfaced, without touching cost calculation, the Closure Review formula, permissions logic, the database schema, or the route itself.

**Task 1/2 — Manager sidebar item:** `components/layout/app-layout.tsx`'s `NavItem` type gained an optional `customGate?: "jobCardIndirectCost"` field, since this one item's visibility can't be expressed as a single `PermissionKey` string — its real gate is `canManageJobCardIndirectCostSetting` (Super Admin always; IT Admin/Maintenance Manager only with `canViewCosts`). `canSee()` was extended with one branch: when `customGate === "jobCardIndirectCost"`, it calls that function instead of the plain permission-slug check. A new item (`label: "Job Card Indirect Cost"`, `iconKey: "Wallet"`, `href: "/admin/settings/job-card-cost"`) was added to `maintenanceManagerNavigationGroups`'s Operations group, positioned exactly per the task's recommended order — directly after "Reports" and before "Notifications". `Wallet` was added to `components/layout/nav-link.tsx`'s lucide-react import and `navIcons` map (previously not present; `Settings` was already used by the full Admin Settings item, so a distinct icon avoids visual confusion since Data Entry's shared array is untouched and Manager's own array now carries both a Reports icon and this new Wallet icon side by side). No other role's navigation array was touched — Super Admin's own sidebar (which still reaches the setting via its 10G.72C card, per Task 6/Case E) was deliberately left unchanged rather than adding a duplicate sidebar item there.

**Task 3 — Dashboard quick action kept, renamed:** in `app/(dashboard)/dashboard/page.tsx`, the Manager Dashboard tile's title was changed from "Job Card Cost Settings" to "Job Card Indirect Cost" (subtitle "Set indirect cost per Job Card" already matched and was left as-is); same `mgCanManageJobCardCost` gate, same href, kept as a second, easy-discovery path alongside the new stable sidebar item.

**Task 4 — Super Admin Settings card renamed:** in `app/(dashboard)/admin/settings/page.tsx`, the card title changed to "Job Card Indirect Cost", the description to "Set the indirect cost added once to each Job Card during Closure Review.", and the button text to "Open Indirect Cost Setting"; the current-value line and the card's underlying data/gate are unchanged.

**Task 5 — Dedicated page wording finalized:** in `app/(dashboard)/admin/settings/job-card-cost/page.tsx`, the page title (both the permission-denied branch and the main render) changed to "Job Card Indirect Cost Setting", and the success banner text to "Job Card Indirect Cost setting saved." The field label ("Indirect Cost per Job Card (KWD)"), helper text, and formula box were already exactly correct from 10G.72C and needed no change.

**Task 6/7 — No broadened access, correct active state:** Manager's `/admin/settings` gate (`requirePermission("admin.settings.manage")`) is completely untouched — still redirects Manager to `/dashboard?error=permission-denied`. Because the new sidebar item lives only in `maintenanceManagerNavigationGroups` and Manager's array has no "Settings" entry at all, there is no full-Settings item that could be wrongly highlighted; `NavLink`'s existing `pathname === href` active-state logic (unchanged) correctly highlights "Job Card Indirect Cost" when Manager is on `/admin/settings/job-card-cost`, verified live via the rendered `aria-current="page"` attribute and active border/background classes on that exact link.

**Manual check results:** Case A ✓ (Manager's live dashboard/sidebar RSC payload shows the "Job Card Indirect Cost" sidebar item with `iconKey: "Wallet"` linking to `/admin/settings/job-card-cost`, positioned right after Reports). Case B ✓ (Manager can open the page directly: correct new title, field label, helper text, formula box, and a "Back to Dashboard" link — not "Back to Settings"). Case C ✓ (Manager requesting `/admin/settings` still gets the same `NEXT_REDIRECT` digest to `/dashboard?error=permission-denied`, confirmed in the raw RSC payload, with no main settings form rendered — the page Manager actually lands on is their own Dashboard, which is why it legitimately contains "Job Card Indirect Cost" text itself, from the sidebar/quick-action, not from a leaked settings card). Case D ✓ (Data Entry's dashboard has neither the sidebar item nor the href anywhere in the payload; direct access to the setting page returns only the permission-denied message, no field labels, no Save button). Case E ✓ (Super Admin's own sidebar is completely unaffected — "Settings"/"Users"/etc. all still render and highlight correctly via `aria-current="page"`; Super Admin's array does not carry the new Manager-only "Wallet"-icon item; the Settings-page card still opens the sub-page with the new wording). Case F ✓ (with the setting live-set to 5.000, `getClosureReviewDetailAction` on a real Closure-Requested Job Card returned `directLaborCostTotal: 0.055`, `materialCostTotal: 0`, `jobCardIndirectCost: 5`, `grandTotalJobCost: 5.055` — exact, unchanged formula).
